      • Lesson 11
        • 11.1 Reading
          • cakkhupāla atīta vatthu Atīte bārāṇasiyaṃ kāsiraññe rajjaṃ kārente eko vejjo gāmanigamesu caritvā vejjakammaṃ karonto ekaṃ cakkhudubbalaṃ itthiṃ disvā pucchi “Kiṃ te aphāsuka”nti. “Akkhīhi na passāmī”ti. “Bhesajjaṃ te karissāmī”ti. “Karohi sāmī”ti. “Kiṃ me dassasī”ti. “Sace me akkhīni pākatikāni kātuṃ sakkhissasi, ahaṃ te saddhiṃ puttadhītāhi dāsī bhavissāmī”ti. So “Sādhū”ti bhesajjaṃ saṃvidahi. Ekabhesajjeneva akkhīni pākatikāni ahesuṃ. Sā cintesi “Ahametassa saputtadhītā dāsī bhavissāmīti paṭijāniṃ, na kho pana maṃ saṇhena samudācārena samudācarissati, vañcessāmi na”nti. Sā vejjenāgantvā “Kīdisaṃ bhadde”ti puṭṭhā “Pubbe me akkhīni thokaṃ rujjiṃsu, idāni pana atirekataraṃ rujjantī”ti āha. Vejjo “Ayaṃ maṃ vañcetvā kiñci adātukāmā, na me etāya dinnāya bhatiyā attho, idāneva naṃ andhaṃ karissāmī”ti cintetvā gehaṃ gantvā bhariyāya etamatthaṃ ācikkhi. Sā tuṇhī ahosi. So ekaṃ bhesajjaṃ yojetvā tassā santikaṃ gantvā “Bhadde, imaṃ bhesajjaṃ añjehī”ti añjāpesi. Athassā dve akkhīni dīpasikhā viya vijjhāyiṃsu. So vejjo cakkhupālo ahosi. Bhikkhave, tadā mama puttena katakammaṃ pacchato anubandhi. Pāpakammañhi nāmetaṃ dhuraṃ vahato balibaddassa padaṃ cakkaṃ viya anugacchatīti

        • 11.2 Grammar
          • declension of akkhi - neuter noun ending in "i" (rattādigaṇa)
            • nom. akkhi / akkhī, akkhīni
            • voc. (bho) akkhi / (bhavantāni) akkhī, akkhīni
            • acc. akkhiṃ / akkhī, akkhīni
            • The remaining forms are equal to that of aggi (m.):
            • ins. akkhinā / akkhīhi, akkhībhi, akkhihi, akkhibhi
            • dat/gen. akkhino, akkhissa / akkhīnaṃ, akkhinaṃ
            • abl. akkhinā, akkhismā, akkhimhā / akkhīhi, akkhībhi, akkhihi, akkhibhi
            • loc. akkhismiṃ, akkhimhi / akkhīsu, akkhisu
          • some neuter gender nouns ending in ‘i’:

          • niggahīta sandhi
            • ñakārādesa sandhi↔sandhi in which the ṁ, when followed by ‘h', ‘e’ and ‘y’, changes into ñ
              • ṁ + h > {{30830733333747595::ñh: evaṃ + hi > evañhi (evañhi vo bhikkhave sikkhitabbaṃ)}} ṁ + e > {{30830733333747595::ññe (double): paccattaṃ + eva > paccattaññeva (paccattaññeva parinibbissāmi)}} ṁ + y > {{30830733333747595::ññ: saṃ + yācikāya > saññācikāya (saññācikāya pana bhikkhunā kuṭiṃ kārayamānena)}}
          • parassara dīgha sandhi
            • sandhi in which the previous vowel is elided and the following is lengthened (vuddhi) such as: buddha + anussati > buddh + anussati > buddh + ānussati > buddhānussati; yāni + idha > yānīdha (yānīdha bhūtāni samāgatāni); appassuto + ayaṃ > appassutāyaṃ (appassutāyaṃ puriso); saddhā + idha > saddhīdha (saddhīdha vittaṃ purisassa seṭṭhaṃ)
        • Lesson 11 - exercises
          • 11.1 exercise
            • translation
              • "In the past, when King Kāsi ruled in Bārāṇasī, a doctor, while wandering through villages and towns, providing medical treatments, saw a woman with weak eyesight and inquired, 'What is your discomfort?' She replied, 'I am unable to see.' The doctor said, 'I will prepare a medicine for you,' to which she replied, 'Please do so, master.' He asked, 'What will you give me in return?' to which she replied, 'If you are able to restore my eyesight to normal, my children and I will become your servants.' He said, 'That is good,' and arranged the medicine. With just one dose of the medicine, her eyes returned to normal. The thought occurred to her, 'I have promised him that my children and I would become his servants, but he will certainly not treat us kindly. I will deceive him.' She approached him, and when asked about her condition, she claimed that her eyes used to hurt a little but now hurt even more. The doctor thought, 'This woman has deceived me and does not intend to give me anything. I am not in need of her payment so now I will surely make her blind.' After thinking this, he went home and shared his idea with his wife, who remained silent. He mixed the medicine, returned to the woman, and said, 'Madam, please apply this medicine,' making her apply it. Soon after, both her eyes burned like the flame of a lamp." "That doctor became Cakkhupāla. Monks, when that deed was performed by my son, it followed after him. The so-called evil deed follows after one, just like the wheel follows the hoof of the beast of burden."
      • Lesson 12
        • 12.1. reading
          • Na verena verāni sammanti Na hi verenāti imaṃ dhammadesanaṃ satthā jetavane viharanto aññataraṃ vañjhitthiṃ ārabbha kathesi. Eko kira kuṭumbikaputto pitari kālakate khette ca ghare ca sabbakammāni attanāva karonto mātaraṃ paṭijaggi. Athassa mātā “Kumārikaṃ te, tāta, ānessāmī”ti āha. “Amma, mā evaṃ vadetha, ahaṃ yāvajīvaṃ tumhe paṭijaggissāmī”ti. “Tāta, khette ca ghare ca kiccaṃ tvameva karosi, tena mayhaṃ cittasukhaṃ nāma na hoti, ānessāmī”ti. So punappunaṃ paṭikkhipitvā tuṇhī ahosi. Sā ekaṃ kulaṃ gantukāmā gehā nikkhami. Atha naṃ putto “Kataraṃ kulaṃ gacchathā”ti pucchitvā “Asukakulaṃ nāmā”ti vutte tattha gamanaṃ paṭisedhetvā attano abhirucitaṃ kulaṃ ācikkhi. Sā tattha gantvā kumārikaṃ vāretvā divasaṃ vavatthapetvā taṃ ānetvā tassa ghare akāsi. Sā vañjhā ahosi. Atha naṃ mātā 'putta, tvaṃ attano ruciyā kumārikaṃ āṇāpesi, sā idāni vañjhā jātā, aputtakañca nāma kulaṃ vinassati, paveṇī na ghaṭīyati, tena aññaṃ te kumārikaṃ ānemī'ti. Tena “Alaṃ, ammā”ti vuccamānāpi punappunaṃ kathesi.

        • 12.2 grammar
          • *declension of the noun mātu (f.; satthādigaṇa)
            • nom. mātā / mātaro
            • voc. (bhoti) māta, " / (bhotiyo) "
            • acc. mātaraṃ, (mātuṁ [nrtdpn]) / mātaro, mātare
            • ins/abl. mātuyā, mātyā, mātarā / mātūhi, mātūbhi, mātarehi, mātarebhi
            • dat/gen. mātu, mātuyā, mātyā, mātussa / mātūnaṁ, mātānaṁ, mātarānaṁ
            • loc. mātuyā, mātyā, mātuyaṃ, mātyaṃ, mātari / mātūsu, mātaresu
            • mem aid:
              • closely related to pitu
              • pitunā > mātuyā, mātyā
              • extra forms in abl. and loc.
            • note:
              • dhītu / duhitu (daughter) are similarly declined but without the shortened forms mātyā or mātyaṁ
          • declension of the noun dhītu / duhitu (f.) (satthādigaṇa) #[[final exam pāḷi]]
            • nom. dhītā / dhītaro
            • voc. (bhoti) dhīta, dhītā / (bhotiyo) dhītaro
            • acc. dhītaraṃ / dhītaro
            • ins. & abl. dhītuyā, dhītarā / dhītūhi/ūbhi, dhītarehi/ebhi
            • dat/gen. dhītu, dhītuyā, dhītussa / dhītūnaṁ, dhītarānaṁ, dhītānaṁ
            • loc. dhītuyā, dhītuyaṃ, dhītari / dhītūsu, dhītaresu
            • mem aid:
              • same as mātu, without the mātyā and mātyaṁ forms
          • niggahīta sandhi
            • niggahīta lopa sandhi (sara / vyañjana)
              • sandhi in which the niggahīta is elided, when followed by either a vowel (vidūnaṃ + aggaṃ > vidūna + aggaṃ > vidūnaggaṃ (a remains short due to the saññoga that follows)) or a consonant (ariyasaccānaṃ + dassanaṃ > ariyasaccānadassanaṃ)
              • note:
                • sometimes the object is written in the genitive case: kammassa karaṇaṁ ariyasaccānaṁ dassanaṁ > ariyasaccāna dassanaṁ etaṁ buddhāna(ṁ) sāsanaṁ
            • niggahīta āgama sandhi
              • sandhi in which a niggahīta is inserted cakkhu + udapādi > cakkhuṃ udapādi sometimes between two letters: ta + sampayuttā > taṃsampayuttā (taṃsampayuttakānañca dhammānaṃ)
              • #corrections
              • #corrections
            • niggahīta sandhi
              • lopa
                • sara
                • vyañjana
              • āgama
                • sara
                • vyañjana
        • Lesson 12 - Exercises
          • translation:
            • Hatred is not appeased by hatred "Not indeed by hatred" - the Master delivered this discourse while dwelling in Jetavana concerning a certain infertile lady. It is said that the son of a householder, when his father passed away, was taking care of his mother while doing all the works in the field and in the house by himself. Then his mother said thus "I will bring a girl for you, son". He replied, "Mother, do not say such things, I will take care of you for my whole life". "Son, you do all the work in the field and in the house by yourself. Due to that there is no such thing as happiness for me. I will indeed bring one." After rejecting her suggestions again and again, he became silent. She then left the house intending to approach a certain family when the son asked "To which family are you going?", and when he was told "To such and such a family" he prevented her departure and informed her the family of his preference. She went there, proposed to a lady, fixed a date for the marriage, brought her and established her in his house. But she turned out to be infertile. Then the mother said "Son, you ordered the girl of your preference, but she turned out to be infertile. By having no children, the family perishes, and the lineage is not continued. Due to that, I will bring you yet another girl". Even though she was told by her son not to do so, she insisted repeatedly.
          • 12.1 Exercises
            • 1). Answer the following questions in Pāḷi.
              • i. Satthā jetavane viharanto kiṃ kathesi?
                • Satthā jetavane viharanto "na hi verenā'ti imaṁ dhammadesanaṁ kathesi
              • ii. Kasmiṃ kālakate kuṭumbikaputto mātaraṃ paṭijaggi?
                • Pitari kālakate kuṭumbikaputto mātaraṁ paṭijaggi.
              • iii. Assa mātā kiṃ ānessāmīti āha?
                • Assa mātā kumārikaṁ ānessāmīti āha.
              • iv. Kuṭumbikaputto kiṃ vatvā ammaṃ nivāresi? (nivāreti = paṭisedheti)
                • Kuṭumbikaputto "amma, mā evaṁ vadetha, ahaṁ yāvajīvaṁ tumhe paṭijaggissāmī'ti vatvā ammaṁ nivāresi
              • v. kasmā ammāya cittasukhaṃ nāhosi?
                • Yasmā khette ca ghare ca kiccaṁ tāya putto eva akari tasmā ammāya cittasukhaṁ nāhosi
              • vi. Ammā abhirucitaṃ kulaṃ gantvā kiṃ akāsi?
                • Ammā abhirucitaṁ kulaṁ gantvā kumārikaṁ vāretvā divasaṁ vavatthapetvā taṁ ānetvā tassa ghare akāsi.
            • 2). Separate the following combined words found in the lesson and name their sandhi.
              • i. verenāti = verena + iti (pubbassara dīgha sandhi)
              • ii. attanāva = attanā + eva (parassara lopa sandhi)
              • iii. tvameva = tvaṁ + eva (makārādesa sandhi)
            • 3). combine the following words using the most appropriate euphonic combination.
              • i. gacchatha + iti = gacchathāti
              • ii. aputtakaṃ + ca = aputtakañca
              • iii. ānessāmi + iti = ānessāmīti
          • 12.2 Exercises
            • 1). Combine the following words using the most appropriate niggahīta sandhi.
              • i. evaṃ + ahaṃ = evamahaṁ
              • ii. bhuñjituṃ + kāmo = bhuñjitukāmo
            • 2). Combine the following words by inserting a niggahīta.
              • i. cakkhu + udapādi = cakkhuṁ udapādi
              • ii. aṇu + thūlāni = aṇuṁ thūlāni
      • Lesson 13
        • 13.1. reading
          • Na verena verāni sammanti - II Vañjhitthī taṃ kathaṃ sutvā “Puttā nāma mātāpitūnaṃ vacanaṃ atikkamituṃ na sakkonti, idāni aññaṃ vijāyiniṃ itthiṃ ānetvā maṃ dāsibhogena bhuñjissanti. Yannūnāhaṃ sayameva ekaṃ kumārikaṃ āneyya”nti cintetvā ekaṃ kulaṃ gantvā tassatthāya kumārikaṃ vāretvā “Kiṃ nāmetaṃ amma, vadasī”ti tehi paṭikkhittā “Ahaṃ vañjhā, aputtakaṃ nāma kulaṃ vinassati, tumhākaṃ pana dhītā puttaṃ vā dhītaraṃ vā labhitvā kuṭumbikassa sāminī bhavissati, mayhaṃ sāmikassa naṃ dethā”ti yācitvā ānetvā sāmikassa ghare akāsi. Athassā etadahosi “Sacāyaṃ puttaṃ vā dhītaraṃ vā labhissati, ayameva kuṭumbassa sāminī bhavissati. Yathā dārakaṃ na labhati, tatheva naṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti. Atha naṃ sā āha “Amma, yadā te kucchiyaṃ gabbho patiṭṭhāti, atha me āroceyyāsī”ti. Sā “Sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā gabbhe patiṭṭhite tassā ārocesi. Itarissā pana sā sayameva niccaṃ yāgubhattaṃ deti, athassā āhāreneva saddhiṃ gabbhapātanabhesajjamadāsi, gabbho pati.
          • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
            • atikkamati↔goes beyond, passes over, overcomes; surpasses
            • sakkoti↔is able of, is capable of
            • vijāyinī (f.)↔the lady who gives birth to children
            • bhoga (m.)↔usage, possession, wealth, enjoyment, the coil of a snake
            • bhuñjati↔makes use of, enjoys, eats
            • yannūna (ind.)↔“It is good …” used mostly with sattamī vibhatti
              • mostly found in sentences with an {{5171270220887123::optative verb}}; it is grammatically connected with the verb of the sentence

        • 13.2 grammar
          • when is the suffix -āya used in the purisādigaṇa?
            • when the dative case of the purisādigaṇa has the meaning of "for", the suffix used is -āya instead of -assa (tassatthāya "for his benefit"), therefore "namo buddhāya" is not in accordance with the pāḷi grammar but is a sanskritization, since the sanskrit grammar allows such use
          • 27 sabbanāmas (pronouns) in Pāḷi (divided into 6 groups):
            • sabba, katara, katama, ubhaya (collection of 2), itara, añña
            • aññatara, aññatama
              • all above are decined as sabba
                • except sabba and ubhaya, the others have 'i' form as katarissa
            • pubba, para, apara, dakkhiṇa, uttara, adhara
              • decined as sabba, but with added purisādi forms in m. and nt., nom.pl., abl.sg. and loc.sg. - pubbā, pubbe
            • (from here onwards, no ālapana and each with its own declension)
            • ya (like sabba), ta, eta, ima, amu, kiṃ
            • eka, ubha, dvi, ti, catu
            • tumha, amha
          • cakārādesa sandhi
            • sandhi in which the syllable ‘ti’ of the prefixes 'ati-', 'pati-' and indeclinable 'iti', is substituted by the consonant ‘c’ which is then doubled as 'cc' (due to dvebhāvasandhi) pati- (pati + ayo > pac + ayo > paccayo) ati- (ati + antaṃ > ac + antaṃ > accantaṃ) iti (iti + etaṃ > ic + etaṃ > iccetaṃ)
              • under the dvebhāvasandhi it says that the beginning consonant of the second word is duplicated, but here it is the ending 'ti' of the first word #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • dakārādi avasesa ādesa sandhi
            • sandhi in which the consonant ‘dh’ changes into ‘d’ (ekamidāhaṃ bhikkhave samayaṁ ⇒ ekamidha + ahaṃ ⇒ ekamidh + ahaṃ ⇒ ekamidh + āhaṃ ⇒ ekamid + āhaṃ ⇒ ekamidāhaṃ)
            • sandhi in which the consonant ‘dh’ changes into ‘h’ when followed by 'u' (sādhu dassanamariyānaṃ ⇒ sāhu dassanamariyānaṃ)
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • avasesa [ava + √sis + *a]→adj. remaining; rest of
          • yakārādesa sandhi
            • sandhi in which the vowels 'e' and 'i' are substituted by 'y', when followed by a vowel and a dissimilar vowel respectively 'e' + vowel (me + ayaṃ > my + ayaṃ > myāyaṃ [adhigato kho myāyaṃ dhammo]) (note: a becoming ā is a vyañjana sandhi) 'i' + dissimilar vowel (paṭisanthāravutti + assa > paṭisaṅthāravuttyassa > paṭisaṅthāravutyassa (tty becomes ty due to another sandhi)
              • according to grammar, when three consonants are together and two of them are similar, the first among them will be elided; this is called {{07400983666244176::byañjana visaṃyoga}}
          • vakārādesa sandhi
            • sandhi in which the vowels ‘o’ and ‘u’, when followed by a vowel, are substituted by ‘v’ 'o' + vowel (atha kho assa > atha khvassa) 'u' + vowel (anu + eti ⇒ anveti)
          • abbha-ajjha ādesa sandhi
            • sandhi in which the prefixes ‘abhi’ and 'adhi', when followed by a vowel, are substituted by ‘abbha’ and ‘ajjha’ respectively abhi -> abbha (abhi + okāso -> abbha + okāso -> abbhokāso [pubbassaralopasandhi]) adhi -> ajjha (adhi + agama -> ajjha + agamā -> ajjhagamā)
        • Lesson 13 exercises
          • 13.1 exercise
            • translation
              • Not by hatred is hatred appeased - II After hearing that conversation the infertile lady thought, "The so-called children are unable to overcome the word of their parents. Now they will bring another fertile lady and will use me as a slave. It is better if I bring a girl by-myself". After thinking in this way, she approached a certain family, and for her husband's benefit, made a proposal to the family's girl. They rejected, saying "What is this you say, dear?". She then insisted saying "I am infertile. Without children a family is certainly destroyed, but your daughter, after having begotten a son or daughter, will become the mistress of the family. Please marry her to my husband." After having begged thus she brought the lady and established her in the house. Then a thought occurred to the infertile lady "If this girl begets a son or daughter she will certainly become the mistress of the family. Whatever prevents her from having a child, it is suitable to do exactly that to her". Then the infertile wife told the newly arrived wife, "Dear, when you get pregnant, do let me know". She replied "Excellent!". When her pregnancy happened, she informed the infertile wife. The infertile one, by herself, used to give the new wife gruel and rice. Then she gave her poison for abortion mixed with the food and due to that, she had a miscarriage.
      • Lesson 14
        • 14.1. reading
          • Na verena verāni sammanti - III Dutiyampi gabbhe patiṭṭhite ārocesi, itarā dutiyampi tatheva pātesi. Atha naṃ paṭivissakitthiyo pucchiṃsu - “Kacci te sapattī antarāyaṃ karotī”ti? Sā tamatthaṃ ārocetvā “Andhabāle, kasmā evamakāsi, ayaṃ tava gabbhassa pātanabhesajjaṃ yojetvā deti. Tena te gabbho patatī”ti vuttā tatiyavāre na kathesi. Atha sā itarissā udaraṃ disvā pariṇate gabbhe okāsaṃ labhitvā bhesajjaṃ yojetvā adāsi. Gabbho pariṇatattā patituṃ asakkonto tiriyaṃ nipati. Kharā vedanā uppajji. Sā “Tvameva maṃ ānetvā tvameva tayopi vāre dārake nāsesi, idāni ahampi nassāmi, ito cutā yakkhinī hutvā tava dārake khādituṃ samatthā hutvā nibbatteyya”nti patthanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā kālaṃ katvā tasmiṃyeva gehe majjārī hutvā nibbatti. Itarampi sāmiko gahetvā “Tvaṃ me kulūpacchedaṃ akāsī”ti taṃ pothesi. Sā teneva ābādhena kālaṃ katvā tattheva kukkuṭī hutvā nibbatti. Kukkuṭī na cirasseva aṇḍāni vijāyi, majjārī āgantvā tāni aṇḍāni khādi. Dutiyampi tatiyampi khādiyeva. Kukkuṭī cintesi “Tayo vāre mama aṇḍāni khāditvā idāni mampi khāditukāmāsī”ti. “Ito cutā saputtakaṃ taṃ khādituṃ labheyya”nti patthanaṃ katvā tato cutā araññe dīpinī hutvā nibbatti. Itarā migī hutvā nibbatti.

        • 14.2 grammar
          • why the verb labhati is with a short a, while the noun lābha is with a long ā?→because the noun is constructed by adding the vikaraṇapaccaya ṇa as so: labh + (ṇ)a > lābha (noun) labh + a + ti > labhati (verb)
          • -tha (suffix) (tattha, yattha, kattha, kuttha, sabbattha, ettha [eta+tha])↔suffix added to pronouns with locative meaning, sometimes meaning "to" as the goal of motion; the word becomes a nipāta
          • 5 types of nāma (nouns) #[[final exam 1st year]]
            • nāmanāma (proper nouns)
            • sabbanāma (pronouns)
            • samāsanāma (compound nouns): constructed by combining two nouns
            • taddhitanāma (secondary derivatives): constructed by adding a suffix to a noun
            • kitakanāma (primary derivative): constructed by adding a suffix to a root (tbc)
          • {{07381633912451924::divādigaṇa }}verbs may have active or passive meaning such as nassati or muccati; since {{07381633912451924::the vikaraṇa paccaya used in both meanings is }}{{07381633912451924::ya}}
          • vyañjana sandhi
            • lopāgama sandhi↔sandhi in which the vowel ‘o’ is elided, and 'a' is inserted when followed by a consonant so + ve = sa ve ([sa ve kāsāvamarahati])
            • o ādesa sandhi↔sandhi in which the prefix ava- is substituted by the vowel 'o' when followed by a consonant (ava + sānaṃ ⇒ o + sānaṃ ⇒ osānaṃ; the same occurs to okāso, otarati, and oruhati)
            • paṭi ādesa sandhi↔sandhi in which the prefix pati- changes into paṭi- when followed by a vowel or a consonant (paṭaggi dātabbo [pati + aggi ⇒ paṭi + aggi])
            • dīgha sandhi↔sandhi in which a vowel is lengthened when followed by a consonant; this mostly happens in gāthās (evaṃ gāme munī care [muni + care])
            • rassa sandhi↔sandhi in which a vowel is shortened when followed by a consonant; this mostly happens in gāthās (puggalā dhammadasā > puggala dhammadasā)
            • asadisa dvebhāva sandhi↔when an aspirated consonant is duplicated, its unaspirated counterpart is augmented (paṭhama + jhāna > paṭhamajjhānaṃ)
        • Lesson 14 exercises
          • translation
            • Not by hatred is hatred appeased - III When she conceived for the second time, she again informed it, and the other once again caused a miscarriage in the same way. Then neighboring women asked her, "Could it be that the other wife of your husband do you harm?". She told the neighbors the matter and they said, "You foolish, why did you do like this? That woman prepares poison for abortion and gives it to you. Because of that your children die". After that, on the third occasion, she did not disclose her pregnancy. Then, the other one, after seeing her belly when the fetus was mature, prepared the poison and gave her when an opportunity arose. Because of being developed, the embryo did not come out but died dislocated, causing an intense pain. The pregnant wife lamented, "You alone brought me here, you alone killed my children on three occasions, and now I will also die! After death, may I be reborn as a female demon capable of eating your children!". After wishing in this way and passing away, she was reborn as a female cat in that very house. The husband then grabbed the other wife shouting, "You have destroyed my family!" and beat her up. Because of that oppression she passed away and was reborn as a hen in that very area. Not long after that, the hen laid eggs and the female cat came and ate them. It did so even for a second and a third time. The hen then thought, "After eating my eggs on three occasions, you are now wishing to eat me as well!". She made a wish, "Passing from here, may I get the opportunity to eat her as well as her children!", and passing from there she was reborn in a forest as a female panther, while the other was reborn as a doe.
      • Lesson 15
        • asavaṇṇādesasandhi↔sandhi in which the vowels i / ī is substituted by e, and the vowels u / ū are substituted by o; these substitutions happen only when the dissimilar previous vowel is elided (upa + ikkhati = upekkhati) (yathā udake ⇒ yath_ + odake ⇒ yathodake)
          • the vowels {{19734471845258872::e}}{{19734471845258872:: and }}{{19734471845258872::o}} do not have another vowel with similar sound so they are called {{19734471845258872::asavaṇṇa}}
        • sandhi chart #[[final exam 1st year]]
          • sarasandhi
            • lopa
              • pubba sara lopa (s + s > _ + s) (loka + aggo ⇒ lok_ + aggo = lokaggo)
              • para sara lopa (s + ≠s > s + _) (cattāro + ime = cattārome)
            • ādesa
              • asavaṇṇādesa (≠s + i / ī > e | ≠s + u / ū > o) (upekkhati) (yathodake)
              • cakārādesa (pati / ati / iti > c > cc [dvebhāva]) (paccayo) (accantaṁ) (iccetaṁ)
              • dakārādi avasesa ādesa (dh + s > d | dh + s > h) (ekamidāhaṃ) (sāhu) (sugato)
              • yakārādesa (e + s > y | i + ≠s > y) (tyāhaṃ) (vutyassa)
              • vakārādesa (o / u + s > v + s) (khvassa) (anveti)
              • abbha-/ajjha-ādesa (abhi + s > abbha | adhi + s > ajjha) (abbhokāso) (ajjhagamā)
              • mem aid: following the alphabet: e and o (from the vowels), ca, da, ya, va, abhi/adhi
            • dīgha
              • pubba sara dīgha (s + s > vu + _) (sādhu + iti ⇒ sādhū + _ti ⇒ sādhūti)
              • para sara dīgha (s + s > _ + vu) (buddha + anussati ⇒ buddh_ + ānussati ⇒ buddhānussati)
            • āgama (s + s > s + yvmdntrl + s)
              • yakārāgama (nayidaṃ)
              • vakārāgama (tivaṅgikaṃ)
              • makārāgama (idhamāhu)
              • dakārāgama (udayo)
              • nakārāgama (ito + āyati = ito nāyati)
              • takārāgama (tasmātiha)
              • rakārāgama (nirantaraṃ)
              • lakārāgama (chaḷabhiññā)
                • there is no difference between l and ḷ; in pāḷi ḷ is used in the place of ḍ in sanskrit
            • note:
              • s = sara rs = rassa sara ≠ = dissimilar b = byañjana mp = mahāpāṇa vu = vuddhi vgk = vaggakkhara vgtb = vaggantabyañjana
          • byañjanasandhi
            • lopāgama (o + b > _ + b > a + b) (esa dhammo sanantano)
            • ādesa
              • o ādesa (ava + b > o + b) (okāsa)
              • paṭi ādesa (pati > paṭi) (paṭihaññati)
            • dīgha (s + b > vu + b) (munī care)
            • rassa (s + b > rs + b) (puggala dhammadasā)
            • āgama
              • dvebhāva āgama
                • sadisa dvebhāva (pa + kamati > pakkamati)
                • asadisa dvebhāva (mp + mp > b + mp [kh + kh > kkh]) (paṭhama jhāna > paṭhamajjhāna)
            • note:
              • s = sara rs = rassa sara ≠ = dissimilar b = byañjana mp = mahāpāṇa vu = vuddhi vgk = vaggakkhara vgtb = vaggantabyañjana
          • niggahītasandhi
            • lopa
              • niggahīta lopa sandhi (ṁ + s/b > _ + s/b)
                • followed by sara: (tāsāhaṃ = tāsaṃ + ahaṃ) (here followed by a parassara dīgha sandhi)
                • followed by byañjana: (ariyasaccāna_ dassanaṃ)
              • parassara lopa sandhi (ṁ + s > ṁ + _) (tvaṃ_si)
            • ādesa
              • vaggantādesa (ṁ + vgk > vgtb + vgk) (taṇhaṅkaro = taṇhaṃ + karo)
              • ñakārādesa (ṁ + h/e/y > ñ + h/e/y) (tañhi = taṃ + hi) (paccattaññeva = paccattaṃ + eva) (saññojanaṃ = saṃ + yojanaṃ)
              • makāra ādesa (ṁ + s > m + s) (tamahaṃ = taṃ + ahaṃ)
              • dakāra ādesa (ya/ta/eta + ṁ > ya/ta/eta + d) (etaṃ + avoca = etadavoca)
            • āgama
              • niggahītāgama sandhi (s/b + s/b > s/b + ṁ + s/b) (cakkhu + udapādi > cakkhuṃ udapādi)
            • note:
              • s = sara rs = rassa sara ≠ = dissimilar b = byañjana mp = mahāpāṇa vu = vuddhi vgk = vaggakkhara vgtb = vaggantabyañjana

      • Lesson 16
        • 16.1. reading
          • Na Verena Verāni Sammanti - IV Tassā migiyā vijātakāle dīpinī āgantvā tayo vāre puttake khādi. Migī maraṇakāle “Ayaṃ me tikkhattuṃ puttake khāditvā idāni mampi khādissati, ito dāni cutā etaṃ saputtakaṃ khādituṃ labheyya”nti patthanaṃ katvā ito cutā yakkhinī hutvā nibbatti. Dīpinīpi tatheva tato cutā sāvatthiyaṃ kuladhītā hutvā nibbatti. Sā vuddhippattā dvāragāmake patikulaṃ agamāsi. Aparabhāge ca puttaṃ vijāyi. Yakkhinīpi tassā piyasahāyikāvaṇṇena āgantvā “Kuhiṃ me sahāyikā”ti “Antogabbhe vijātā”ti vutte “Puttaṃ nu kho vijātā udāhu dhītaranti passissāmi na”nti gabbhaṃ pavisitvā passantī viya dārakaṃ gahetvā khāditvā gatā. Puna dutiyavārepi tatheva khādi. Tatiyavāre itarā garubhārā hutvā sāmikaṃ āmantetvā “Sāmi, imasmiṃ ṭhāne ekā yakkhinī mama dve putte khāditvā gatā, idāni mama kulagehaṃ gantvā vijāyissāmī”ti kulagehaṃ gantvā vijāyi. Tadā sā yakkhinī udakavāraṃ gatā hoti. Vessavaṇassa hi yakkhiniyo vārena anotattadahato sīsaparamparāya udakamāharanti. Tā catumāsaccayenapi pañcamāsaccayenapi muccanti. Aparā yakkhiniyo kilantakāyā jīvitakkhayampi pāpuṇanti. Sā pana udakavārato muttamattāva vegena taṃ gharaṃ gantvā “Kuhiṃ me sahāyikā”ti pucchi. “Kuhiṃ naṃ passissasi, tassā imasmiṃ ṭhāne jātajātadārake yakkhinī āgantvā khādati, tasmā kulagehaṃ gatā”ti.

        • Lesson 16 - Exercises
          • translation:
            • Not by hatred is hatred appeased - IV When the doe had given birth the female panther came and on three occasions ate the doe's fawns. At the time of its death the doe made the wish, "This one, after eating my fawns on three occasions, will now eat me as well! After dying here, may I now get the chance of eating her and her children!". After death she was reborn as a female demon. In the same way the female panther passed away from there and was reborn as the daughter of a family in Sāvatthi. After growing up she went to live with the family of her husband by the village gate. After some time she delivered a son and the female demon came with the appearance of her close friend and said "where is my girlfriend?". When she was told that she had delivered and was inside the room, she said "I will take a look whether she has delivered a son or a daughter" and entered the room as if to take a look, took the child and after eating it, she was gone. In the same way, on a second occasion she ate the child again. On the third time the other became pregnant, she addressed her husband, "Dear husband, in this place a female demon ate my two children and was gone. This time I will go to my family's house in order to give birth." She did so and gave birth. At that time that female demon was gone for carrying water. The meaning is this: the female demons of Vessavaṇa take turns to bring water from the lake Anotatta by passing it from head to head in a line. After four or five months have elapsed, they are released. Some exhausted female demons pass away. Right when that female demon was released from carrying water, she hurriedly went to that house and asked, "Where is my girlfriend?". She was told, "How could you see her? In this place a female demon comes and eats all the children who are born, so she has gone to her family's house."
      • Lesson 17
        • 17.1. reading
          • Na verena verāni sammanti - V Sā yakkhinī “Yattha vā tattha vā gacchatu, na mayā muccissatī”ti nagarābhimukhī pakkhandi. Itarāpi nāmaggahaṇadivase naṃ dārakaṃ nhāpetvā nāmaṃ katvā, “Sāmi, idāni sakagharaṃ gacchāmā”ti puttamādāya sāmikena saddhiṃ vihāramajjhe gatamaggena gacchantī puttaṃ sāmikassa datvā vihārapokkharaṇiyā nhātvā sāmike nhāyante uttaritvā puttassa thaññaṃ pāyamānā ṭhitā yakkhiniṃ āgacchantiṃ disvā sañjānitvā, “Sāmi, vegena ehi, ayaṃ sā yakkhinī, vegena ehi, ayaṃ sā yakkhinī”ti uccāsaddaṃ katvā yāva tassa āgamanaṃ saṇṭhātuṃ asakkontī nivattetvā antovihārābhimukhī pakkhandi. Tasmiṃ samaye satthā parisamajjhe dhammaṃ desesi. Sā puttaṃ tathāgatassa pādapiṭṭhe nipajjāpetvā “Tumhākaṃ mayā esa dinno, puttassa me jīvitaṃ dethā”ti āha. Dvārakoṭṭhake adhivattho sumanadevo nāma yakkhiniyā anto pavisituṃ nādāsi. Satthā ānandattheraṃ āmantetvā “Gaccha, ānanda, taṃ yakkhiniṃ pakkosāhī”ti āha. Thero pakkosi. Itarā “Ayaṃ, bhante, āgacchatī”ti āha. Satthā “Etu, mā saddamakāsī”ti vatvā taṃ āgantvā ṭhitaṃ “Kasmā evaṃ karosi, sace tumhe mādisassa buddhassa sammukhībhāvaṃ nāgamissatha, ahinakulānaṃ viya acchaphandanānaṃ viya kākolūkānaṃ viya ca kappaṭṭhitikaṃ vo veraṃ abhavissa, kasmā veraṃ paṭiveraṃ karotha. Verañhi averena upasammati, no verenā”ti vatvā imaṃ gāthamāha – “Na hi verena verāni, sammantīdha kudācanaṃ; averena ca sammanti, esa dhammo sanantano”ti.

        • 17.2 grammar
          • kālātipatti vibhatti (conditional mode)
            • kālātipatti vibhatti is used to express:
              • an action that could have happened but didn't
              • an action that could have happened but was prevented by to another action
              • the action that prevented the main action
              • note:
                • sometimes both actions are expressed by kālātipatti
                  • 'sace so paṭhamavaye pabbajjaṃ alabhissa, arahā abhavissa'
                • sometimes both sattamī and kālātipatti verbs are used in the same sentence
                  • 'sace sukkā dhammā lokaṃ na pāleyyuṃ, sambhedaṃ loko agamissa'
            • verbal terminations of kālātipatti
              • (a)....(i)ssā, (a)....(i)ssa / (a)....(i)ssaṃsu
              • (a)....(i)sse / (a)....(i)ssatha
              • (a)....(i)ssaṃ / (a)....(i)ssāmhā, (a)....(i)ssāmha
              • note:
                • while forming verbs in the kālātipatti vibhatti, as in the case of ajjatanī vibhatti, the vowel ‘a’ is augmented at the beginning of the root and the vowel ‘i’ is augmented at the end of the root
                • long endings ā can become short a
            • conjugation of the kālātipatti vibhatti of √bhū – to exist
              • abhavissā, bhavissā, abhavissa, bhavissa / abhavissaṃsu, bhavissaṃsu
              • abhavisse, bhavisse / abhavissatha, bhavissatha
              • abhavissaṃ, bhavissaṃ / abhavissāmhā, bhavissāmhā, abhavissāmha, bhavissāmha
        • 17.2 exercises
          • translation
            • Not by hatred is hatred appeased - V That demoness thought "whatever place you may go to, you will not escape from me" and sprung forward heading towards the city. The other one, in the naming day, bathed the child, gave the child a name and requested her husband, "Dear husband, let us now go to our house." She then took the child, and together with him went by a road that passed through the middle of the monastery. She gave the child to him, took a bath in the monastery's pond, came out and stood breastfeeding while he bathed. She then saw and recognized the demoness approaching and shouted, "Husband, come quickly, this is that demoness! Come quickly, this is that demoness!". Being unable to stand still until his arrival, she turned back and sprung forward, heading towards the inside of the monastery. At that time, the Teacher was expounding the Dhamma in the presence of the assembly. She placed the child lying on the Tathāgata's feet and pleaded, "This child is offered to you by me, I beseech you to grant life to my son!". The deva by the name of Sumana, who dwelt in the chamber over the gate, did not grant the demoness permission to enter. The Teacher then addressed the thera Ānanda saying, "Go, Ānanda, and summon that demoness". The thero did so. The other one exclaimed "This is the one, bhante, she is coming!" The Teacher then said "Come, do not make a sound". The demoness came and stood still. "Why do you do like this? Had you not met an Awakened One like me face to face, like snakes and mongooses, like bears and phandana-trees, like crows and owls, your enmity would have lasted for an aeon. Why are you hostile and vengeful? Hatred is only appeased by amity, not by hatred". After saying this, He uttered the following verse: "Not indeed by hatred is hatred ever appeased here, but by amity it is appeased, this is an everlasting truth."
      • Lesson 18
        • 18 reading
          • Sāriputta Thera Vatthu - I Anuppanneyeva buddhe rājagahato avidūre upatissagāmo kolitagāmoti dve brāhmaṇagāmā ahesuṃ. Tesu upatissagāme sāriyā nāma brāhmaṇiyā gabbhassa patiṭṭhitadivaseyeva kolitagāme moggaliyā nāma brāhmaṇiyāpi gabbho patiṭṭhāsi. Tāni kira dvepi kulāni yāva sattamā kulaparivaṭṭā (abl.) paṭibaddhasahāyakāneva (...āni eva) ahesuṃ, tāsaṃ dvinnampi ekadivasameva gabbhaparihāraṃ adaṃsu. Tā ubhopi dasamāsaccayena putte vijāyiṃsu. Nāmaggahaṇadivase sāriyā brāhmaṇiyā puttassa upatissagāmake jeṭṭhakulassa puttattā upatissoti nāmaṃ kariṃsu, itarassa kolitagāme jeṭṭhakulassa puttattā kolitoti nāmaṃ kariṃsu. Te ubhopi vuḍḍhimanvāya sabbasippānaṃ pāraṃ agamaṃsu. Upatissamāṇavassa kīḷanatthāya nadiṃ vā uyyānaṃ vā gamanakāle pañca suvaṇṇasivikasatāni parivārāni honti, kolitamāṇavassa pañca ājaññayuttarathasatāni. Dvepi janā pañcapañcamāṇavakasataparivārā honti. Rājagahe ca anusaṃvaccharaṃ giraggasamajjo nāma ahosi. Tesaṃ dvinnampi ekaṭṭhāneyeva mañcaṃ bandhanti. Dvepi ekato nisīditvā samajjaṃ passantā hasitabbaṭṭhāne hasanti, saṃvegaṭṭhāne saṃvejenti, dāyaṃ dātuṃ yuttaṭṭhāne dāyaṃ denti.

        • Lesson 18 - exercises
          • translation:
            • The story of the Elder Sāriputta - I When the Buddha had not yet arisen, not very far from Rājagaha, there were two brahmin villages called Upatissa Village and Kolita Village. Among them, in the Upatissa village, on the very same day of the conception of the embryo of the brahmin lady named Sārī, in the Kolita village as well, the embryo of the brahmin lady named Moggalī got conceived. It is said that both of these families, from as far as the seventh generation, were bound by friendship. On the very same day, both families provided protection to the embryo of each. Both of them gave birth to a son after ten months had passed. On the day of their naming ceremony, they gave the brahmin lady Sāri's son the name Upatissa, due to being the son of the eldest family in the Upatissa Village. In the Kolita Village, they gave the other the name of Kolita, also due to being the son of the eldest family in the Kolita Village. And both of them after growing up achieved mastery of every field of knowledge. (lit. went to the other shore of every skill) At the time of going to the river or to the garden for the sake of entertainment, the young man Upatissa was accompanied by five hundred golden palanquins as retinue. Five hundred chariots with thoroughbred horses would accompany the young man Kolita as retinue. Each of the two fellows had a following of 500 young men. In Rājagaha there was an annual festival called Giragga and a seat was prepared in the same place for both of them. After sitting together, while watching the performance, they would laugh at moments of humor, feel fear at the frightening moments, and make donations at appropriate occasions for doing so.
      • Lesson 19
        • 19.1 reading
          • Sāriputtattheravatthu - II Tesaṃ (dat./gen pl.) imināva niyāmena ekadivasaṃ samajjaṃ passantānaṃ paripākagatattā ñāṇassa purimadivasesu viya hasitabbaṭṭhāne hāso vā saṃvegaṭṭhāne saṃvego vā dātuṃ yuttaṭṭhāne dānaṃ vā nāhosi. Dvepi pana janā evaṃ cintayiṃsu – “Kimettha oloketabbaṃ atthi, sabbepime appatte vassasate apaṇṇattikabhāvaṃ gamissanti, amhehi pana ekaṃ mokkhadhammaṃ pariyesituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti ārammaṇaṃ gahetvā nisīdiṃsu. Tato kolito upatissaṃ āha – “Samma upatissa, na tvaṃ aññesu divasesu viya haṭṭhapahaṭṭho, idāni anattamanadhātukosi, kiṃ te sallakkhita”nti? “Samma kolita, etesaṃ (dat.pl.) volokane (loc.sg.) sāro natthi, niratthakametaṃ, attano mokkhadhammaṃ gavesituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti idaṃ cintayanto nisinnomhi. Tvaṃ pana kasmā anattamanosī'ti? Sopi tatheva āha. Athassa attanā saddhiṃ ekajjhāsayataṃ ñatvā upatisso āha – “Amhākaṃ ubhinnampi sucintitaṃ, mokkhadhammaṃ pana gavesantehi ekā pabbajjā laddhuṃ vaṭṭati. Kassa santike pabbajāmā”ti?

        • Lesson 19 - exercises
          • translation
            • The story of venerable Sāriputta - II One day, while watching the festival in the same manner, due to the maturity of their wisdom, to them there was no laughter in moments of humor, no fear on the frightening moments and no donations in the occasions for giving, like there had been in previous days. It occured to both of them, "What is there to see here? Before the elapse of a hundred years, all this will have been forgotten (lit. will have gone to the state where not even the name remains), so it is fitting for us to seek a liberating doctrine." They sat contemplating such idea. After that, Kolita addressed Upatissa, "Friend Upatissa, you are not very elated as in other days. You are unhappy now. What are you thinking about? (lit. what is considered by you?)" "Friend Kolita, watching them is not worthwhile (lit. there is no value in watching them). This is meaningless. It is suitable to search for one's own liberation." I am seated considering this. And why are you unhappy?". He also spoke in the same way. Then, after understanding the fact that the same intention had occurred to his friend as to himself, Upatissa said, "It was well thought by both of us. It is appropriate for those who are seeking a liberating doctrine to take up the ascetic life. Under whom should we ordain?"
      • Lesson 20
        • 20.1. reading
          • Sāriputtattheravatthu - III Tena kho pana samayena sañcayo nāma paribbājako rājagahe paṭivasati mahatiyā (f., ins.sg. of mahantī) paribbājakaparisāya (ins.) saddhiṃ. Te “Tassa santike pabbajissāmā”ti pañcamāṇavakasatāni “Sivikāyo ca rathe ca gahetvā gacchathā”ti uyyojetvā ekāya sivikāya ekena rathena gantvā sañcayassa santike pabbajiṃsu. Tesaṃ (gen.) pabbajitakālato paṭṭhāya sañcayo atirekalābhaggayasaggappatto (atireka'lābha'agga'yasa'agga'patto) ahosi. Te katipāheneva sabbaṃ sañcayassa samayaṃ parimadditvā (parigaṇhitvā), “Ācariya, tumhākaṃ (gen.pl.) jānanasamayo ettakova, udāhu uttarimpi atthī”ti pucchiṃsu. “Ettakova, sabbaṃ tumhehi (ins.pl.) ñāta”nti vutte cintayiṃsu – “Evaṃ sati (loc.) imassa santike brahmacariyavāso niratthako, mayaṃ yaṃ mokkhadhammaṃ gavesituṃ nikkhantā, so imassa santike uppādetuṃ na sakkā, mahā kho pana jambudīpo, gāmanigamarājadhāniyo (acc.pl.) carantā addhā mokkhadhammadesakaṃ kañci ācariyaṃ labhissāmā”ti. Tato paṭṭhāya, “Yattha yattha paṇḍitā samaṇabrāhmaṇā atthī”ti vadanti, tattha tattha gantvā sākacchaṃ karonti. Tehi puṭṭhaṃ pañhaṃ aññe (nom.) kathetuṃ na sakkonti, te pana tesaṃ (gen.) pañhaṃ vissajjenti. Evaṃ sakalajambudīpaṃ pariggaṇhitvā nivattitvā sakaṭṭhānameva āgantvā, “Samma kolita, amhesu yo paṭhamaṃ amataṃ adhigacchati, so itarassa ārocetū”ti katikaṃ akaṃsuṃ.

        • Lesson 20 - exercise
          • translation:
            • The story of the elder Sāriputta - III On that occasion, the wandering ascetic named Sañcaya was dwelling in Rājagaha together with a great following of wandering ascetics. Thinking, "Let us ordain under him", they (each) sent their five hundred young men to take the palanquins and chariots and leave, went with (just) one palanquin and chariot and ordained under Sañcaya. Starting from the time of their going-forth, Sañcaya became one who received an abundance of the highest gain and praise. Having investigated (lit. rubbed) all of Sañcaya's philosophy in just a few days, they asked, "Teacher, is the philosophy you know only this much, or is there more?". When they were told, "It is only this much, all of it is known by you", they considered, "If it is so (lit. when being thus), living the noble life under his guidance is meaningless. We left in search of that which is liberation. It is not possible for that to arise under him. But Jambudīpa is very large. Wandering through villages, towns and the royal capital, we will certainly find some teacher who is an expounder of the liberating doctrine". From then onwards, wherever it was said to be wise contemplatives and brahmins, they would go there and have discussions with them. The others were incapable of answering the questions posed by them, but they would answer their questions. After investigating the whole of Jambudīpa in this way, turning back and returning to their very own place, they made an agreement, "Friend Kolita, whichever of us attains the deathless first, let him inform the other".

Tadā “Caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṃ bahujanahitāyā”ti ratanattayaguṇapakāsanatthaṃ uyyojitānaṃ (dat./gen.) ekasaṭṭhiyā arahantānaṃ antare pañcavaggiyānaṃ abbhantaro assajitthero paṭinivattitvā rājagahaṃ āgato, punadivase pātova pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Tasmiṃ samaye upatissaparibbājakopi pātova bhattakiccaṃ katvā paribbājakārāmaṃ gacchanto theraṃ disvā cintesi – “Mayā evarūpo pabbajito nāma na diṭṭhapubboyeva, ye loke arahanto (pl.) vā arahattamaggaṃ vā samāpannā, ayaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ aññataro, yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā puccheyyaṃ – ‘Kaṃsi (kaṁ asi) tvaṃ, āvuso, uddissa pabbajito, ko vā te satthā, kassa vā tvaṃ dhammaṃ rocesī’”ti? (āvuso, tvaṁ kaṁ uddissa pabbajito asi?) Athassa etadahosi – “Akālo kho imaṃ bhikkhuṃ pañhaṃ pucchituṃ, antaragharaṃ paviṭṭho piṇḍāya carati, yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandheyya”nti. So theraṃ laddhapiṇḍapātaṃ aññataraṃ okāsaṃ gacchantaṃ disvā nisīditukāmatañcassa (nisīditukāmataṁ ca assa) ñatvā attano paribbājakapīṭhakaṃ paññāpetvā adāsi, so bhattakiccapariyosānepissa attano kuṇḍikāya udakaṃ adāsi.

        • Lesson 21 - exercises
          • translation
            • The story of the elder Sāriputta - IV While they were living in this way after making the agreement, the Master, travelling by stages as it was previously mentioned, reached Rājagaha, accepted the Bamboo Grove and was dwelling there. At that time, in order to make the qualities of the Triple Gem public, sixty-one arahats, including the group of five, were sent off thus, "Go wander, monks, for the benefit of many people". The elder Assaji, who was included, turned around, came back, reached Rājagaha, and on the early morning of the following day, after taking his bowl and robes, entered Rājagaha for alms. And on that occasion, the wandering ascetic Upatissa, after eating very early morning, while going to the monastery of the wandering ascetics, saw the elder and thought, "Such renunciant, which looks like this, was never seen by me indeed. Of those in the world who are arahants or that have attained the path of arahatship, this individual is one among those monks. It would be good if I were to approach this monk and ask, "Under whom are you ordained? Or who is your teacher? Or whose teachings do you like?". Then it occured to him, "It is the wrong time to ask this monk a question, he has entered the village and is wandering for alms. It is good if I follow this monk from close behind". Having seen the elder going to another place after having received alms, and having understood his desire to sit, he prepared and gave him his own small ascetic chair and at the end of the meal, gave him water from his own water jug.

        • Lesson 22 - exercises
          • translation:
            • The story of the elder Sāriputta - V Having done the teacher's duty in this way and had a pleasant conversation together with the elder who had finished his meal, he said the following, "Friend, your faculties are very clear, your complexion is pure and bright. Under whom, friend, have you ordained, or who is your teacher, or whose teachings do you like?", he asked. The thera tought, "These so called ascetics are opposed to the dispensation, I will show the profundity of this dispensation". Making known his status as a newcomer he said, "Friend, I am a newcomer, recently ordained, newly arrived to this doctrine and discipline, for now I will not be able to preach the doctrine in detail". The ascetic thought, "I am Upatissa, speak according to your ability, be it little or much. It is my responsibility to comprehend it in a hundred ways, in a thousand ways", and said the following, "May you speak, be it little or much. Tell me just the essence. Only the essence is what I need. What is the use of many words? (lit. What will many words do?)". When the elder was told so, he uttered the following verse, "Whatever realities produced by a cause...". Having heard just the first couple lines, the ascetic was established in the fruition of stream-entry adorned with a thousand methods. The other couple lines ended at the time of being a stream-enterer.
      • Lesson 23 - samāsa
        • introduction
          • samāsa is
            • the act of combining (compounding) two or more words into one
            • the final compound becomes a single word with a single vibhatti
          • {{5833039149094952::vibhattyantaṁ padaṁ}} (if it has a case ending at its end it is a word) note: upasaggas have "non apparent" case endings suffixes, roots, stems...do not have vibhatti and are not part of speech
          • examples
            • {{6961285582034247::nīlaṃ vatthaṃ}} ⇒ {{5287727321568152::nīlavatthaṃ}} {{6961285582034247::nīlaṃ uppalaṃ}} ⇒ {{5287727321568152::nīluppalaṃ}} {{6961285582034247::paṇḍito puriso}} ⇒ {{5287727321568152::paṇḍitapuriso}}
          • general contruction of samāsa
            • both words lose their case endings
            • in their stem form they are compounded
            • a case ending is added to the final compound and, as it has one single vibhatti, it is one single word
          • 2 purposes / benefits of samāsa (not for exam)
            • ekapadattaṁ (the state of having one word)
            • ekavibhattittaṁ (the state of having one case ending)
          • the difference between sandhi and samāsa with an example
            • both sandhi and samāsa combine words, but in sandhi the case endings are not elided and the two words do not become one, while in samāsa both these grammatical functions happen
            • sandhi: lokassa + anto ⇒ lokassanto (2 words with their respective vibhattis)
            • samāsa: lokassa + anto ⇒ lokanto (one word with one single vibhatti) (pubbassaralopa sandhi has happened here as well)
            • note: sandhi can occur within samāsa
          • 6 types of samāsa #[[final exam 1st year]]
            • kammadhārayasamāsa
            • digusamāsa
            • tappurisasamāsa
            • dvandasamāsa
            • bahubbīhisamāsa
            • abyayībhāvasamāsa
            • mem aid: work (kamma) ⇒ 2 cows (digu) ⇒ cowboy (tappurisa) ⇒ 2 & 2 (dvanda) ⇒ many paddy (bahubbīhi) ⇒ unchanging (avyayībhāva)
        • kammadhārayasamāsa
          • the object (kamma) can hold (dhāraya) 2 things (not for exam)
            • kiriyaṁ (verb)
            • payojanaṁ (benefit)
          • meaning of kammadhārayasamāsa
            • the compound that holds two names for the same object of reference
          • kammadhāraya samāsa has 2 main features
            • the words are tulyādhikaraṇa pada (words in apposition: they refer to the same thing)
            • the meaning of the 2nd word is more prominent
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • tulya [√tul + ya]↔adj. equal; similar; of same kind; lit. balancing
              • tulyādhikaraṇa [tulya + adhikaraṇa]↔adj. (gram) having the same location
          • examples of kammadhāraya samāsa
            • {{11450326116538534::paṇḍito puriso}} ⇒ {{1006199841224682::paṇḍitapuriso}} (wise man) {{11450326116538534::setaṃ chattaṃ}} ⇒ {{1006199841224682::seta}}{{1006199841224682::c}}{{1006199841224682::chattaṃ }}(white parasol) {{11450326116538534::rattaṃ candanaṃ}} ⇒ {{1006199841224682::rattacandanaṃ }}(red sandalwood) {{11450326116538534::suvaco sisso}} ⇒ {{1006199841224682::suvacasisso }}(obedient student) {{11450326116538534::kāruṇiko samaṇo}} ⇒ {{1006199841224682::kāruṇikasamaṇo }}(compassionate monk) {{11450326116538534::ucco rukkho}} ⇒ {{1006199841224682::uccarukkho }}(high tree) {{11450326116538534::thūlo brāhmaṇo}} ⇒ {{1006199841224682::thūlabrāhmaṇo }}(fat brahmin) {{11450326116538534::bhinnaṃ sīlaṃ}} ⇒ {{1006199841224682::bhinnasīlaṃ }}(broken sīla)
              • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
                • rattaṁ [√raj + ta] (nt.)↔day; night; 2.1 pp. dyed; coloured; 2.2 adj. red; crimson; 2.3 nt. blood; 3.1 pp. (+loc) infatuated (with); enamoured (with); fond (of) ; 3.2 masc. (+loc) who is infatuated (with); who is enamoured (with); fond (of); (f.) night; rattā (f.) time; lit. night
          • construction of a kammadhārayasamāsa
            • both words are written in the nominative case (singular or plural): paṇḍito puriso
              • why? this is because only the nominative can stand alone without any other information needed, so whenever a word is written by itself in pāḷi it is written in nominative case
                • so why are some other samāsas written in other cases? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • the case ending of both words are elided: paṇdita purisa
            • the word are combined: paṇḍitapurisa
            • the final word is written in nominative case (but that word can be used in any case according to the context): paṇḍitapuriso
          • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
            • acchariya [accharā + iya]↔adj. wonderful; marvellous
            • paṇḍu↔pale-yellow, yellowish
            • kambala↔woolen cloth (s.w/ k)
        • digusamāsa
          • digusamāsas are {{5357809604958916::the }}{{5357809604958916::kammadhārayasamāsas}}{{5357809604958916:: that have a }}{{5357809604958916::cardinal number}}{{5357809604958916:: as the }}{{5357809604958916::first}}{{5357809604958916:: noun and are mostly kept in }}{{5357809604958916::neuter}}{{5357809604958916:: gender }}{{5357809604958916::singular}}{{5357809604958916:: form}}
            • 2 types of digusamāsa
              • samāhāra digusamāsa (neuter singular) (more frequent)
                • tayo lokā ⇒ tilokaṁ
              • asamāhāra digusamāsa (all genders and numbers)
                • catasso disā ⇒ catuddisā
                • eko dhammo ⇒ ekadhammo
              • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
                • samāhāra↔(m.) (gram) copulative compound with plural meaning and singular termination
                • asamāhāra↔adj. (gram) copulative compound with plural meaning and plural termination
            • 3 features of digusamāsa
              • the two nouns are in apposition (tulyādhikaraṇa)
              • the first is an adjective of the second
              • of the final compound noun, the meaning of the last morpheme is more prominent over the other
              • the first word is a cardinal number
              • the final compound is written in neuter singular (if samāhāra: tilokaṁ) or any gender and number (if asamāhāra: catuddisā)
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • digu (m.) [di + go + u]↔(gram) numerical (compound); lit. two cows
              • samāsati [saṃ + √ās + a + ti] pr.↔(+instr) associates (with); keeps close company (with); lit. sits together
              • kammadhāraya (m.)↔(gram) adjectival compound; appositional compound; lit. bearing the object
              • dhāraya (adj.) [√dhar + *aya + a]↔(+acc) bearing; holding; supporting
              • veneyya [vi + √nī + *eyya]↔ptp. instructible; teachable; educatable; lit. to be taught
          • examples:
            • {{35561654279294763::tayo lokā}} ⇒ {{5357809604958916::tilokaṁ}} {{35561654279294763::tīṇi lakkhaṇāni}} ⇒ {{5357809604958916::tilakkhaṇaṃ}} {{35561654279294763::catasso disā}} ⇒ {{5357809604958916::catuddisaṃ}} {{35561654279294763::cha āyatanāni}} ⇒ {{5357809604958916::saḷāyatanaṃ}} (cha ⇒ sa and ḷ is inserted) {{35561654279294763::dve rattiyo}} ⇒ {{5357809604958916::dvirattaṃ}} (the ending vowel i changes into a) {{35561654279294763::tayo daṇḍā}} ⇒ {{5357809604958916::tidaṇḍaṃ}}
          • mahanta in samāsa
            • the noun mahanta (which belongs to the gacchantādigaṇa) changes into {{14598626938955706::mahā}} mahanto puriso ⇒ {{14598626938955706::mahāpuriso}} mahanto muni ⇒ {{14598626938955706::mahāmuni}} and if the second noun begins with a double consonant {{14598626938955706::the ending }}{{14598626938955706::ā}}{{14598626938955706:: of the word }}{{14598626938955706::mahā}}{{14598626938955706:: is shortened}} mahantaṃ phalaṃ ⇒ {{14598626938955706::mahapphalaṃ}} mahantaṃ bhayaṃ ⇒ {{14598626938955706::mahabbhayaṃ}}
          • construction of a digusamāsa
            • both words are written in nominative case: tayo lokā
            • the case endings are elided: ti loka
            • the words are combined: tiloka
            • the final compound is written in neuter singular if samāhāradigu: tilokaṁ; or in any gender and number if asamāhāradigu: catuddisā
          • 18.2 exercise
            • 1).Write down the features which makes digu samāsa different from kammadhāraya samāsa.
              • The difference lies in the fact that digusamāsa has a cardinal number as the first noun and the final compound is written in neuter singular
            • 2).What is the gender and number in which digu samāsa words are written often?
              • Digusamāsas are most often written in neuter gender singular form
            • 3).Categorize the kammadhāraya and digu samāsa words in the following sentences and dissect them.
              • i.Bhagavā sukhumañāṇena tilokaṃ viditvā veneyyasattānaṃ dhammaṃ desesi.
                • sukhumañāṇena = sukhumena ñāṇena (kammadhārayasamāsa)
                • tilokaṁ = tayo lokā (digusamāsa)
                • veneyyasattānaṁ = veneyyānaṁ sattānaṁ (kammadhārayasamāsa)
                • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
                  • veneyyasatta (m.)↔instructible being
              • ii.Sāriputtatthero upāsakassa dasasīlaṃ adāsi.
                • sāriputtatthero = sāriputto thero (kammadhārayasamāsa)
                • dasasīlaṁ = dasa sīlāni (digusamāsa)
            • 4). Combine the following words in terms of samāsa and write them in their nominative case.
              • aṭṭha sīlāni ⇒ aṭṭhasīlaṁ
              • mahanto satto ⇒ mahāsatto
              • pahīnā kilesā ⇒ pahīnakilesā
              • nava sattāvāsā ⇒ navasattāvāsaṁ
              • satta ahāni ⇒ sattāhaṁ
              • pañca sikkhāpadāni ⇒ pañcasikkhāpadaṁ
        • tappurisasamāsa
          • tappurisa samāsa is
            • the resultant noun from the act of compounding two words with different vibhattis
            • in which the first word is in any of the cases other than nominative case
            • and the second word is prominent in meaning
            • each noun refers to a different object, hence they are not tulyādhikaraṇa but bhinnādhikaraṇa
            • it is of 6 kinds as dutiyā-, tatiyā-, catutthī-, pañcamī-, chaṭṭhī- and sattamī-tappurisa samāsa
            • example: sukhaṃ (acc.) patto (nom.) ⇒ sukha + patta ⇒ sukhappatta (one who has attained happiness)
          • 6 types of tappurisa samāsa, according to the nāmavibhatti of the first word, with an example
            • dutiyā tappurisa samāsa: buddhaṁ gato ⇒ buddha gata ⇒ buddhagato (gone to the Buddha)
              • {{12783491510803624::buddhaṁ gato}} ⇒ {{4189980701411524::buddhagato}} (gone to the Buddha) {{12783491510803624::dukkhaṃ patto}} ⇒ {{4189980701411524::dukkhappatto}} (the person who fell into suffering) {{12783491510803624::bhūmiṃ gato}} ⇒ {{4189980701411524::bhūmigato}} (the thing or being that has gone into the earth) {{12783491510803624::nirodhaṃ samāpanno}} ⇒ {{4189980701411524::nirodhasamāpanno}} (one who has entered the attainment of cessation)
            • tatiyā tappurisa samāsa: buddhena bhāsito ⇒ buddha bhāsita ⇒ buddhabhāsito (spoken by the Buddha)
              • {{21036381771796075::buddhena bhāsito}} ⇒ {{49666399088847846::buddhabhāsito}} (doctrine or teaching expounded by the Buddha) {{21036381771796075::sīlena sampanno}} ⇒ {{49666399088847846::sīlasampanno}} (one who is endowed with virtue) {{21036381771796075::ñāṇena sampayutto}} ⇒ {{49666399088847846::ñāṇasampayutto}} (mentality that is connected with wisdom)
            • catutthī tappurisa samāsa: buddhassa deyyaṃ ⇒ buddhadeyyaṃ (offerings to the Buddha)
              • {{8786783673424827::buddhassa deyyaṃ}} ⇒ {{7970843429653556::buddhadeyyaṃ}} (thing that should be given to the Buddha) {{8786783673424827::kaṭhinassa dussaṃ}} ⇒ {{7970843429653556::kaṭhinadussaṃ}} (cloth for the kaṭhina) {{8786783673424827::yāguyā taṇḍulā}} ⇒ {{7970843429653556::yāgutaṇḍulā}} (rice for gruel)
            • pañcamī tappurisa samāsa: buddhā cuto ⇒ buddha cuta ⇒ buddhacuto (fell from the Buddha)
              • {{3608994792130633::methunā apeto}} ⇒ {{28903065116455684::methunāpeto}} (one who has departed (abstained) from sex) {{3608994792130633::nagarā niggato}} ⇒ {{28903065116455684::nagaraniggato}} (one who has left the city) {{3608994792130633::sāsanā cuto}} ⇒ {{28903065116455684::sāsanacuto}} (one who has fallen from the Sāsana)
            • chaṭṭhī tappurisa samāsa: buddhassa sāvako ⇒ buddhasāvako (disciple of the Buddha)
              • {{9895163365655246::rañño putto}} ⇒ {{8334812485372394::rājaputto}} (son of the King) {{9895163365655246::buddhassa sāvako}} ⇒ {{8334812485372394::buddhasāvako}} (disciple of the Buddha) {{9895163365655246::rukkhassa mūlaṃ}} ⇒ {{8334812485372394::rukkhamūlaṃ}} (root of the tree)
            • sattamī tappurisa samāsa: buddhe rato ⇒ buddharato (delighted with the Buddha)
              • {{40970073639800275::rūpe saññā}} ⇒ {{644593305638508::rūpasaññā}} (perception on (regarding) rūpa / matter or visible object) {{40970073639800275::dhamme rato}} ⇒ {{644593305638508::dhammarato}} (one who is delighted in Dhamma) {{40970073639800275::bhavantare kataṃ}} ⇒ {{644593305638508::bhavantarakataṃ}} (something that was done in a different life)
          • features which make tappurisa samāsa different from kammadhāraya samāsa
            • different vibhatti: the words have different vibhattis (buddhaṁ gato)
            • bhinnādhikaraṇa: words are not tulyādhikaraṇa (in apposition), they each refer to a different thing (bhinnādhikaraṇa)
            • not nominative: the first word is in a case other than the nominative (6 possibilities)
          • 2 types of visesana (adjective)
            • tulyādhikaraṇa visesana / samānādhikaraṇa visesana
              • same gender, case and number
              • refer to the same thing
            • bhinnādhikaraṇa visesana: sukhaṁ patto - sukhaṁ is a bhinnādhikaraṇa visesana of patto
              • different gender, number, case
              • refer to different things
              • why is sukhaṁ an adjective of patto? because it modifies the noun patta, specifying what type of patta; it is not an adverb because they only modify real verbs: sukhaṁ supati
              • mayhaṁ gehaṁ: they refer to different objects
          • exercise
            • 1). What is the most prominent feature which differatiates tappurisa samāsa from kammadhāraya and digu samāsa.
              • The most prominent feature which differentiates them is that the nouns involved are bhinnādhikaraṇa
            • 2). Dissect the following t hoappurisa samāsa words found in the reading lesson and name the type of tappurisa samāsa under which they were combined. #homeworks
              • i. rukkhamūlaṃ = rukkhassa mūlaṁ
              • ii. nagaraniggato = nagarā niggato
              • iii. nirodhasamāpanno = nirodhaṁ samāpanno
              • iv. buddhabhāsito = buddhena bhāsito
              • v. rūpasaññā = rūpe saññā
              • vi. buddhadeyyaṃ = buddhassa deyyaṁ
            • 3). Select samāsa words from the following sentences and name group they belong to, i.e., kammadhāraya, digu or tappurisa.
            • i. Ānandatthero bhikkhūnaṃ saṃsāradukkhaṃ kathesi.
              • Ānandatthero (kammaddhāraya) saṁsāradukkhaṁ (tappurisa)
            • ii. Abhiññappatto mahāsāvako tilokaṃ olokesi.
              • abhiññappatto (tappurisa)
              • mahāsāvako (kammadhāraya)
              • tilokaṁ (digu)
        • dvandasamāsa
          • 3 characteristics of dvandasamāsa
            • independent: nouns are not visesana and visesya, they are independent nouns
            • ca: the indeclinable “ca” collects the two nouns
            • equal prominence: in the final compound both words are equally prominent in their meaning
          • construction
            • (sāriputto ca moggallāno ca)
            • elision of case endings and 'ca' (sāriputta moggallāna)
            • compounding (sāriputtamoggallāna)
            • declension:
              • if samāhāradvanda it is declined in the neuter gender, nominative case, singular (cakkhusotaṁ)
              • if itarītarayogadvanda, in the gender of the last noun, nominative case, plural (sometimes singular) (sāriputtamoggallānā)
            • usage: the newly formed word can be then used in any case according to context
          • samuccaya
            • the grammatical act of collecting two or more nouns / verbs together, normally performed by the indeclinable 'ca': sāriputto ca moggallāno ca
          • samuccayattha
            • the meaning of the indeclinable “ca”; literally this means that the indeclinable “ca” performs the act of collecting the two nouns
          • 2 types of dvandasamāsa
            • samāhāradvanda: declined in the neuter gender, nominative case, singular
              • {{08827942898988317::cakkhuñca sotañca}} ⇒ {{021964824289815166::cakkhusotaṃ }} {{08827942898988317::gītañca vāditañca}} ⇒ {{021964824289815166::gītavāditaṃ}} {{08827942898988317::hatthino ca assā ca}} ⇒ {{021964824289815166::hatthiassaṃ}}
            • itarītarayogadvanda (most common): declined in the nominative case, gender of the last noun, plural (sometimes singular)
              • {{7915471359143464::sāriputto ca moggallāno ca}} ⇒ {{04265527879008979::sāriputtamoggallānā}} {{7915471359143464::candimā ca sūriyā ca}} ⇒ {{04265527879008979::candimasūriyā}}
          • examples
            • {{03301991049718045::sāriputto ca moggallāno ca}} ⇒ {{8702764775362479::sāriputtamoggallānā}} {{03301991049718045::samaṇo ca brāhmaṇo ca}} ⇒ {{8702764775362479::samaṇabrāhmaṇā}} {{03301991049718045::cando ca sūriyo ca}} ⇒ {{8702764775362479::candasūriyā}} {{03301991049718045::brāhmaṇo ca gahapatiko ca}} ⇒ {{8702764775362479::brāhmaṇagahapatikā}} {{03301991049718045::mātā ca pitā ca}} ⇒ {{8702764775362479::mātāpitaro}}

              • v. ahinakulā (kammadhāraya)
          • exercise pg 9
            • 1). Name whether the following samāsa words are samāhāra dvanda or itarītarayoga dvanda.
              • i. ḍaṃsamakasaṃ (samāhāra)

        • bahubbīhisamāsa
          • main characteristics of bahubbīhisamāsa
            • aññapada: they are compounded in the meanings of the pronouns “{{39695965465452976::ya}}”, “{{39695965465452976::ta}}”, “{{39695965465452976::eta}}” and “{{39695965465452976::ima}}”, called {{08807171274529613::aññapada}}{{08807171274529613:: }}(the word that refers to what the compound refers to)
            • {{9854419301691595::aññapadattha}}: the final samāsa refers to the noun that is referred to by the aññapada
            • aññapadattha's gender and number: the gender and number of the final compound is the same as the aññapadattha's
            • example:
              • {{6392113992480484::āgatā samaṇā yaṃ}}{{6392113992480484:: }}{{6392113992480484::so}} {{8398184444548966::āgatasamaṇo }}{{8398184444548966::(saṅghārāmo) (the place where recluses have arrived is called “āgatasamaṇa”; that is the “saṅghārāma”)}}
              • though āgata and samaṇa are connected, the final word āgatasamaṇa, does not refer to recluses who have arrived but the place where they have arrived (saṅghārāma); thus, the two nouns āgata and samaṇa are compounded referring to the noun yaṁ which refers to the place saṅghārāma; the meaning of the final compound āgatasamaṇo is saṅghārāma
          • 7 types of bahubbīhi based on the nāmavibhatti of the aññapada #[[final exam 1st year]]
            • paṭhamā bahubbīhi (to be explained later)
            • dutiyā bahubbīhi
              • {{07659482907351456::āgatā samaṇā imanti}} {{8734812530915086::āgatasamaṇo (saṃghārāmo)}} {{07659482907351456::āruḷhā vāṇijā imanti}} {{8734812530915086::āruḷhavāṇijā (nāvā) }}
            • tatiyā bahubbīhi
              • {{43486072178904944::jitāni indriyāni yenāti}} {{6185287331590414::jitindriyo (samaṇo)}} {{43486072178904944::kataṃ kiccaṃ yenāti}} {{6185287331590414::katakicco (samaṇo)}}
            • catutthī bahubbīhi
              • {{30974531241212344::dinno suṅko yassāti}} {{777740859244938::dinnasuṅko (rājā) }} {{30974531241212344::upanītaṃ bhojanaṃ assāti}} {{777740859244938::upanītabhojano (samaṇo)}}
              • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
                • suṅka (m.)↔tax; toll; duty; customs
                • upanīta [upa + √nī + ta]↔adj. (+loc) led (into); brought (into); presented; lit. lead near; 2 pp. (+acc) (of a sacrifice) led (to); offered; presented; lit. lead near
            • pañcamī bahubbīhi
              • {{4544481058917993::niggatā janā asmāti}} {{5062727004199752::niggatajano (gāmo)}} {{4544481058917993::apetaṃ viññāṇaṃ asmāti}} {{5062727004199752::apetaviññāṇo (matakāyo)}}
            • chaṭṭhī bahubbīhi
              • {{911810463960715::chinnā hatthā assāti}} {{4362055353708487::chinnahattho (puriso)}} {{911810463960715::cha abhiññā assāti}} {{4362055353708487::chaḷabhiñño (khīṇāsavo)}}
            • sattamī bahubbīhi
              • {{8513244047282129::sampannāni sassāni yasminti}} {{7883495962815101::sampannasasso (janapado) }} {{8513244047282129::bahavo tāpasā etasminti}} {{7883495962815101::bahutāpaso (assamo) }}
              • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
                • sassaṁ (nt.)→corn; grain; crop; harvest
          • exercise
            • 1). Construct bahubbīhi samāsa words from the following sentences and give their meaning. Be aware of the gender and the number of the final noun.
              • i. {{6841164535424689::Vidito dhammo yena samaṇenāti}} {{9797008901020616::viditadhammo}}{{9797008901020616:: (the one by whom the dhamma was experienced)}}

              • ii. Tisso vijjā yassa khīṇāsavassāti tevijjo (?) (the one who possesses the three knowledges)
              • iii. Kataṃ pāpaṃ imehi puggalehīti katapāpo (the one who has done evil)
              • iv. Bahū rukkhā yasmiṃ vaneti bahurukkhaṁ (the one in which many trees are found)
            • 2). Chose bahubbīhi samāsa words from the below sentences and give a suitable definition sentence.
              • i. Katapuñño ubhayattha nandati.
                • kataṁ puññaṁ yenāti katapuñño
              • ii. Apetaviññāṇo kāyo niratthaṃva kaliṅgaraṃ
                • apetaṁ viññāṇaṁ yassāti apetaviññāṇo
          • note:
            • ariyaṁ ñāṇaṁ tassa so ariyañāṇo
            • the genitive case does not expect a verb
        • avyayībhāva / abyayībhāva samāsa
          • main characteristics
            • avyaya: a samāsa that involves the combination of nouns with indeclinables or prefixes (avyaya)
            • upasagganipātapubbaka (I): the meaning of the avyaya is more prominent (pubbaka) over the noun
            • upasagganipātapubbaka (II): the avyaya is placed before (pubbaka) the noun in the final compound
            • nt. nom.: the final compound is declined in neuter gender, nominative case, singular or plural
          • bhāva in avyayībhāva has 2 meanings (extra information)
            • makes the avyaya prominent (vibhāveti)
            • makes nouns avyaya: the final compound becomes avyaya
            • avyaya (non-changing) vibhāveti (makes something evident, apparent, visible): the samāsa which makes the avyaya evident
          • examples
            • nipāta: {{13630946607325467::pāsādassa anto}} ⇒ {{39822792692338305::antopāsādaṃ }}(inside the palace) {{13630946607325467::pāsādassa heṭṭhā}} ⇒ {{39822792692338305::heṭṭhāpāsādaṃ }}(below the palace) {{13630946607325467::bhattassa pacchā}} ⇒ {{39822792692338305::pacchābhattaṃ}} (after the mealtime) {{13630946607325467::bhattassa pure}} ⇒ {{39822792692338305::purebhattaṁ}} (before the mealtime) upasagga: {{13630946607325467::nagarassa samīpaṃ}} ⇒ {{39822792692338305::upanagaraṃ }}(proximity of the city) {{13630946607325467::gaṅgāya samīpaṃ}} ⇒ {{39822792692338305::upagaṅgaṃ}} (proximity of the river Ganges) {{13630946607325467::rathassa pacchā}} ⇒ {{39822792692338305::anurathaṃ}} (behind / after the vehicle)
              • note:
                • upasaggas are not found independently in sentences but always attached either to roots or nouns, therefore it is not possible to have a definition sentence as “nagarassa upa upanagaraṃ”; therefore, the definition sentence is made by using the word {{16441967910888522::samīpa }}which has a similar meaning to that of upa – proximity; these types of definitions that are done using different words to that of the word that is being defined are called {{16441967910888522::asapada viggaha}} #[[final exam 1st year]]
                • adjectives are not as prominent as the nouns they modify, so dussīla is not avyayībhāvasamāsa, but dubbhikkhā is, since the first du is an adjective as 'bad' while on the second it means 'scarcity'
          • exercise
            • 1). Write down the avyayībhāva samāsa words that are made by the following definition sentence and write their meanings as well.
              • i. {{49354526766693074::pāsādassa upari}} ⇒ {{45904532199935::uparipāsādaṁ}} (upper terrace of a palace)
              • ii. {{9716409001979558::kuṭṭassa tiro}} ⇒ {{44983543910673274::tirokuṭṭaṁ }}(outside the wall)
              • iii. {{4943601324952023::nagarassa bahi}} ⇒ {{03606551602492547::bahinagaraṁ}} (on the outskirts of the city)
              • iv. {{5470117830790286::Makasānaṃ abhāvo}} (The word abhāva is used for the prefix {{8510370283951421::ni}}) ⇒ {{8510370283951421::nimakasaṁ }}(the absence of mosquitoes)
              • v. {{30445315076909374::Vātassa pacchā}} (The word pacchā is used for the prefix {{9336105349324828::anu}}) ⇒ {{9336105349324828::anuvātaṁ}} (after the wind, windward)
        • note:
          • prominence of words in each samāsa #[[final exam 1st year]]
            • kammadhāraya: second word is more prominent
            • digu: second
            • tappurisa: second
            • dvanda: both have equal prominence
            • bahubbīhi: aññapadattha
            • avyayībhāva: first (abyaya)
          • apart from kammadhāraya and avyayībhāva samāsas, the other samāsa's names themselves are examples of their respective samāsa types: {{45895093857308034::dve gāvo}} ⇒ {{4593874717260322::digu}} (two cows) {{45895093857308034::tassa puriso}} ⇒ {{4593874717260322::tappurisa}} (his man) {{45895093857308034::dve ca dve ca}} ⇒ {{4593874717260322::dvanda}} (two and two) {{45895093857308034::bahu vīhi assa}} ⇒ {{4593874717260322::bahubbīhi}} (the one who has a lot of paddy)
      • Lesson 24
        • 24.1. reading
          • Sāriputtattheravatthu - VI So sotāpanno hutvā uparivisese (higher distinction) appavattante “Bhavissati ettha kāraṇa”nti sallakkhetvā theraṃ āha – “Bhante, mā upari dhammadesanaṃ vaḍḍhayittha (mā + ajjatanī), ettakameva hotu, kuhiṃ amhākaṃ satthā vasatī”ti? “Veḷuvane, āvuso”ti. “Tena hi, bhante, tumhe purato yātha (√yā, pañcamī), mayhaṃ eko sahāyako atthi, amhehi ca aññamaññaṃ katikā katā ‘Amhesu yo amataṃ paṭhamaṃ adhigacchati, so itarassa ārocetū’ti. Ahaṃ taṃ paṭiññaṃ mocetvā sahāyakaṃ gahetvā tumhākaṃ gatamaggeneva satthu santikaṃ āgamissāmī”ti pañcapatiṭṭhitena therassa pādesu nipatitvā tikkhattuṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā theraṃ uyyojetvā paribbājakārāmābhimukho agamāsi. Atha kho kolitaparibbājako taṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ disvā, “Ajja mayhaṃ sahāyakassa mukhavaṇṇo na aññadivasesu viya, addhā tena amataṃ adhigataṃ bhavissatī (it must be)”ti amatādhigamaṃ pucchi. Sopissa “Āmāvuso, amataṃ adhigata”nti paṭijānitvā tameva gāthaṃ abhāsi. Gāthāpariyosāne kolito sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhahitvā āha – “Kuhiṃ kira, samma, amhākaṃ satthā vasatī”ti? “Veḷuvane kira, samma, evaṃ no ācariyena assajittherena kathita”nti. “Tena hi, samma, āyāma ([ā + √yā + āma]), satthāraṃ passissāmā”ti

        • Lesson 24 - exercises
          • translation
            • The story of the elder Sāriputta - VI After becoming a stream-enterer, when the higher distinctions were not taking place, he reflected, "There must be a reason here (lit. There will be a reason here)", and said to the elder, "Venerable sir, do not expand the teaching further, let it be only this much. Where is our teacher residing?", "In the Bamboo Grove, friend", "If it is so, venerable sir, may you go ahead. There is one friend of mine, and a mutual agreement was done by us in this way, "Whoever of us attains the deathlessness first, let him inform the other". After having fulfilled that promise and picked up my friend, I will come to the Teacher by the same road taken by you". Having fallen at the feet of the elder with the fivefold prostration, circumumbulated him thrice and seen the elder off (lit. sent the elder off), he went facing towards the monastery of the ascetics. Then, the ascetic Kolita, after seeing him coming from afar (thought), "Today my friend's facial expression is not like in previous days, certainly the deathlessness must have been attained by him", and asked about it (the attainment of the deathlessness). And he (Upatissa) acknowledged it to him, "Yes, friend, the deathless state has been attained", and uttered that very same verse. When the verse was completed, Kolita said, after having established himself in the fruition of stream-entry, "Where is it said, friend, that our Teacher dwells?", "It is said, friend, that in the Bamboo Grove. It was said in this way by our teacher the elder Assaji", "If it is so, friend, let us go, we shall see the Teacher!".
      • Lesson 25
        • 25.1. reading
          • Sāriputtattheravattthu - VII Sāriputtatthero ca nāmesa (nāma eso [pubbassaralopa + lopāgamasandhi]) sadāpi ācariyapūjakova, tasmā sahāyaṃ evamāha – “Samma, amhehi adhigataṃ amataṃ amhākaṃ ācariyassa sañcayaparibbājakassāpi kathessāma, bujjhamāno paṭivijjhissati, appaṭivijjhanto amhākaṃ saddahitvā satthu santikaṃ gamissatī”ti. Tato dvepi janā sañcayassa santikaṃ agamaṃsu. Sañcayo te disvāva – “Kiṃ, tātā, koci vo (ins.pl.) amatamaggadesako laddho”ti pucchi. “Āma, ācariya, laddho, buddho loke uppanno, dhammo loke uppanno, saṅgho loke uppanno, tumhe tucche asāre vicaratha, tasmā etha, satthu santikaṃ gamissāmā”ti. “Gacchatha tumhe, nāhaṃ sakkhissāmī”ti. “Kiṃ kāraṇā'ti? “Ahaṃ mahājanassa ācariyo hutvā vicariṃ, na sakkhissāmahaṃ antevāsikavāsaṃ vasitu”nti. “Mā evaṃ karittha, ācariya, loke buddhassa uppannakālato paṭṭhāya mahājano gandhamālādihattho gantvā tameva pūjessati, mayampi tattheva gamissāma. Tumhe kiṃ karissathā”ti? “Tātā, kiṃ nu kho imasmiṃ loke dandhā bahū, udāhu paṇḍitā”ti. “Dandhā, ācariya, bahū, paṇḍitā ca nāma katipayā eva hontī”ti. “Tena hi, tātā, paṇḍitā paṇḍitassa samaṇassa gotamassa santikaṃ gamissanti, dandhā dandhassa mama santikaṃ āgamissanti, gacchatha tumhe, nāhaṃ gamissāmī”ti. Atha kho te attano antevāsikehi aḍḍhateyyehi paribbājakasatehi saddhiṃ veḷuvanaṃ agamaṃsu. Satthā catuparisamajjhe nisinno dhammaṃ desento te dūratova disvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “Ete, bhikkhave, dve sahāyakā āgacchanti kolito ca upatisso ca, etaṃ me sāvakayugaṃ bhavissati aggaṃ bhaddayuga”nti. Te satthāraṃ vanditvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, nisīditvā ca pana bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “Labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada”nti. “Etha, bhikkhavo”ti bhagavā avoca – “Svākkhāto dhammo, caratha brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā (dat.)”ti. Sabbepi iddhimayapattacīvaradharā saṭṭhivassikattherā viya ahesuṃ.
