      • 2. Declensions of pronouns ‘ta’ and ‘eta’ (Chapter III) (Masculine, Neuter and Femine)
        • declension of the pronoun ‘ta’
          • masculine declension
            • Nom. so / te, ne
            • Acc. taṃ, naṃ / te, ne
            • Ins. tena, nena / tehi, tebhi, nehi, nebhi
            • Dat/gen. tassa, nassa, assa / tesaṃ, tesānaṃ, nesaṃ, nesānaṃ
            • Abl. tasmā, nasmā, asmā, tamhā, namhā / tehi, tebhi, nehi, nebhi
            • Loc. tasmiṃ, nasmiṁ, asmiṃ, tamhi, namhi / tesu, nesu
            • memory aid:
              • 1 - t ⇒ n
              • 2 - sa, sma, smiṁ: ta ⇒ a
          • neuter declension↓
            • Nom. taṁ, naṃ / tāni, nāni
            • Acc. taṃ, naṃ / tāni, nāni
            • (same as masculine)
            • Ins. tena, nena / tehi, tebhi, nehi, nebhi
            • Dat/gen. tassa, nassa, assa / tesaṃ, tesānaṃ, nesaṃ, nesānaṃ
            • Abl. tasmā, nasmā, asmā, tamhā, namhā / tehi, tebhi, nehi, nebhi
            • Loc. tasmiṃ, nasmiṁ, asmiṃ, tamhi, namhi / tesu, nesu
            • memory aid:
              • 1 - t ⇒ n
              • 2 - sa, smā, smiṁ: ta ⇒ a
          • feminine declension
            • Nom. sā / tā, tāyo, nā, nāyo
            • Acc. taṃ, naṃ / tā, tāyo, nā, nāyo
            • Ins. / Abl. tāya, nāya / tāhi, tābhi, nāhi, nābhi
            • Dat/gen. tāya, nāya - tassā, nassā, assā, tissā - tassāya, nassāya, assāya, tissāya / tāsaṃ, tāsānaṃ, nāsaṃ, nāsānaṃ
            • Loc. tāyaṃ, nāyaṃ, tassaṃ, nassaṃ, assaṃ, tissaṃ / tāsu, nāsu
            • memory aid:
              • 1 - t ⇒ n
              • 2 - sa, smā, smiṁ, sā, saṁ: ta ⇒ a
              • 3 - dat. gen.: ending in sā: add ya
              • 4 - ta ⇒ ti, sa ⇒ saṁ
        • Declension of the noun "eta" (this) which is declined in all three genders.
          • "eta" masculine declension (sabbanāmagaṇa)
            • Nom. eso / ete
            • Acc etaṃ / ete
            • Ins. etena / etehi, etebhi
            • Dat/gen. etassa / etesaṃ, etesānaṃ
            • Abl. etasmā, etamhā / etehi, etebhi
            • Loc. etasmiṃ, etamhi / etesu
          • "eta" neuter declension (sabbanāmagaṇa)
            • Nom. etaṃ / etāni
            • Acc etaṃ / etāni
            • The remaining cases are similar to that of the masculine declension:
            • Ins. etena / etehi, etebhi
            • Dat/gen. etassa / etesaṃ, etesānaṃ
            • Abl. etasmā, etamhā / etehi, etebhi
            • Loc. etasmiṃ, etamhi / etesu
          • "eta" feminine declension (sabbanāmagaṇa)
            • Nom. esā / etā, etāyo
            • Acc. etaṃ / etā, etāyo
            • Ins. / Abl. etāya / etāhi, etābhi
            • Dat/gen. etāya, etissā, etissāya / etāsaṃ, etāsānaṃ
            • Loc. etāyaṃ, etissaṃ / etāsu

      • 5. Samāsa (Only from samāsa revision lesson)
        • i. Describe kammadhāraya samāsa with an example.
          • the compound that holds two names for the same object of reference
          • kammadhāraya samāsa has 2 main features
            • the words are tulyādhikaraṇa pada (words in apposition: they refer to the same thing)
            • the meaning of the 2nd word is more prominent
          • paṇdito puriso ⇒ paṇḍitapuriso (wise man)
        • ii. Describe digu samāsa with an example.
          • note: it is the same as kammadhārayasamāsa but the has a cardinal number as the first noun and is written in neuter singular (if samāhāradigu) or in any gender and number (if asamāhāradigu)
          • tayo lokā ⇒ tilokaṁ
          • catasso disā ⇒ catuddisā
        • iii. Describe tappurisa samāsa with an example.
          • tappurisa samāsa is
            • the resultant noun from the act of compounding two words with different vibhattis
            • in which the first word is in any of the cases other than nominative case
            • and the second word is prominent in meaning
            • each noun refers to a different object, hence they are not tulyādhikaraṇa but bhinnādhikaraṇa
            • it is of 6 kinds as dutiyā-, tatiyā-, catutthī-, pañcamī-, chaṭṭhī- and sattamī-tappurisa samāsa
            • example: sukhaṃ (acc.) patto (nom.) ⇒ sukha + patta ⇒ sukhappatta (one who has attained happiness)
        • iv. Describe dvanda samāsa with an example.
          • 3 characteristics of dvandasamāsa
            • independent: nouns are not visesana and visesya, they are independent nouns
            • ca: the indeclinable “ca” collects the two nouns
            • equal prominence: in the final compound both words are equally prominent in their meaning
            • declension:
              • if samāhāradvanda it is declined in the neuter gender, nominative case, singular (cakkhusotaṁ)
              • if itarītarayogadvanda, in the gender of the last noun, nominative case, plural (sometimes singular) (sāriputtamoggallānā)
              • samuccaya
                • the grammatical act of collecting two or more nouns / verbs together, normally performed by the indeclinable 'ca': sāriputto ca moggallāno ca
              • samuccayattha
                • the meaning of the indeclinable “ca”; literally this means that the indeclinable “ca” performs the act of collecting the two nouns
            • example:
              • samāhāradvanda
                • cakkhuñca sotañca ⇒ cakkhusotaṁ
              • itarītarayogadvanda
                • sāriputto ca moggallāno ca ⇒ sāriputtamoggallānā
        • v. Describe bahubbīhi samāsa with an example.
          • main characteristics of bahubbīhisamāsa
            • aññapada: they are compounded in the meanings of the pronouns "ya”, “ta”, “eta” and “ima”, called aññapada
            • aññapadattha: the final samāsa refers to the noun that is referred to by the aññapada
            • aññapadattha's gender and number: the gender and number of the final compound is the same as the aññapadattha's
            • example:
              • āgatā samaṇā yaṃ so āgatasamaṇo (saṅghārāmo) (the place where recluses have arrived is called “āgatasamaṇa”; that is the “saṅghārāma”)
        • vi. Describe avyayībhāva samāsa with an example.
          • main characteristics
            • avyaya: a samāsa that involves the combination of nouns with indeclinables or prefixes (avyaya)
            • upasagganipātapubbaka (I): the meaning of the avyaya is more prominent (pubbaka) over the noun
            • upasagganipātapubbaka (II): the avyaya is placed before (pubbaka) the noun in the final compound
            • nt. nom.: the final compound is declined in neuter gender, nominative case, singular or plural
            • example
              • pāsādassa heṭṭhā ⇒ heṭṭhāpāsādaṁ (below the palace)
              • nagarassa samīpaṁ ⇒ upanagaraṁ (proximity of the city)
        • vii. Name the type of samāsa under which the following samāsa nouns are formed.
          • Catuddisaṃ
            • digusamāsa (samāhāradigu)
            • catasso disā catuddisaṁ (four directions)
          • sāriputtamoggallānā
            • dvandasamāsa (itarītarayogadvanda)
            • sāriputto ca moggallāno ca
          • methunāpeto
            • tappurisasamāsa (pañcamītappurisasamāsa)
            • methunā apeto methunāpeto (one who has departed from sex)
          • chinnahattho puriso
            • bahubbīhisamāsa (chaṭṭhībahubbīhi)
            • chinnā hatthā assāti chinnahattho (whose hands have been cut off)
          • upanagaraṃ
            • avyayībhāvasamāsa
            • nagarassa samīpaṁ upanagaraṁ (the vicinity of the city)
      • 6. Taddhita
        • i. Describe apacca taddhita with an example.
          • nouns formed by adding one of the 4 suffixes with the meaning 'the offspring of' to it vasudevassa apaccaṁ vāsudevo (vasudeva + ṇa)
          • ṇa,
          • ṇāyana / ṇana,
          • ṇeyya,
          • ṇera
        • ii. Describe aneka&ha taddhita with an example.
          • what is anekatthataddhita? secondary derivatives constructed by adding an anekatthataddhitapaccaya which has several meanings to a noun
          • visesataddhita
          • visesena pāpo (evil one) — pāpataro, pāpatamo (one who is more / the most evil) (pāpa + tara)
          • ṇa
          • ṇeyya
          • ṇika
          • ima
          • iya
          • ya
          • maya
          • tara
          • tama
        • iii. Describe assa&hi taddhita with an example.
          • assatthitaddhita are secondary derivatives that are constructed by adding to nouns suffixes that denote the sense of taṃ assa atthi (he possesses / has it) as well as occasional additional meanings such as 'abundance' (kesavo), or 'disgrace' and the most common of them are -vantu, -mantu, -ī and -ṇa
          • guṇa + vantu ⇒ guṇavā
          • guṇo assa atthīti guṇavā (one who has wholesome virtues)
          • -vantu: used for any stems ending in 'a' or 'ā'
          • -mantu: used for stems endings in 'i', 'ī', 'u', 'ū' and 'o' (there are no stems ending in 'e')
          • -imantu
          • -vī
          • -va
          • -sī
          • -sa
          • -āla
          • -ila
          • -ika and -ī
          • -ra
          • -ṇa
        • iv. Describe saṅkhyā taddhita with an example.
          • saṅkhyātaddhita are secondary derivatives constructed by adding to a noun suffixes that are related to numbers a group of them are pūraṇataddhitas which are used to form ordinal numbers pūraṇataddhitapaccaya: tiya tha ma ṭha ī (11-18) dvinnaṁ pūraṇo dutiyo (second) (dvi + tiya)
        • v. Describe avyaya taddhita with an example.
          • abyayataddhitas are secondary derivatives constructed by adding to a noun suffixes that make it act as indeclinables (abyaya) dvīsu vāresu dvikkhattuṁ (two times) (dvi + kkhattuṁ)
          • some of them are vibhattipaccayantapada which are abyayataddhitas that end with vibhattipaccayas which are suffixes that express the meaning of nominal cases such as -to
          • gāmato (from the village)
          • abyayataddhitapaccayas:
            • kkhattuṁ
            • dhā
            • thā
            • thaṁ
            • (vi.pa.pada)
            • to
            • tra
            • tha
            • dhi
            • hiṁ
            • haṁ
            • va
            • dha
            • dā
            • dācanaṁ
            • dāni
        • vi. Describe bhāva taddhita with an example.
          • taddhita nouns that are made with suffixes with the meaning "its nature (bhāva)"
          • bhāvataddhitapaccayas:
            • tā
            • tta
            • ttana
            • ṇa
            • ṇeyya
            • ṇya
          • sabbaññuno bhāvo sabbaññutā (the nature of omniscience)
        • vii. Describe sva&ha taddhita with an example.
          • svatthataddhitas (sa +attha), also called sakatthataddhitas (saka + attha) are secondary derivatives do not convey any new meaning, but simply the same meaning of the noun to which the suffix was added
          • -tā
          • -ma
          • -maya
          • -ṇya
          • -ṇika
          • devoyeva devatā (deity) (deva + tā)
        • viii. Dissect the noun and suffix of the following taddhita nouns and write the meanings eloborating the meaning of the suffix.
          • i. Bāladevo
            • baladevassa apaccaṁ bāladevo (Baladeva's offspring)
            • baladeva + ṇa (apaccataddhita)
          • kāyikaṃ
            • kāyena kataṁ kāyikaṁ (done with the body)
            • kāya + ṇika (anekatthataddhita - kataṁtaddhita)
          • nāgaro
            • nagare jāto nāgaro (something which arose / someone who was born in the city)
            • nagara + ṇa (anekatthataddhita - jātataddhita)
          • dakkhiṇeyyo
            • dakkhiṇaṁ arahatīti dakkhiṇeyyo (one who deserves the offering)
            • dakkhiṇa + ṇeyya (anekatthataddhita - arahatitaddhita)
          • pacchimo
            • pacchā jāto pacchimo (that which was born / arose later)
            • pacchā + ima (anekatthataddhita - jātataddhita)
          • thaññaṃ
            • thanato jātaṁ thaññaṁ (that which arose from the breast)
            • thana + ya (anekatthataddhita - jātataddhita)
          • rajatamayaṃ
            • rajatena pakataṁ rajatamayaṁ (that which is made of silver)
            • rajata + maya (anekatthataddhita - pakatataddhita)
          • pāpataro
            • visesena pāpo pāpataro (one who is more evil)
            • pāpa + tara (anekatthataddhita - visesataddhita)
          • guṇavā
            • guṇo assa atthīti guṇavā (one who has virtues)
            • guṇa + vantu (assatthitaddhita)
          • tatiyo
            • tiṇṇaṁ pūraṇo tatiyo (the third)
            • ti + tiya ⇒ ta + tiya ⇒ tatiya (saṅkhyātaddhita - pūraṇataddhita)
          • dvidhā
            • dvīhi vibhāgehi dvidhā (in two divisions / ways)
            • dvi + dhā (abyayataddhita)
          • ālasyaṃ
            • alasassa bhāvo ālasyaṁ (laziness)
            • alasa + ṇya (bhāvataddhita)
          • devatā
            • devoyeva devatā (deity)
            • deva + tā (sakatthataddhita)
      • 7. Kitaka
        • i. What is ‘kitaka nāma’? Describe with an example.
          • kitaka nāma are the nouns formed by {{2285640549629302::adding a kitaka suffix to a root (pac + anta ⇒ pacanta ⇒ one who is cooking)}}
        • ii. What are ‘Sādhana’ Describe with an example.
          • sādhana are the meanings bore by kitaka suffixes; meanings that complete an action (kiriyaṁ sādheti); they can be of 7 types
            • (1). Kattu sādhana (main one): har + māna ⇒ haramāna (one who is carrying)
            • (2). Kamma sādhana: the object completes the action in many cases
            • (3). Karaṇa sādhana: for many actions there must be an instrument
            • (4). Sampadāna sādhana: for many actions there must be a receiver
            • (5). Apādāna sādhana
            • (6). Adhikaraṇa sādhana
            • (7). Bhāva sādhana: merely the meaning of the action itself (bhāva nāma kiriyā)
        • iii. Dissect the root and suffix of the following kitaka nouns and write the meanings eloborating the meaning of the suffix
          • {{8107647500330273::√lubh + ṇa}} = {{19722655637722974::lobho – the reality that attaches (kattusādhana) }}
          • {{6414265070895344::√kar + tu}} = {{8876015249835867::kattā – one who does; subject / agent of a action (kattusādhana) }}
          • {{9355657797020283::√sās + ratthu}} = {{29808046884130546::satthā – one who admonishes; teacher (kattusādhana)}}
          • {{19871786901269783::√dhar + ramma}} = {{08876850032696892::dha + amma ⇒ dhammo (that which holds others without letting them fall into woeful states) (kattusādhana)}}
          • {{4448445825691174::vi + √ñā + yu}} = {{7329474126591848::vi + ñā + ana ⇒ viññāṇaṃ (the reality which knows) (kattusādhana)}}
          • {{5703417481373991::√ji + ina}} = {{9216907844407078::jino (one who defeated the akusalas) (kattusādhana)}}
          • {{8851523193529705::ā + √gam + tuka}} = {{7141043304180246::āgantuko (one who comes / visitor) (kattusādhana) }}
          • {{5395446431772941::√gam + anta}} = {{6341658750338055::gacchanto (one who is going)(kattusādhana)}}
          • {{7260204262620225::√sam + tha}} = {{5583826110033907::samath}}{{5583826110033907::o (the reality that appeases defilements) (kattusādhana)}}
          • {{7662589138634839::√kar + }}{{7662589138634839::tvā}} = {{9923649786002497::ka}}{{9923649786002497::tvā}}{{9923649786002497:: (having done) (kattu and bhāva sādhana as gerunds (pubba kiriyā))}}
          • {{7990000989378885::√pac + tabba}} - {{38205790255975747::pacitabbo – thing that is cooked (kammasādhana) }}
          • {{012583136881556767::√kar + ta}} = {{250566981434748::kata}}{{250566981434748::ṃ - thing that was done (kamma sādhana) }}
          • {{056243836174936446::√pad + ṇa}} = {{47843800962510263::pādo}}{{47843800962510263:: – thing that is instrumental for going / moving; leg (karaṇa sādhana) }}
          • {{23707047844377027::(vi) √har + ṇa}} = {{8228770093898874::vihār}}{{8228770093898874::o – place one lives (adhikaraṇa sādhana) }}
          • {{835958262105374::√su + ti}} = {{4696344215189481::suti – hearing (bhāva sādhana) }}
          • {{19092005251446897::√dā + yu}} = {{34611117329788343::dāna}}{{34611117329788343::ṃ - reality that in instrumental in giving that is to say }}{{34611117329788343::dāna}}{{34611117329788343:: cetanā (volition in giving) (karaṇa sādhana) }}
      • 8. Kāraka
        • i. Why are some meanings of nominal cases called as ‘kāraka’?
          • Some of the meanings conveyed by nominal case endings are directly involved in producing the action. They are also called kāraka since they produce the action – “Kriyaṃ karoti abhinipphādetīti kārako”
        • ii. List down the six kāraka meanings.
          • (1). Kattu attha
          • (2). Kamma attha
          • (3). Karaṇa attha
          • (4). Sampadāna attha
          • (5). Apadāna attha
          • (6). Adhikaraṇa attha
        • iii. Give two examples for akāraka meanings.
          • liṅga attha and sāmi attha
        • iv. Describe a meaning of Nominative case with an example.
          • every noun is a liṅga and its meaning is called liṅgattha when a word merely conveys the meaning of a liṅga without referring to special meanings such as kattu, kamma and so on, the nominative case is added to it 'puriso gacchati' puriso is the subject expressed by the verb, therefore there is no need for an additional nominal case ending to 'purisa' to show that it is the subject so only the nominative case is used in the meaning of liṅgattha
        • v. Describe ‘accanta saṃyoga’ meaning of accusatve case with an example.
          • The term accanta saṃyoga means “being mixed or involved without any gap or interval If something exists, if some action happens or if some quality exists throughout a certain duration of time without any interval or throughout a certain distance without any gap, that happening, or existence is called accanta saṃyoga. When this meaning is to be expressed, accusative cases is added to the noun that indicates the duration of time or the distance.
          • Kāla Accanta Saṃyoga
            • Bhagavā sattāhaṃ ekapallaṅkena nisīdati.
            • In the above example sentence, the Blessed One sat in the crossed-leg posture for one week. But as he sat in that posture continuously without changing his posture, the time period throughout which he sat is written in accusative case. Therefore, instead of writing as “Bhagavā sattāhe ekapallaṅkena nisīdi” the word that indicates the duration of time is written in accusative case – “Bhagavā sattāhaṃ ekapallaṅkena nisīdi”
          • Addhā Accanta Saṃyoga
            • Addhā means “distance.”
            • Yojanaṃ dhāvati.
            • According to the above sentence, the act of running has happened throughout the entire yojana. Therefore, the word yojana is written in accusative case
        • vi. “antarā ca rājagahaṃ antarā ca nālandaṃ addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti” In this sentence, in which meaning is accusative case used in rājagahaṃ and nālandaṃ?
          • Accusative Case in Chaṭṭhi Vibhatti
            • He is going (He has started a journey) on the long road between the cities of Rājagaha and Nālanda. In this sentence, Rājagaha and Nālanda should have been written in genitive case. But due to the influence of “antarā” both rājagaha and nālandā are written in accusative case.
        • vii. Describe any three meanings of instrumental case with examples.
          • Karaṇattha
            • We have already studied the meaning of karaṇattha (meaning of instrument) and the tatiyā vibhatti (instrumental case) which is used to indicate that meaning. See how the instrumental case is used in the meaning of karaṇa.
            • Kassako dāttena vīhiṃ lunāti.
            • Puriso cakkhunā candaṃ passati.
          • Kattvattha
            • In passive voice sentences, the subject is written in instrumental case.
            • Purisena odano paccate
          • Hetvattha
            • The reason for the happening of something is called “hetu.” Hetu is indicated by the instrumental case.
              • Kammunā vasalo hoti. – One becomes an outcast due to (his or her) action.
              • Na jaccā vasalo hoti. – One does not become an outcast due to birth.
              • Dānena bhogavā – One becomes wealthy due to offering (charity)
        • viii. “namo tassa bhagavato arahato” Why dative case is used in “tassa bhagavato arahato” here?
          • (7). When a noun is used together with indeclinables such as “namo, sotthi, svāgataṃ” it must be written in dative case.
            • Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammā sambuddhassa
            • Sotthi te hotu sabbadā
            • Svāgataṃ te mahārāja
        • ix. Describe two meanings of abla;ve case with examples.
          • Pañcamī vibhatti is used in the meaning of apādāna.
            • Gāmā apenti munayo.
            • In the above example, the “village (gāmā)” is the apādāna since sages depart from the village. As in the case of sampadāna, apādāna too covers various kinds of meanings. We shall learn them in detail at a later stage
          • Hetvattha/Kāraṇattha
            • Sometimes, the cause (hetu or kāraṇa) of some happening is written in pañcamī vibhatti.
              • Avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā (sambhavanti) – Saṅkhāras arise due to the cause called avijjā (ignorance).
        • x. “pupphassa buddhaṃ yajati” In which meaning is genitive case used in pupphassa?
          • (1). Sometimes, chaṭṭhi vibhatti is used in the karaṇattha (instrumental meaning).
            • Pupphassa buddhaṃ yajati = Pupphena buddhaṃ yajati.
        • xi. Describe any three meanings of loca;ve case with examples.
          • Sattamī vibhatti is used in the meaning of ādhāra.
            • Sakuṇo rukkhe nisīdati.
          • Niddhāraṇa
            • Sattamī - "Amhesu yo paṭhamaṁ amataṁ adhigacchati, so itarassa ārocetū"
          • Bhāvalakkhaṇa
            • Sattamī - rukkhe patante sakuṇā palāyanti
  • Fundamentals of Theravāda - Bhante Maggavihāri
    • vīthiparicchedo
      • intro
        • introduction
          • 3 phylosophical branches
            • divine / intelligent creation
            • accident (such as big bang)
            • doctrine of necessity (things have been there forever)
              • governed by natural laws (as opposed to human / divine laws)
        • cittavīthi
          • the natural processes tend towards protraction, towards continuance, towards extending saṁsāra, not towards cessation
          • cittavīthi ‒ definition
            • the sequential chains of consciousnesses that arise in order to perform various mental activities
            • whatever change that occurs in the mind-stream due to the impingement of an object
          • 3 stages of every conditioned reality
            • uppādakhaṇa (arising / genesis moment): the period the reality arises and is strengthened
            • ṭhitikkhaṇa (persisting moment): the period the reality is decaying / persisting
              • bhaṅgābhimukha↔heading towards dissolution
                • vibhāvinī: during ṭhiti, the dhamma stands facing its own dissolution (bhaṅgābhimukhāvathā)
              • saṅkhatalakkhaṇasuttaṃ "tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, saṅkhatassa saṅkhatalakkhaṇāni. katamāni tīṇi? uppādo paññāyati, vayo paññāyati, ṭhitassa aññathattaṃ paññāyati. imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi saṅkhatassa saṅkhatalakkhaṇānī"ti.
            • bhaṅgakkhaṇa (dissolution / perishing moment): the period the reality is vanishing
            • note:
              • ledi: ṭhiti could be the mid point between arising and vanishing, and could also be the entire period of the existence of the dhamma
          • dhammas in a cittuppāda have the same birth / arising, therefore saying that they "arise together" is not precise
        • duration of conditioned realities
          • duration of conditioned realities
            • citta / cetasikas
              • uppādakkhaṇa: 1 anucittakkhaṇa
              • ṭhitikkhaṇa: 1 anucittakkhaṇa
              • bhaṅgakkhaṇa: 1 anucittakkhaṇa
              • total: 3 anucittakkhaṇa = 1 cittakkhaṇa
            • rūpa (22, except viññatti and lakkhaṇarūpa)
              • uppādakkhaṇa: 1 anucittakkhaṇa
              • ṭhitikkhaṇa: 49 anucittakkhaṇa
              • bhaṅgakkhaṇa: 1 anucittakkhaṇa
              • total: 51 anucittakkhaṇa = 17 cittakkhaṇa (51/3=17)
            • rūpa (short lived)
              • 2 viññatti: 1 ck
              • upacaya: 1 ack
              • santati: 1 ack
              • jaratā: 49 ack
              • aniccatā: 1 ack
            • what is the ultimate measure of time?→anucittakkhaṇa
          • are rūpas arising and vanishing in phase? what about nāmas?
            • kammaja-, utuja- and āhāraja-rūpas can arise in any anucittakkhaṇa, cittajarūpas every arising moment of citta, therefore they do not arise and vanish in phase; in the case of nāmas, it is not given, but it may be that they all arise in phase
          • how many rūpakalāpas can be taken as object by one single cakkhu- / sota-dvāra vīthis? why?
            • only 1 / 51th of the present rūpakalāpas (1.96%), since they must be of the same "age" and they last 51 anucittakkhaṇas
            • only those that are visible (depending on light, one's position, etc.)
          • the pasāda serving as vatthu for dvepañcaviññāṇa is of which age?
            • the same age as the object
          • samudāyaggāhī: grasping after a collection; referring to a vīthi that puts together a collection of data to form a whole picture
          • samudāya (m.) [saṃ + ud + ā + √i + *a]↔collection; multitude (s.w/ s) #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
          • gāhī (adj.)↔(+acc) grasping after; grabbing hold (of) #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
          • how many rūpakalāpas are taken at once by each of the 5 senses?
            • cakkhuviññāṇa and sotaviññāṇa take multiple of their respective objects at a time, while ghāna, jivhā and kāya take only one single rūpa at a time
          • if rūpa lasts 17 cittakkhaṇas why change is not seen in material objects?
            • because they do not vanish simultaneously
            • and new rūpas arise in the places where previous ones vanished
          • is there a reason given for rūpas to last for 17 ck, not more, not less? why higher quality rūpas cannot last longer? #q🙋🏼‍♂
        • visayappavatti
          • visayappavatti ‒ definition
            • the presentation of an object to consciousness at one of the six doors, or the occurrence of states of consciousness upon the presentation of an object visaya: object, objective field pavatti: occurance, appearance, manifestation
          • 6 sixes
            • 6 dvāra
            • 6 vatthu
            • 6 viññāṇa
            • 6 ārammaṇa
            • 6 visayappavatti
            • 6 vīthi
          • 6 visayappavatti: 4 types of objects of the five senses and 2 mind-door objects
            • five sense-doors:
              • atimahantārammaṇa (very great / distinguished object)
              • mahantārammaṇa (great / distinguished object)
              • parittārammaṇa (slight / undistinguished object)
              • atiparittārammaṇa (very slight /very undistinguished object)
            • mind-door:
              • vibhūtārammaṇa (clear object)
              • avibhūtārammaṇa (obscure object)
              • note:
                • ledi: there is also ati vibhūta, vibhūta, avibhūta and atiavibhūta
            • maha and paritta in this context refers to what?→the clarity of the object for consciousness, indicating the number of vīthicittas that arise taking it as object
          • 4 main types of objects according to prominence
            • atimahantārammaṇa (1) (very distinguished object)
              • highly prominent / distinguished object
              • impinges on any of the five doors
              • impinges after one mind moment from its genesis (during the second mind moment)
            • mahantārammaṇa (2) (distinguished object)
              • prominent / distinguished object but less than atimahanta
              • impinges on any of the five doors
              • impinges after two or three mind moments from its genesis (during the third or fourth mind moment); therefore it is of 2 types
            • parittārammaṇa (6) (undistinguished object)
              • undistinguished object less prominent than mahanta
              • impinges on any of the five doors
              • impinges after four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine mind moments after genesis (on the 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th or 10th mind-moment, respectively) therefore it is of 6 types
            • atiparittārammaṇa (6) (very undistinguished object)
              • very undistinguished object / non-prominent objects
              • impinges on any of the five doors
              • impinges after ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, or fifteen mind moments from genesis; therefore it is of 6 types
            • what are the 75 visayappavatti / pañcadvārika vīthis?
              • 15 types of objects according to prominence
                • 1 atimahanta
                • 2 mahanta
                • 6 paritta
                • 6 atiparitta
              • X 5 doors = 75 visayappavatti
          • strength of rūpa / citta during their existence and why
            • rūpa:
              • weak during the uppādakkhaṇa strong during the ṭhitikkhaṇa very weak during the bhaṅgakkhaṇa why? bc it has the support of tejo, oja, jīvitindriya, citta & cetasikas (pacchājātapaccaya) during the ṭhitikkhaṇa; not during upppādakkhaṇa
            • citta:
              • strong during the uppādakkhaṇa weaker during ṭhitikkhaṇa very weak during bhaṅgakkhaṇa why? bc it has the support of anantara-, samanantara-, anantarupanissaya-paccayas during the uppādakkhaṇa; not during ṭhitikkhaṇa
          • rūpa cannot impinge during the {{832082747788661::first and last cittakkhaṇas of its lifespan}}; that is so due to {{832082747788661::its weakness during the uppāda and bhaṅgakkhaṇas}} ; after impingement has happened, it can still be an object during its last mind moment; only {{832082747788661::manoviññāṇa}} can see its genesis
            • problem: the uppādakkhaṇa and bhaṅgakkhaṇas only lasts 1/3 of a cittakkhaṇa; no answer; solved by mūlaṭīkā's method in which citta only has uppāda and bhaṅgakkhaṇas; it takes a fulll cittakkhaṇa for the arising of rūpa
            • 2 types of "impingement" (WIP)
              • the impingement of kalāpa with kalāpa (such as the production of sound): this happens physically, while kalāpas arise in proximity to each other
              • the impingement of sense objects with pasāda (such as in the case of rūpārammaṇa in which it produces an image while being far away)
            • how can the arising of rūpa be seen if rūpa cannot impinge during uppādakkhaṇa?
              • even though it cannot impinge and become the object of 10 viññāṇas, manoviññāṇa can see its arising
        • naming vīthis
          • 3 ways of naming vīthis
            • according to visayappavatti (atimahantārammaṇavīthi...)
            • according to dvāra (cakkhudvārikavīthi...sota...ghāna...jivhā...kāya...mano...)
              • missakadvāravīthi: a name for pañcadvāravīthis since they involve both a material and the mental door
              • suddhamanodvāravīthi: process that is only of the mind door
            • according to viññāṇa (cakkhuviññāṇavīthi...manoviññāṇavīthi [process in which only manoviññāṇas arise])
              • but since there are no five sense viññāṇa arising in pañcadvārika atiparittārammaṇavīthis, this naming is not precise
        • vīthi chart (244 vīthis)
          • pañcadvārikavīthi - 75
            • 15 cakkhudvārikavīthi
              • 1 atimahantārammaṇacakkhudvārikavīthi
              • 2 mahantārammaṇacakkhudvārikavīthi
              • 6 parittārammaṇacakkhudvārikavīthi
              • 6 atiparittārammaṇacakkhudvārikavīthi
            • 15 sotadvārikavīthi
            • 15 ghanadvārikavīthi
            • 15 jivhādvārikavīthi
            • 15 kāyadvārikavīthi
          • manodvārikavīthi - 14 types (total 169)
            • kāmajavanavīthi / kāmāvacaravīthi - 9
              • kāmāvacara manodvāravīthi that lasts for 17 cittakkhaṇa ("long vīthis") - 7
                • vibhūtārammaṇa - 5
                • avibhūtārammaṇa - 2
              • kāmāvacara manodvāravīthi shorter than 17 cittakkhaṇa ("short vīthis") - 2
                • vibhūtārammaṇa - 1
                • avibhūtārammaṇa - 1
            • appaṇājavanavīthi / appaṇāvīthi - 5 (total 160)
              • mahaggatajhānavīthi / jhānavīthi - 72
                • 9 jhānas x 2 puggala x 2 stages x 2 jāti
              • abhiññāṇavīthi - 4
                • 2 jāti x 2 puggala
              • maggavīthi - 40
                • 4 maggas x 5 jhānas x 2 puggalas
              • phalasamāpattivīthi - 40
                • 4 phalas x 5 jhānas x 2 puggalas
              • nirodhasamāpattivīthi - 4
                • 2 puggalas x 2 jāti (kusala for anāgāmi / kiriya for arahant)
        • mūlacitta
          • what is mūlacitta?→it is the bhavaṅgacitta which is the fundamental consciousness, due to which the stream of consciousness keeps on arising
          • terms for the bhavaṅga as the default citta:
            • Base / Home Base: (Common, versatile)
            • Default: (Especially for systems, settings, or typical states)
            • Origin: (Where it began, and from which it returns)
            • Resting state: (For more technical or physical contexts)
            • Anchor: (Metaphorical, something that grounds it)
            • Starting point / Point of origin: (If it returns to where it began)
            • Baseline: (If it returns to a standard or normal level)
            • Status quo: (The existing state that it reverts to)
            • IIT - Nissayamuttaka Course
          • paṭisandhi and cuti cittas, according to paṭṭhāna, can also be called bhavaṅga

            • does the mahāvipākas take paññatti as object when acting as paṭisandhi for those coming from brahma realms or does it necessarily take another object related to it? prmtdpn: upacarasamaāḍhi, dies, born in kāmarealm; ptbg nimitta be the obj of ptsd; what would b the obj if mahāvipāka does not take paññatti? it cannot get it as obj; so maraṇāsanna obj and ptsd obj in some cases do not match; vmtvndn: opinion: mvi Td are only kāmāvacara; someone offer flower and die, becomes kāmanimimtta, is it pure paramattha or mixed with paññatti? as obj of mvi, it thinks sappaññatti is capable to be obj of mvi but not suddhapaññatti; prmtdpn: cannot take pñt bc it doesnt' have that thinking capacity; just the color of the monk, not mixed with paññatti; ‒ human, ptbg nmt as maraṇāsanna obj, asaññasatta no mrnsn obj, human 00 human with upacara, focus on ptbg nmt in mrnsn, born as deva, ptsd cannot take pñt; in arupa realm having gatinimitta as obj in mrnsn, (to be expanded) 3 occasions ptsd is not taken by mrnsn of the previous life #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • the influence of the bhavaṅga on the mind stream

      • types of pañcadvāravīthi
        • atimahantārammaṇavīthi
          • what happens immediately before the atimahantārammaṇa cakkhudvārikavīthi begins, and what is the simile for it?
            • a rūpārammaṇa arises, after 1 ck it impinges at the cakkhupasāda that is of the same age and, at the same time, impinges at the bhavaṅga, which causes it to "vibrate" for 2 cittakkhaṇas and be arrested
            • simile for the double strike (missakadvāra)
              • like a bird landing on a branch and its shadow hitting the ground at the same time
              • like a drum that when striken on one side, causes the other side to vibrate
          • atimahantārammaṇacakkhudvāravīthi
            • / 1. Tī | 2. {Na} | 3. Da | 4. Pa | 5. Cv | 6. Sp | 7. Sn | 8. Vo | 9. J | 10. J | 11. J | 12. J | 13. J | 14. J | 15. J | 16. Td | 17. Td \
            • note:
              • / = object arises
              • \ = object vanishes
              • {} = object strikes
              • = vīthicittas
          • how many cittas comprise the atimahantārammaṇavīthi?→14
          • extra notes:
            • bhavaṅga
              • bhavaṅga upaccheda can also be called calana since it also vibrates due to the impingement of the object
              • why is bhavaṅga atīta given?→in order to show when the pasāda and the ārammaṇa arose
            • impingement / striking
              • why does the fivedoor object strike on the bhavaṅga?→a reason is not given; it simply occurs according to natural laws
                • "{{9816670435009833::na hi paccakkhasiddhe yuttimagganaṃ yuttanti}}" (when smth is obvious or directly seen, an explanation is not needed) (Dhammasaṅgaṇīmūlaṭīkā)
                • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
                  • paccakkha (adj.) [pati + √akkh + a]↔seen; witnessed; 2 visible; self-evident; clear; perceivable
                  • siddha↔pp. happened, succeeded, availed
                  • yutti (f.)↔justice, fitness
                  • magganaṁ (nt.) magganā (f.)↔search, tracing out (s.w/ m)
              • does the object repeatedly strikes the pasāda?
                • when the object strikes it keeps in contact for the duration of the vīthi; the impingement lasts for the duration of the vīthi
              • can another object strike the pasāda after it has been impinged on?
                • prmtdpn: cakkhu pasāda comes to vikāra after being impinged on, (like the stamping with lac) and another object cannot strike it
            • arising of rūpa
              • kammaja, utuja and aharajarūpas arise {{6085002502161843::in every anucittakkhaṇa}} while cittajarūpas arise {{6085002502161843::in the uppādakkhaṇa of the citta}}
              • what is the similarity of these 3 dhammas: atītabhavanga, cakkhupasāda and rupārammaṇa?→they arise at the same time
            • tī here is said to be the moment a sense object enters a sense door. What is meant by entering the sense door, because it is not impinging at that time.
        • notation of processes
          • notation / symbols / abbreviations of vīthicittas
            • 1 Atīta bhavaṅga {{1556824048666945::Tī}} 2 Bhavaṅga calana {{1556824048666945::Na}} 3 Bhavaṅgupaccheda {{1556824048666945::Da}} 4 Pañcadvārāvajjana {{1556824048666945::Pa}} 5 Cakkhuviññāṇa {{1556824048666945::Cv}} 6 Sotaviññāṇa {{1556824048666945::Sv}} 7 Ghānaviññāṇa {{1556824048666945::Ghv}} 8 Jivhāviññāṇa {{1556824048666945::Jv}} 9 Kāyaviññāṇa {{1556824048666945::Kv}} 10 Sampaṭicchana {{1556824048666945::Sp}} 11 Santīraṇa {{1556824048666945::Sn}} 12 Votthapana {{1556824048666945::Vo}} 13 Javana {{1556824048666945::J}} 14 Tadārammaṇa {{1556824048666945::Td}} Bhavaṅga {{1556824048666945::Bh}} Manodvārāvajjana {{1556824048666945::Ma}} Cuticitta {{1556824048666945::Cuti}} Jhāna {{1556824048666945::Jh}} Abhiññāṇa {{1556824048666945::Abhi}} Vodāna {{1556824048666945::Vd}} Magga {{1556824048666945::Mg}} Phala {{1556824048666945::Ph}}
          • object of each cakkhudvāravīthicitta
            • bhavaṅgas (atīta, calana, upaccheda): kamma, kammanimitta or gatinimitta
            • from Pa to Td: present rūpārammaṇa
          • simile of the mango
            • a man is asleep under a mango tree with ripe fruits (Bh)
            • suddenly, a ripe mango falls near his ear (rūpārammaṇa strikes cakkhupasāda; Na)
            • causing him to wake up due to the noise (Pa)
            • he then opens his eyes and looks at the mango (Cv)
            • picks it up (Sp)
            • presses it to check its ripeness (Sn)
            • smells it to confirm its ripeness (Vo)
            • proceeds to eat the mango (J)
            • swallowing the remaining bits (Td)
            • and finally, he goes back to sleep (Bh)
          • comments on each citta
            • the role of pañcadvārāvajjana and simile
              • to direct the flux of consciousnesses towards the newly arrived gocara without seeing it
              • simile: like a spider turning towards a newly arrived creature on its web
            • Pa is also called
              • vīthi paṭipādaka citta since the vīthi takes the object due to it
            • purpose of the Cv is to see the object clearly
              • the decay of rūpa means {{46599940869026346::decay in its ability to sustain itself, not in its appearance}} #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • Sp cannot have somanassavedanā because {{4158811027937397::of its weakness due to the change of base, like receiving and passing bricks on without investigating them}}
              • why does the base come back to being hadayavatthu after cakkhuvatthu?→in order to give rise to javanas to experience the object intensely, to gain a better understanding of it, and due to cakkhuvatthu being a weak base
            • simile for Sn: like a child getting a new object: if it is very pleasing, the child experiences somanassa, otherwise upekkhā
            • due to the repetitive cognition of the object, Vo arises judging / deciding on / reacting to the object; in pañcadvāravīthi this decision is mostly influenced {{3839693896180625::by habits or by previous processes}}
              • notes on nimitta and ākāra #wip🚧 #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • citta nimitta, citta ākāra
                • saññaja (mind created image, nimitta, not reality, ākāra)
                • ārammaṇa or ākara/nimitta; in some places the ākāra may be called ārammaṇa
                • rūpaṁ attato samanupassati (regarding materiality as atta)
                • diṭṭhasadisa (taking the object similar to what was seen)
            • the javanas are the consciousnesses that fully apprehend the object
            • at which stage is the process of seeing the rūpārammaṇa completed? what is the importance of Td?
              • it is completed with the 7 javanas
              • the Td are of lesser significance since brahmas can perceive objects accurately without registering them
            • each citta arises, performs its function and vanishes; they are not aware of anything beyond performing their own respective functions
              • IIT - Nissayamuttaka Course
        • occurrence of cittavīthis
          • cittavīthis cannot be intentionally produced or organized by one's effort nor by the power of any god or entity; these processes arise according to natural laws due to the influence of the preceding consciousnesses and the impact of an object
            • IIT - Nissayamuttaka Course
          • what is niyāma / dhammatā / niyati
            • natural laws that have not been established by anyone, nor are the result of the wish of a self or god, that govern the manifestation of realities
            • dhamma is {{31357120857323584::the realities}} and dhammatā is {{31357120857323584::the laws which govern their manifestation}}
              • dhammatā sometimes is explained as the paccayasatti
        • mahantārammaṇavīthi
          • what are some of the reasons for rūpārammaṇa to delay its strike?
            • small: the object being smalla
            • distant: object being at a distance even if it is large
            • dark: or the light in the surrounding being dim
          • why tadārammaṇacittas do not arise in the first type of mahantārammaṇavīthi?
            • weak: cdvml: during the last mind moment, the visible object is very weak and incapable of being a condition for the arising of a tadārammaṇa citta, therefore they only arise in pairs
            • past: if 2 tadārammaṇas were to arise, the second would have to take a past object which violates the cittaniyāma
            • note: there are differing opinions on the reason why tadārammaṇacittas do not arise

          • how many vīthicittas comprise the parittārammaṇavīthis?
            • from the 1st to the 5th parittārammaṇavīthi, there are 7 cittas, while in the 6th one, there are 6 cittas
          • what is the usual number of javanas? what happens when they do not arise?
            • javanas normally occur in a group of 7
            • if that is not possible, they do not arise at all and the vīthi will either have a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 3 votthapanas
          • 6 special situations in which javanas may be less than 7 (this list may not include all possibilities)
            • during birth
            • close to death
            • when one is unconscious
              • when one has drowned (but is not dead yet)
            • during the 2 most difficult pāṭihāriya (miracles)
              • yamakapāṭihāriya (only performed by SSB)
              • lokavivaraṇapāṭihāriya
          • how does the mind "know" there is not enough time for javanas to arise?
            • it is not clear, but there is some connection between the object and the citta; this is related, for example, to mettājjhāna not being able to be developed if the living being that is taken as object has died
          • in what aspects are objects in a single vīthi alike (in most cases)?
            • same dhamma
            • same kāla
            • note: there are a few occasions, in which this law is broken; some teachers do not take this law as binding, especially when explaining the mind processes which occur while reading others’ minds

          • what happens when the minimum of 2 votthapanas cannot arise?
            • no Vo: if the object impinges from the 11th to the 16th cittakkhaṇa, there is not enough time for two votthapanas to arise, and since there cannot be a vīthi with only a single votthapana, no votthapana arises
            • no vīthicittas: when there is no votthapana, none of the vīthi cittas occur; since no vīthicittas occur, the stream of bhavaṅga is not interrupted, therefore after the impingement, only two bhavaṅga calana arise
          • why do the other vīthicittas not arise if votthapana does not arise?
            • because the object is very weak, therefore its impact will only result in the vibration of the bhavaṅga
          • there is a minimum of {{6574093613632828::2}} bhavaṅga calana in atiparittārammaṇavīthis because {{6574093613632828::rūpa does not strike at the last cittakkhaṇa due to its weakness}}
          • minimum of Bh before any vīthi
            • 2; even during the twin miracle, they occur
          • why are there only 15 possibilities of cakkhudvārikavīthi?
            • because the object does not strike in its 1st and 17th mind moments, so 15 are left
          • why, even though there are no vīthicittas, the atiparittārammaṇavīthi is still called vīthi?
            • because whatever change occurs in the mind due to the impingement of an object can be called vīthi
          • why tadārammaṇas only arise in the kāma realm? (opinion)
            • because they are the realms that take sense objects the most, and such vīthi can experience the object for a longer period
          • how well objects are known by each vīthi
            • known very well by atimahantārammaṇavīthis and mahantārammaṇavīthis
            • not known well, felt unclear, like a dream by parittārammaṇavīthis because no javanas arise
            • not known at all by atiparittārammaṇavīthis
          • names of the vīthis according to vāra
            • atimahantārammaṇavīthi can be called tadārammaṇavāra
            • mahantārammaṇavīthi can be called javanavāra
            • parittārammaṇavīthi can be called votthapanavāra
            • atiparittārammaṇavīthi can be called bhavaṅgavāra or moghavāra (due do there being no awareness of the object)
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • mogha [√muh + *gha] adj.↔useless; stupid; in vain; waste; wrong; foolish; lit. empty
        • cittaniyāma
          • jāti of the cittas of the pañcadvāravīthi
            • Pa is a kiriyacitta
            • Cv, Sv, Ghv, Jv, Kv, Sp and Sn cittas are vipākacittas
            • Vo is a kiriyacitta
            • J can be either kusala, akusala, or kiriyacittas
            • Td, Tī, Na, Da, Bh are vipākacittas
          • the relationship between the ārammaṇarasa and the vīthicittas
            • if iṭṭhārammaṇa impinges
              • kusalavipāka cittas arise (5 kusalavipākaviññāṇas, 1 Sp, 2 Sn, 10 Td)
              • javanas can be kusala / akusala / kiriya
            • if ati-iṭṭhārammaṇa impinges
              • kusalavipāka cittas arise and the Sn and Td are accompanied by somanassavedanā (5 ku vip viññāṇas, 1 Sp, 1 Sn [som], 5 Td [4 som mvip and 1 som Sn])
              • āgantukabhavaṅga #editing
                • sometimes, when the J is domanassa, an āgantuka Bh occurs instead of Td or som Bh
                  • upe Bh is upe Sn (2 cittas; standard), but prmtdpn seems that mvip can also be (6 cittas as āgantuka)
                  • there are special atimahantārammaṇavīthis without Td;
                  • considered out of the vīthi
                  • mahantārammaṇa with 1 Td possible (not discussed) (mūla-ṭ)
                • always upekkhā vedanā
                • takes a diferent object iṭṭhamajjhatta object; any object taken frequently previously;
                • somanassabhavaṅgaṁ...(paṭṭhāna)
                • two successive cittas cannot be domanassa and somanassa and vice-versa
                • dom ⇒ dom / up
                • som ⇒ som / up
                • up ⇒ up / som / dom
                • if the Bh is 1st mvip (som); and Td is 2nd Som citta; that citta is also called āgantuka bhavaṅga (not so common meaning);
                • what determines which citta occurs as Td?
                • dhms-a: explains Td like this; mūla Bh, Td same as Bh, then a dfr Td is called āgantuka Bh; give t impression that Bh and Td should be the same;
                  • Td seems to be considered an extension of Bh
            • if aniṭṭhārammaṇa impinges
              • akusalavipāka cittas arise (5 akusalavipākaviññāṇa, 1 Sp, 1 Sn, 1 Td)
            • note: javanas can be kusala / akusala / kiriya in any case
          • according to the commentaries, the evaluation of the nature of the object as iṭṭha or aniṭṭha should be based on what?
            • the consideration of middle-class people
          • in whom do kusala / akusala javanas normally arise?
            • kusala javanas can arise regarding any object in people who
              • are deeply engaged in wholesomeness
              • are close to the Dhamma
              • habitually have yoniso manasikāra / wholesome disposition (kusalajjhāsaya)
            • akusala javanas can arise regarding any object in people who are
              • deeply engaged in unwholesomeness
              • distant from the Dhamma
              • and habitually have ayoniso manasikāra
            • kiriya javanas arise in the processes of Arahants
          • can kusalavipāka and akusalavipākacittas be in the same vīthi?
            • no, always either kusala or akusala vipāka
          • vatthu of each pañcadvārikavīthicitta
            • dvepañcaviññāṇas arise in their respective vatthu
            • the others arise in hadayavatthu
          • dvāra of each pañcadvārikavīthicitta
            • all the cittas in the entire process that arises due to the striking of a rūpārammaṇa on the cakkhudvāra are called cakkhudvārikacittas (including cittas that have hadayavatthu as vatthu)
            • the same for the other doors
          • minimum and maximum number of cittas in a vīthi (not counting atiparittārammaṇavīthi)
            • maximum: 14
            • minimum: 6
          • what cittas do / do not arise in atimahanta / mahanta / paritta / atiparittārammaṇavīthis #tbc🕵 #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • atimahantārammaṇavīthi: all 54 kāmāvacaracittas can arise
            • mahantārammaṇavīthi: 8 mahāvipākas cannot arise
            • parittārammaṇavīthi: 8 mahāvipākas, 29 kāmajavanas cannot arise
            • atiparittārammaṇavīthi: no cittas arise
      • types of manodvāravīthis
        • manodvāravīthi
          • 2 main types of manodvāravīthi
            • kāmajavanavīthis / kāmāvacaravīthis / parittavīthi (definition)
              • mind-door processes in which only kāmajavanas arise in the place of javana they are of 2 kinds based on objects
                • kāmāvacara manodvāravīthi that lasts 17 cittakkhaṇas
                • kāmāvacara manodvāravīthi that lasts less than 17 cittakkhaṇa
            • appaṇājavanavīthi / appaṇāvīthi (definition)
              • mind-door processes in which at least one appaṇājavana arises in the place of javana (though kāmāvacaracittas also arise in this vīthi)
              • is there a mind process solely constituted of appaṇā cittas?
                • no
          • 9 kāmāvacara manodvāravīthis according to object
            • 7 vīthis that last 17 ck ‒ 2 types with their objective range
              • 5 vibhūtārammaṇavīthi
              • 2 avibhūtārammaṇavīthi
              • their object range is Group A objects (22 paccuppanna rūpas which last 17 ck)
            • 2 vīthis that last less than 17 ck ‒ 2 types with their objective range
              • 1 vibhūtārammaṇavīthi: kāmāvacaradhammas of Group B objects
              • 1 avibhūtārammaṇavīthi: Group B objects
            • notes:
              • Group A objects, Group B objects, and kāmāvacaradhamma of Group B objects

          • what is vibhūta and avibhūtārammaṇavīthi?
            • vibhūtārammaṇavīthi is a vīthi that takes a distinct / clear / powerful object while avibhūtārammaṇavīthi is one that takes an indistinct / obscure / weak object
            • however, in the way Abhidhamma is taught these days, it is not easy to establish a strong relationship between the clarity or obscurity of the object and the relevant mind processes
            • it is acceptable to consider kāmāvacaravīthis in which tadārammaṇa is found as vibhūtārammaṇavīthis, whereas kāmāvacaravīthis in which tadārammaṇa is not found as avibhūtārammaṇavīthis
            • appaṇājavanavīthis are all vibhūtārammaṇavīthis even though they do not possess Td

        • manodvāravīthis according to occasion
          • the act of seeing something corresponds to the arising of a {{45721754993026353::cakkhudvārika vīthi }}that has as object the {{45721754993026353::paccuppanna rūpārammaṇa}} if one recalls what was seen, it corresponds to the arising of a {{45721754993026353::manodvārika vīthi}} that has as object the {{45721754993026353::atīta rūpārammaṇa}}{{45721754993026353:: which was the object of has as object the {{45721754993026353::past rūpas}}{{45721754993026353:: that existed while you were experiencing it (these are the eight }}{{45721754993026353::avinibbhoga rūpas}}{{45721754993026353:: and }}{{45721754993026353::ākāsadhātu}}{{45721754993026353::)}} If one worships the Mahāceti from home, it corresponds to the arising of {{45721754993026353::one of the 7 manodvāravīthis that last for 17 ck}} that has as object the {{45721754993026353::present rūpakalāpas of the Mahāceti, }}{{45721754993026353::not the Mahāceti that was previously seen,}}{{45721754993026353:: }}{{45721754993026353::because all the rūpas that were seen previously as the Mahāceti no longer exist in the present}} If one directs the attention towards the concept of Mahāceti (attha paññatti) or its name (nāma paññatti), it corresponds to the arising of {{45721754993026353::an avibhūtārammaṇa manodvārika vīthi that lasts less than 17 ck}}that has as object the {{45721754993026353::attha / nāmapaññatti}} if one remembers the act of seeing the Mahāceti, it corresponds to the arising of {{45721754993026353::one of the two manodvārikavīthis that last less than seventeen mind moments}} that has as object the {{45721754993026353::past cakkhuviññāṇa or the entire cakkhudvārika vīthi}} if one recalls the pīti / vedanā / love / hatred...one experienced in the past, it corresponds to the arising of {{45721754993026353::a manodvāravīthi that lasts less than 17 ck}} that has as object {{45721754993026353::that respective past dhamma}} when one empathizes with the emotions of others, it correspond to the arising of {{45721754993026353::a manodvāravīthi}} that has as object {{45721754993026353::the dhammas that arise in the minds of others}} if one perceives         • causes for the arising of manodvāravīthi
          • 4 main causes for the arising of manodvāravīthi
            • diṭṭhavasena: manodvāravīthi caused by an object experienced through the 5 doors (diṭṭha here includes all 5 doors); it is of 2 types:
              • immediately upon experiencing it: one sees with cakkhudvāravīthi rūpārammaṇas of a tree and the following manodvāravīthis occur recognizing and thinking about the tree
              • by recalling it at a later time: one remembers having seen the tree (tbc)
            • diṭṭhasambandhavasena: manodvāravīthi caused by an object connected to what was diṭṭha, by inference from what was directly perceived: e.g.: after seeing the tree, one remember a song about trees; one sees smoke, and understands there is fire
            • sutavasena: manodvāravīthi caused by an object acquired by oral or written report, not direct experience - e.g.: one who has never seen snow, hears and thinks about it (note: under diṭṭha, hearing a sound is included; here the mind focuses on what is meant, not the sound itself)
              • hearing
                • diṭṭhavasena: hear the sound of a peacock; mdv occur thinknng "this is the sound of the peacock"
                • diṭṭhasambandhavasena: hear the sound of the peacock; mdv occur taking something connected to that sound: "the sound of a cat"
                • sutavasena: hear the teacher talking about the ocean; mdv occur taking the ocean as object
                • sutasambandhavasena: hear the teacher talking about the ocean; mdv occur taking something else connected to the ocean "a boat"
            • sutasambandhavasena: manodvāravīthi caused by an object connected to what was suta - e.g.: after hearing about snow, one remembers a friend who lives in a cold place
            • note:
              • diṭṭha, in other cases, can mean objects seen by the eye-door only
              • moreover, manodvāravīthis can occur due to:
                • paripucchāvasena: in response to others asking questions
                • parivitakkavasena: during contemplation and thinking
                • nijjhānakkhantivasena: when one comes into a conclusion
                • anubodhavasena: during vipassanā
                • paṭivedhavasena: magga/phalañāṇa
                • samādhivasena: abhiññāṇa
                • devatopasaṁharaṇavasena: obects made manifest by deities perticularly during dreams
                • kammavasena: gatinimitta in maraṇāsanna
                • dhātukhobhavasena: due to imbalances in physical elements (vāta, pitta, and semha)
                • as well as experiences of hunger, thirst, physical pains, meeting enemies, and meeting friends
                • note:
                  • bhavaṅga, though having its own object, is in a constant state of excitement or "buzz", inclining towards other objects, seeking to acquire a clear cognition of an object manasikāra, present in the bhavaṅga, constantly causes it to vibrate, directing consciousness repeatedly to advert to other objects which have gained conditions to appear when an object acquires sufficient prominence through various operative conditions, it draws the mental continuum out of bhavaṅga
        • anubandhaka manodvāravīthi
          • what is anubandhaka manodvāravīthi, and what type of vīthis are they typically?
            • manodvāravīthis which occur subsequently to pañcadvāravīthis taking objects that are related to the object perceived through the five doors
            • they typically last for less than seventeen mind moments since they do not involve a present rūpa; they can be either vibhūtārammaṇa or avibhūtārammaṇa
          • stanza about the functions of each vīthi (from poṭṭhapādasuttavaṇṇanā)
            • “paṭhamaṃ saddaṃ sotena, tītaṃ dutiyacetasā; nāmaṃ tatiyacittena, atthaṃ catutthacetasā”ti.
            • 1st (paṭhamaṁ saddaṁ sotena): ear-door process arises taking that (present) sound as object
            • 2nd (tītaṁ dutiya cetasā): 1st anubandhaka manodvāravīthi taking the same (now atīta) object
            • 3rd (nāmaṁ tatiyacittena): 2nd anubandhaka manodvāravīthi takes nāmapaññatti
            • 4th (atthaṁ cacutthacetasā): 3rd anubandhaka manodvāravīthi knows the object's meaning (attha), which is mostly hīnattha, but could also be paramattha; the perception "I saw such and such a thing" only occurs after the arising of this third manodvāravīthi
            • note:
              • after which pañcadvāravīthi anubandhaka manodvāravīthis do not arise?
                • subsequent to an atiparittārammaṇa pañcadvāravīthi
                • IIT - Nissayamuttaka Course
        • appaṇāvīthis
          • 5 types of appaṇāvīthis
            • mahaggatajhānavīthi / jhānavīthi (mind processes of sublime absorption)
            • abhiññāvīthi (mind processes of psychic power)
            • maggavīthi (mind processes of the supramundane path)
            • phalasamāpattivīthi (mind processes of the attainment of supramundane fruition)
            • nirodhasamāpattivīthi (mind processes of the attainment of cessation)
          • appaṇāvīthis can only be achieved by individuals with {{674214331558151::tihetuka}}paṭisandhi
          • among tihetukas there are two groups
            • khippābhiñña / tikkhapañña (those with swift wisdom / keen faculties)
            • dandhābhiñña / dandhapañña / mandapañña (those with dull or sluggish wisdom / average faculties)
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • tikkha (adj.) [√tij + kha]↔sharp; piercing; acute; 2 (of mind) sharp; quick; keen; penetrating; astute
              • dandha (adj.)↔slow; sluggish; 2 slow, silly, stupid
          • all appaṇavīthis share several characteristics; here are 5
            • Na Da Ma: they are preceded by bhavaṅga calana and bhavaṅga upaccheda and begin with the manodvārāvajjanacitta
            • ñkJ: their javana process starts with ñāṇasampayutta kāmāvacara kusala / kiriya javanas
            • 3 or 4: an appaṇā javana arises only after a certain ñāṇasampayutta kāmāsobhana javana has arisen three (tikkhapañña) or four times (dandhapañña)
              • the opinion that it could occur on the 6th javana has been refuted based on the fact that {{2522746643646383::only the javanas which are in the }}{{2522746643646383::growing process}}{{2522746643646383:: or in the }}{{2522746643646383::peak}}{{2522746643646383:: of power can cause the appaṇājavana to arise, therefore the appaṇā javana must be either the 4th or 5th}}
                • appaṇā javanas have the capacity to maintain the vīthi for a longer period of time, so why are they not in a higher position than gotrabhū in dandhapaññā? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • no Td: tadālambaṇas never arise in these vīthis, as they do not follow the appaṇā javanas
            • vibhūta: they are always vibhūta vīthis because mental absorptions are never attained on obscure objects (but there is no Td)
            • note: appaṇā javanas can only be followed by another appaṇā javana or bhavaṅga

            • mandapañña
              • Bh | Na | Da | Ma | Pk | U | Nu | Go | ApJ | ([...] | ApJ) | Bh

                • anulomacittas
          • name, notation, and function of the 4 kāmāvacara ñs J in appaṇāvīthis
            • parikamma (Pk) (preparation / preliminary work [paṭisaṅkhāraka]): facilitates the arising of the ApJ by balancing the 5 spiritual faculties (saddhā...);
            • upacāra (U) (access): facilitates the arising of appaṇā javana by being in the proximity of absorption
            • anuloma (Nu) (conformity): called so for being in conformity with the meditation done in preceding processes and the absorption about to arise ‒ it removes the disturbances, such as hindrances, for the arising of the ApJ
            • gotrabhū (Go) (change-of-lineage [gotta]): it changes / destroys the kāma gotta / puthujjana lineages respectively, surpassing the lower linage and attaining a higher lineage; it also produces the following ApJ
              • in mahaggatavīthi: changes from kāmāvacara ⇒ mahaggata
              • in the first maggavīthi: destroys the puthujjana ⇒ ariya
              • in higher maggas: cleanses (vodāna [Vo], not Go)
              • it produces, in a way, the following ApJ
              • kāmagotta↔the lineage / clan of sensuality; kāmāvacara; that which is an object of kāmataṇhā
              • mahaggatagotta→the exalted lineage / clan; rūpa- / arūpa- avacara
              • can we say puthujjanagotta and ariyagotta? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • note:
              • their jhānaṅgas are stronger than ordinary kāmāvacaracittas
              • how these 4 cittas can be called
                • all 4 can be termed as parikamma, upacāra and anuloma, but only the fourth citta can be named gotrabhū
                  • Bh Na Da Ma Pk Pk Pk Pk ApJ...Bh
                  • Bh Na Da Ma U U U U ApJ...Bh
                  • Bh Na Da Ma Nu Nu Nu Nu ApJ Bh
              • parikamma is represented as {{5111722210588865::Pk}} upacāra is represented as {{5111722210588865::U}} anuloma is represented as {{5111722210588865::Nu}} gotrabhū is represented as {{5111722210588865::Go}}
          • appaṇā javanas
            • appaṇājavanas are classified into 4 types
              • jhānajavanas
              • abhiññājavanas
              • maggajavanas
              • phalajavanas
              • note: the ekaggatā of these cittas is much stronger than that of the kāmāvacara cittas
            • why are jhānacittas called appaṇā?
              • jhānacittas are called so due to their strong connection with vitakka (also called appaṇā) since all jhānas can only be achieved with its support or involvement; even jhānas higher than the first require its assistance in preliminary meditation which is done with kāmāvacara kusala or kiriya cittas that are accompanied by vitakka; in meditation, vitakka is a crucial mental factor for approaching the object of meditation

            • × 2 (dandhapañña and tikkhapañña) = 36
            • × 2 (kusala and kiriya) = 72
