        • abhiññāvīthi
          • there are mainly 2 attainments in the sāsana
            • abhiññāṇa - under samādhi
            • maggaphala - under paññā
          • what abhiññāvīthi is→vīthi in which kusala / kiriya lokiya abhiññāṇa (5th jh rūpāvacara) citta arises
          • 5 abhiññās and their subcategories
            • iddhividhañāṇa (performing supernatural feats); 2 subtypes
              • manomayaiddhividhañāṇa (creating forms similar one's own form, like Cūlapanthaka)
                • nimittabuddharūpa→creating an image that can preach dhamma; only Buddhas can do it
              • vikubbanaiddhi (changing one's own form into another form, like Mahāmoggallāna while taming nandopananda; it is prohibited in vinaya and is the only offense committed by a mahaggatacitta)
            • dibbasotañāṇa / sotadhātuvisuddhiñāṇa (divine ear / purified ear element)
            • cetopariyañāṇa / paracittavijānana (penetration of minds / knowing other's minds)
            • pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇa (seeing past lives)
              • atītaṁsañāṇa (seeing one's past up to the present life's conception) (not abhiññā)
              • jātissarañāṇa: capacity to recall past lives; usually acquired by birth; many individuals, after experiencing hardships in the womb lose this ability
            • dibbacakkhuñāṇa (divine eye)
              • yathākammūpagañāṇa (seeing the kamma done by other beings)
              • anāgataṃsañāṇa (ability to see into the future; includes the future of inanimate things)
              • note: cutupapātañāṇa (dibbacakkhu, yathākammūpaga and anāgataṁsa can be called collectively so)
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • aṃsa (m.) [√aṃs + a]↔share; portion; part (s.w/ a)
              • vikubbanaṁ (nt.), vikubbanā (f.) [vi + √kar + o + anā]↔miraculous transformation; 2. versatility; (f.) being versatile; being skilful; lit. doing in different ways
              • pariya (m.) [pari + √i + *a]↔encompassing; surrounding; comprehending
              • nivāsa (m.) [ni + √vas + *a]↔dwelling; living place; 2. life; existence; (nt.) clothing; garment; dress
          • method for using abhiññās in general
            • prerequisites:
              • attain all jhānas (rūpā and arūpāvacara)
              • develop cuddasākāravasībhāva (14 ways of mastery)
              • some abhiññāṇas also have their own preliminary work
            • at the time of using:
              • enter the pādakajjhāna (the 5th rūpāvacarajjhāna of a suitable kasiṇa to generate higher power)
              • do paccavekkhaṇa (reflect on its jhānaṅga)
              • perform the adhiṭṭhāna such as, "may a beam of fire be emitted from my body"
              • enter the pādakajjhāna again
              • do paccavekkhaṇa again
              • perform the adhiṭṭhāna again which makes the abhiññāṇa occur
          • vīthis that occur in the method for using abhiññās
            • pādakajjhānavīthi (appaṇāvīthi)
              • mandapañña: Bh Na Da Ma Pk U Nu Go Jh (…) Jh Bh
              • tikkhapañña: Bh Na Da Ma U Nu Go Jh (...) Jh Bh
            • paccavekkhaṇavīthi (avibhūtārammaṇa kāmāvacaravīthi that lasts less than 17 ck and takes past rūpāvacara cetasikas as object)
              • Bh Na Da Ma J J J J J J J Bh
            • adhiṭṭhānavīthi (kāmāvacaravīthi)
              • Bh Na Da Ma J J J J J J J Bh
                • what is the object here? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • abhiññāvīthi (appaṇāvīthi)
              • mandapañña: Bh Na Da Ma Pk U Nu Go Abhi Bh
              • tikkhapañña: Bh Na Da Ma U Nu Go Abhi Bh
              • note:
                • abhiññā acronym is {{40161122039100605::Abhi}}
          • method for emitting a beam of fire from one's body
            • enter into the 5th jhāna of tejo kasiṇa
            • emerge and contemplate its jhāna factors
            • determine, "may a beam of fire be emitted from my body!"
            • enter again the same jhāna
            • emerge and contemplate its jhāna factors
            • determine again for the emission of fire (abhiññā vīthi occurs and along with it, the fire is emitted)
          • kasiṇas used for dibbacakkhu→tejo, odāta or āloka kasiṇa as the pādakajjhāna; some teachers say that āloka kasiṇa suits the best for the divine eye
          • khippanisantitā (tbc): state of being quick in using the abhiññās #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
            • nisanti (f.)→(close) observation; careful attention
          • is there any change of object in these vīthis? #q🙋🏼‍♂
        • maggavīthi
          • anaññātaññassāmītindriya (na aññāta aññassāmi iti indriya) (faculty of "I will know that which is not yet known")
          • some ideas that were rejected in the 3rd council
            • rejected idea: "anupubbeva thokathokaṁ" (the path takes 4 mind moments to destroy defilements); it was rejected by ratanasutta "sahāvassa (saha eva assa) dassanasampadāya tayassudhammā jahitā bhavanti"
          • enumeration of 40 maggavīthis
            • 4 maggavīthis (sotāpatti-, sakadāgāmī-, anāgāmī- and arahatta-maggavīthi)
            • x 5 jhānas = 20
            • × 2 puggala (dandha- / tikkha-pañña) = 40
          • sotāpattimaggavīthi for manda and tikkhapañña
            • mandapañña
              • Bh Na Da Ma Pk U Nu Go Mg Ph Ph Bh
            • tikkhapañña
              • Bh Na Da Ma U Nu Go Mg Ph Ph Ph Bh
            • note:
              • Go is like an avajjanā for magga; it does not have the strength to erradicate defilements
              • Pk, U and Nu can be called {{15597296246755765::anulomañāṇa}}
            • object of each citta
              • Ma: {{3053619890653352::a certain one, or a group of, }}{{3053619890653352::saṅkhāradhamma}} Pk, U, Nu: {{3053619890653352::that saṅkhāradhamma as either }}{{3053619890653352::anicca}}{{3053619890653352::, }}{{3053619890653352::dukkha}}{{3053619890653352:: or }}{{3053619890653352::anatta}} Go, Mg, Ph: {{3053619890653352::Nibbāna}} when discerning saṅkhāras as anicca, dukkha or anatta one does not see simply the lakkhaṇa by itself, but the object with its lakkhaṇa ({{3053619890653352::lakkhaṇavanta}})
            • magga
              • akālika
                • applied by some teacher to pariyatti (since the teaching about akālika is akālika), paṭipatti and paṭivedha; but the highest meaning of akālika is magga giving results immediately; kālika being something that takes time to give result (maggadhamma is not kālika)
              • ānantarikasamādhi↔samādhi of maggacitta that gives results immediately
              • dassana↔sotāpattimaggacitta which sees Nibbāna for the first time (not gotrabhū)
            • nature of each citta
              • Ma: {{13316961217296464::kiriya}} Pk, U, Nu, Go: {{13316961217296464::kusala}} Mg: {{13316961217296464::kusala}} Ph: {{13316961217296464::vipāka}}
            • cittas that arise performing such functions
              • Ma: {{7753764904485299::manodvārāvajjanacitta}} Pk, U, Nu, Go: {{7753764904485299::one of the 4 ñāṇasampayutta mahākusalacittas}} Mg: {{7753764904485299::sotāpattimaggacitta}} Ph: {{7753764904485299::sotāpattiphalacitta}} the functions of Pk, U, Nu, Go are not included in the 14 functions but are special functions of the cittuppāda; amohacetasika plays a prominent role here
          • the only difference between sotāpattimaggavīthi and the other maggavīthis is {{476901861031912::the absence of gotrabhūcitta}} in these vīthis that citta is called {{476901861031912::vodāna}} and refers to the citta that {{476901861031912::purifies the mind by removing the defilements obstructing the arising of maggacitta}} Pk, U, Nu and Go can also be referred to as {{476901861031912::vodāna}}
          • vodāna (nt.) [vi + ava + √dā + ana]↔purifying; cleansing
          • sakadāgāmī-, anāgāmi- and arahatta-maggavīthis for manda and tikkhapañña
            • mandapañña
              • Bh Na Da Ma Pk U Nu Vd Mg Ph Ph Bh
            • tikkhapañña
              • Bh Na Da Ma U Nu Vd Mg Ph Ph Ph Bh
            • note: javanas are always 7
          • paccavekkhaṇavīthi
            • 5 types of paccavekkhaṇavīthi that can occur after the attainment of supramundane paths (test: we should know how to explain them at least in English)
              • maggapaccavekkhaṇavīthi (process reviewing the path)
              • phalapaccavekkhaṇavīthi (process reviewing the fruition)
              • nibbānapaccavekkhaṇavīthi (process reviewing Nibbāna)
              • pahīnakilesapaccavekkhaṇavīthi (process reviewing eradicated defilements)
              • appahīnakilesapaccavekkhaṇavīthi (process reviewing uneradicated defilements)
                • paramatthajātikas cannot be known by sāvakas so this is known based on dhammañāṇa and the power of paccavekkhaṇañāṇa
              • notes:
                • mahānāmasutta: mahānāma, who was a sakadāgāmī, thought sakadāgāmīs were free from kāmarāga and paṭigha completely, and got confused seeing such defilements in himself
                • difference in knowledge between ariyas; some examples:
                  • sotāpannas and sakadāgāmīs don't inherently know they are free from apāya realms
                  • anāgāmi and arahats inherently know they cannot be born in woeful states
                  • arahats inherently know they will not be born again (neither by dhammañāṇa, nor by checking the future...)
                • recalling and paccavekkhaṇa are different things; paccavekkhaṇa investigates; it can occur many times over
                • there is no order to their occurance
                • abhidhammatthasaṅgaha: the first 3 occur to everyone after attaining mahānāmasutta: at least one must occur ledi: mostly 3 occur, but for one who is dying, at least pahīnakilesa occurs
                • separate paccavekkhaṇavīthis arise for each type of reviewing
            • there are a total of {{4097381967903211::19}} paccavekkhaṇavīthis since arahants do not experience the last one which reviews uneradicated defilements
            • 19 paccavekkhaṇavīthis (vīthi cittas)
              • Bh Na Da Ma J J J J J J J Bh
            • 5-fold sāsana
              • sīla
              • samādhi
              • paññā
              • vimutti (phala) (which one?) #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • vimuttiñāṇadassana (19 paccavekkhaṇas or maggaphala paccavekkhaṇa) (tbc) #q🙋🏼‍♂
        • phalasamāpattivīthi
          • enumeration of 40 phalasamāpattivīthis
            • 4 phalasamāpattivīthi (sotāpatti-, sakadāgāmi-, anāgāmi- and arahatta-phalasamāpattivīthi)
            • x5 jhānas = 20
            • x2 puggala (dandhapañña & tikkhapañña) = 40
          • phalasamāpattivīthi for manda and tikkhapañña
            • mandapañña
              • Bh Na Da Ma Nu Nu Nu Nu Ph … Ph Bh
            • tikkhapañña
              • Bh Na Da Ma Nu Nu Nu Ph … Ph Bh
            • note:
              • instead of Pk, U, Nu and Go it is just Nu
                • why? Bh. Mgvhr: I think it is because there is no lessening of defilements as done in maggavīthi
              • the number of phala cittas in a phala samāpatti vīthi is not fixed; it can range from hundreds to even tens of millions or more
              • Nu is ñāṇasampayutta kāmāvacara citta which is kusala for trainees and kiriya for arahats
        • nirodhasamāpattivīthi
          • method for attaining nirodhasamāpatti
            • prerequisites:
              • an anāgāmī or arahat should attain all the 5 rūpa and 4 arūpāvacarajjhānas
            • enter the 1st jhāna
              • of any kasiṇa other than space kasiṇa? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • in this case there is no paccavekkhaṇa of jhānaṅgas? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • emerge and contemplate the 1st jhāna's saṅkhāras as anicca, dukkha and anatta
            • the same should be done for each successive jhāna up to the ākiñcaññāyatanajjhāna
            • after contemplating the saṅkhāras of the ākiñcaññāyatanajjhāna as anicca, dukkha and anatta, one should perform the four preliminary acts of nirodhasamāpatti
            • attain the nevasaññānāsaññāyatanajjhāna intending to cease the mind-stream (nirodha occurs during the vīthi)
            • after emerging phalacitta arise once and then bhavaṅgas
          • 4 preliminary acts of nirodhasamāpatti
            • nānābaddhaavikopana
              • determination: "may all these things not be destroyed by fire, water and so on while I abide in the attainment of cessation"
              • the attainment naturally protects the meditator, his robes and sitting place against any harm (during the attainment and for some times after emerging) but other things should be protected by such determination
            • saṅghapaṭimānana
              • determination: "if the Saṅgha needs me for any vinayakamma may I instantly rise from the attainment"
              • in case this is not done, one will only emerge if the saṅgha sends a messenger who calls one within listening range
            • satthupakkosana
              • determination: "if the Buddha needs to meet me, may I emerge from the attainment instantly."
              • in case this is not done, one will only emerge if the Buddha sends a messenger who calls one within listening range
            • addhānapariccheda
              • consideration of one's remaining lifespan
              • if death is set to occur during the period of the attainment of cessation, the practitioner will automatically rise from it, therefore, it is required to check the remaining lifespan before entering
              • ariyas do not enter the nirodha samāpatti if their death is imminent during that period to avoidkk accusations from others
            • note: it is possible to enter the attainment without such determination
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • vikopanaṁ (nt.) [vi + √kup + *e + ana]↔disturbing; upsetting; harming
              • nānābaddha (adj.)↔belonging to many
              • pakkosanaṁ (nt.) pakkosanā (f.)↔calling (nt./f.)
              • addha (adj.)↔soiled; dirty; moist; (m.) half; part; (nt.) long road; highroad; journey; (nt.) time; period; extent; course (of saṃsāra)
              • pariccheda (m.) [pari + √chid + *a]↔boundary; limit; 2 (m.) definition; classification; distinction; lit. limit; 3 division, chapter in a book
          • nirodhasamāpattivīthi for manda and tikkhapañña
            • mandapañña
              • Bh Na Da Ma Pk U Nu Go Ne (Ne) (acittaka kāla) Ph Bh
            • tikkhapañña
              • Bh Na Da Ma U Nu Go Ne (Ne) (acittaka kāla) Ph Bh
            • note:
              • why is the second Ne optional? #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • Ne may arise once or twice
              • acittaka kāla is the period the mind strem ceases
              • this is not a special vīthi but a nevasaññānāsaññāyatanajjhānavīthi
              • why Ne is interrupted
                • they are the only cittas which are subtle enough to be interrupted
              • in this vīthi {{7076651037492381::3}} types of javanas occur: {{7076651037492381::mahākusala or mahākiriya, NeJ and Ph}}
              • nevasaññānāsaññāyatanajjhāna acronym {{09565184819540185::Ne / NeJ}}
              • ākiñcaññayatanajjhāna acronym {{9495733827057904::AkJ}}
              • the samatha practice produces the {{24077168742883037::NeJ}} while the vipassanā practice produces the {{24077168742883037::Ph}}
              • this is another vīthi in which a change of object occurs; what are the objects in this vīthi?→ākiñcaññāyatanajjhānacitta and Nibbāna
          • the diagram of the javanas is based on the potential to maintain the vīthi (vīthipatita [tbc]), not the strength of the cittas themselves, therefore a stronger citta might be in a weaker position in the vīthi #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • why do ariyas not enter nirodhasamāpatti before death?→ariyapuggalas normally admonish others, informing their attainments and encouraging appamāda before death, therefore they do not attain nirodhasamāpatti at that time; another reason might be to avoid others criticizing the Triple Gem Ariyadhamma Mahāthera thinks that during this era, one who attained Nibbāna would let his sabrahmacarīs know in order to encourage them
          • the arūpajjhānas are developed by {{27672249502204127::refining the saññā which leads to nevasaññānāsaññāyatanajjhāna}}
          • jhānas are sometimes compared to the 8 / 9 directions
          • nirodhasamāpatti cannot be attained by those other than {{4109648100324288::anāgāmīs and arahats}} because {{4109648100324288::they still have latent sensual craving (kāmarāga) as well as the other }}{{4109648100324288::orambhāgiyasaṁyojanas }}{{4109648100324288::(lower fetters), which act as an obstacle to concentration}} this samāpatti is possible only in the{{4109648100324288:: kāma and rūpa}} realms
          • nirodhasamāpatti is nippariyāya (tbc) #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
            • nippariyāya (adj.) [nir + pari + √i + *a]↔literal; actual; real; lit. not going around; 2 non-metaphorical; 3 without distinction or difference
          • why does one attain nirodhasamāpatti?→because it is comparable to the bliss of parinibbāna (avedayitasukha)
          • is asaññasatta the same as nirodhasamāpatti?→in terms of vedayitasukha, yes, it is the same, but not in terms of avedayitasukha, since asaññasatta beings are not free from saṁsaric suffering
          • 2 types of sukha
            • vedayitasukha (happiness which is felt): such as the bliss of sense pleasures and jhānas
            • avedayitasukha (happiness which is not felt): such as the bliss of parinibbāna and nirodhasamāpatti
      • bhedas
        • puggalabheda
          • there are 2 main groups of living beings (puggala)
            • puthujjana (worldlings); 4 types based on paṭisandhi
              • duggati ahetuka (rootless beings in woeful states): born with akusalavipāka upekkhāsahagata santīraṇacitta
              • sugati ahetuka (rootless beings in good destinations); 2 types
                • one born with kusalavipāka upekkhāsahagata santīraṇacitta
                • one born in asaññāsatta realm
                    • IIT - Nissayamuttaka Course
              • dvihetuka (double-rooted beings): born with one of the 4 ñāṇavippayutta mahāvipāka cittas‒2 types
                • one born from a dvihetukaukkaṭṭhakusalakamma
                • one born from a tihetukaomakakusalakamma
                • note: both are born with 4 ñāṇavipayutta mahāvipāka as paṭisandhi, but have some differences in their capacity (what is the difference in their capacity?)
              • tihetuka (triple-rooted beings) (in this lesson it does not include Noble beings, even though they are tihetuka): born with one of the 4 ñāṇasampayutta mahāvipākacittas or 9 mahaggatavipākacittas
            • ariya (nobles); 8 types (all are tihetuka)
              • sekha
                • sotāpattimaggaṭṭha (one who is abiding with the sotāpattimaggacitta (the next cittakkhaṇa he is phalaṭṭha)
                • sotāpattiphalaṭṭha (one who has attained the sotāpattiphala but not the sakadāgāmimagga yet [he is so called until vodānacitta])
                • sakadāgāmimaggaṭṭha (one who is abiding with the sakadāgāmimaggacitta)
                • sakadāgāmiphalaṭṭha (one who has attained the sakadāgāmiphala but not the anāgāmimagga yet)
                • anāgāmimaggaṭṭha (one who is abiding with the anāgāmimaggacitta)
                • anāgāmiphalaṭṭha (one who has attained the anāgāmiphala but not the arahattamagga yet)
                • arahattamaggaṭṭha (one who is abiding with the arahattamaggacitta)
              • asekha
                • arahattaphalaṭṭha (one who has attained the arahatta phala)
              • notes:
                • sekha, in suttanta, can also refer to a puthujjana who is practicing very diligently to attain asap
                • asekha (vuddhipatta asekha) means one who is beyond training or the highest among the trainees ('a' meaning the biggest, largest, highest; normally it is ā)
                  • "na sikkhatīti asekho. sekkhadhamme atikkamma aggaphale ṭhito, tato uttari sikkhitabbābhāvato khīṇāsavo "asekho"ti vuccati"
                • dakkkhiṇavibhaṅgasutta:
                  • when one offers dāna to a maggaṭtha puggala one is most likely offering to 3 types of people: puthujjana, maggaṭṭha and phalaṭṭha; if the dāna starts on the magga moment, then 2 people; if the magga coincides with a bhavaṅga between the vīthis of the donor, then 2 people, puthujjana and phalaṭṭha; it refers to muñcanacetanā mainly
                  • IIT - Nissayamuttaka Course
        • vīthicittas according to puggala
          • there are {{9850484414477942::80}}vīthi cittas, excluding the {{9850484414477942::9 mahaggata vipākas}}
          • max. no. of vīthicittas according to puggala (it follows the 89 system; 9 mahaggatavipākas are not included)
            • duggati ahetuka puggala
              • 12 akusala
              • 17 ahetuka (except hasituppāda)
              • 8 mahākusala
              • total: 37
              • note: 8 mahāvipākas do not arise in akusalavipākabhavaṅga
            • sugati ahetuka puggala (asaññasatta)
              • total: 0
            • sugati ahetuka puggala (avasesa)
              • 12 akusala
              • 17 ahetuka (except hasituppāda)
              • 8 mahākusala
              • 4 ñāṇavippayutta mahāvipāka
              • total: 41
              • note:
                • there are discussions about the 4 ñaṇavippayuttamahāvipāka
                • mem aid: dugati ahetuka (37) + 4 ñaṇavippayutta
            • dvihetuka puggala
              • 12 akusala
              • 17 ahetuka (except hasituppāda)
              • 8 mahākusala
              • 4 ñāṇavippayutta mahāvipāka
              • total: 41
              • mem aid:
                • the same as sugati ahetuka puggala (avasesa)
                • dugati ahetuka (37) + 4 ñāṇavipayutta
            • tihetuka puggala
              • 12 akusala
              • 17 ahetuka (except hasituppāda)
              • 8 mahākusala
              • 8 mahāvipāka
              • 9 mahaggatakusala
              • total: 54
              • note:
                • tihetukas and ariyas who have not attained jhānas do not experience mahaggatacittas
                • lokuttaracittas are not included because they fall under the ariyapuggalas
                • mahaggata vipākas are not included because these are just vīthicittas
            • sotāpattimaggaṭṭha puggala

              • note: all maggaṭṭhapuggalas have only 1, their respective magga
            • sotāpattiphalaṭṭha puggala
              • 7 akusala (except 4 diṭṭhigatasampayutta and vicikicchāsampayutta)
              • 17 ahetuka (except hasituppāda)
              • 8 mahākusala
              • 8 mahāvipāka
              • 9 mahaggatakusala
              • 1 sotāpattiphalacitta
              • total: 50
              • mem aid: tihetuka puggala (54) - 5 (diṭṭhi and vicikicchā) + 1 (sot phala)
              • note: the comm reject the idea that sakadagami can have sex (ven. Mahāsiva thinks it is possible, but Bdgs and Ledi not)
            • sakadāgāmimaggaṭṭha puggala
              • 1 sakadāgāmīmaggacitta
              • total: 1
              • note: all maggaṭṭhapuggalas have only 1, their respective magga
            • sakadāgāmiphalaṭṭha puggala
              • 7 akusala cittas (except 4 diṭṭhigatasampayutta and 1 vicikicchāsampayutta)
              • 17 ahetuka (except hasituppāda)
              • 8 mahākusala
              • 8 mahāvipāka
              • 9 mahaggatakusala
              • 1 sakadāgāmīphalacitta
              • total: 50
              • mem aid: tihetuka (54) - 4 diṭ. - 1 vic. + 1 lokuttara (sk phala)
            • anāgāmimaggaṭṭha puggala
              • 1 anāgāmimaggacitta
              • total: 1
              • note: all maggaṭṭhapuggalas have only 1, their respective magga
            • anāgāmiphalaṭṭha puggala
              • 5 akusala (except 4 diṭṭhigata sampayutta, 1 vicikicchāsampayutta and 2 paṭighasampayutta)
              • 17 ahetuka (except hasituppāda)
              • 8 mahākusala
              • 8 mahāvipāka
              • 9 mahaggatakusala
              • 1 anāgāmiphalacitta
              • total: 48
              • note: tihetuka puggala (54) - 4 diṭṭhi - 2 (dosa) - 1 vicikicchā + 1 anāgāmiphala
            • arahattamaggaṭṭha puggala
              • 1 arahattamaggacitta
              • total: 1
              • note: all maggaṭṭhapuggalas have only 1, their respective magga
            • arahattaphalaṭṭha puggala
              • 18 ahetuka
              • 8 mahākiriya
              • 8 mahāvipāka
              • 9 mahaggatakiriya
              • 1 arahattaphalacitta
              • total: 44
              • note:
                • tihetuka puggala (54) - 12 akusala + 1 hasituppāda + 1 arahattaphala and all kusalas become kiriyā
                • tihetukas and ariyas who have not attained jhānas do not experience mahaggatacittas
            • principles extracted from the enumeration of cittas according to puggala
              • kiriyā javana and appaṇā javanas do not arise in {{2414724585391499::ahetukas and dvihetukas}}
              • the 4 ñāṇasampayutta mahāvipākas do not arise in {{679389334901078::sugati ahetukas and dvihetukas}} (ñaṇasampayutta tadārammaṇas only arise in {{679389334901078::ñāṇasampayutta }}bhavaṅga)
              • the 8 mahāvipākas do not arise in {{8988307758118859::dugati ahetukas}} (mahāvipāka tadārammaṇas only arise in {{8988307758118859::kusalavipāka }}bhavaṅga)
              • kusala or akusala javanas do not arise in {{6198727512776894::arahattaphalaṭṭha}}
              • kiriya javanas do not arise in {{06230351791308841::sekkhas and puthujjanas}}
              • no sekkhas have the {{48831608620716094::4 diṭṭhigatasampayuttacittas and vicikicchāsampayuttacitta}}
              • anāgāmīs do not have {{3590369649208274::2 paṭighasampayuttacittas}}
              • among the sekkhas, the 4 maggaṭṭhabeings only possess {{7377602998379817::their respective maggacitta}}
        • bhūmibheda
          • vīthicittas: bhūmibheda
            • kāmabhūmi
              • all 80 vīthi cittas
              • total: 80
              • note: all 80 may arise because of the presence of all 5 faculties and puggalas
            • rūpabhūmi

          • niraya
            • 8 mahāniraya
              • sañjīva (the hell of revival): here beings keep on living even when cut into pieces and rolled on heated ground; those born here are those who quarreled with intense hatred and conceit, those who hurt the weak and poor and killed animals
              • kāḷasutta (the hell of the carpenter's measuring lines): here beings are tied up and rolled on heated ground; those born here are those who committed crimes against parents, friends and the virtuous
              • saṅghāta (the hell of death / mass): here beings sink into 9 yojanas deep iron ground and remain silent; rocks roll to and fro crushing them; those born here have tortured and killed animals
              • roruva (the hell of intense howling): here beings are burnt from within and without, howling in pain caused by garments that attach themselves to their bodies causing them to burn
              • mahāroruva: here beings are exposed to fire and smoke due to which their blood pours out while they wail
              • tāpana (the scorching hell): here being are burnt alive on a hot iron floor, pinned down with hot iron rods held by tormentors; beings born here have burnt animals alive or burnt down other's houses
              • mahātāpana: beings born here have committed evil deeds with the wrong view that there is no life after death
              • avīci (the hell without gap): here fire is emitted from each of the 6 directions, each reaching the other end; beings here suffer without interruption; there is no space between flames, suffering or beings; beings born here have committed heinous deeds, killed virtuous people, destroyed cetiyas, stolen from the Triple Gem, lied, consumed intoxicants and held wrong views, etc
              • mem aid: saṅjīva (jīva ⇒ kāla), kālasutta (kāla ⇒ kill ⇒ ghāta), saṅghāta, 2 pairs and the obvious

              • paradattūpajīvika: petas who live with what is given by others; they obtain food and beverages by rejoicing in merits shared by others; paradattūpajīvī petas accept merits from their past life relatives and friends

              • nijjhāmataṇhika: petas whose the inside and outside of their bodies are constantly burning
              • kālakañjika: petas with little blood and flesh and with dried up bodies which are about 3 gāvutas in length; their protruding eyes and tiny mouth are placed on top of their heads as in the case of crabs, and must lower the head to consume food; they are also called asuras and together constitute the asurakāya

              • (suññakappa (empty aeon): no Buddhas appear; most common)

              • sārakappa (excellent?): 1 Buddha appears

              • sāramaṇḍakappa (excellent and decorated?): 3 Buddhas appear

        • introduction
          • 2 bhūmis of kamma-vipāka
            • paccuppannabhūmi: understood by ordinary reflection (ānisaṁsa and ādīnava)
              • akusalakamma may lead to happiness, in which case {{3752871900717891::hiri}} should be developed suffering, in which case {{3752871900717891::ottappa}} should be developed kusalakamma may lead to happiness, in which case {{3752871900717891::pīti}} should be developed suffering, in which case {{3752871900717891::khanti}} should be developed
              • note:
                • they may happen in future lives
                • results are not confined to the doer
                • ledi: cetanā, viriya and paññā are the forerunners of kammas that lead to effects in the paccuppannabhūmi
            • anāgatabhūmi: not understood by ordinary reflection (vipāka)
              • akusalakamma always produces suffering, never happiness; kusalakamma always produces happiness, never suffering
              • note:
                • they may happen in the present life as diṭṭhadhammavedanīya
                • results are confined to the doer

              • sujīvaṁ ahirikena, kākasūrena dhaṁsinā, life is light for one without shame, with the bold courage of a crow, pakkhandinā pagabbhena, saṅkiliṭṭhena jīvitaṁ. [244] living a life with backbiting, recklessness, and defilements. hirīmatā ca dujjīvaṁ, niccaṁ sucigavesinā, life is hard when endowed with shame, for the one constantly seeking purity, alīnenāpagabbhena, suddhājīvena passatā. [245] for one sincere, and not reckless, looking for purity of life
              • prmdpn: stages of kammasatti
                • unripe kamma
                  • kiriyā visesa→energy of the kamma that remains after the cetanā vanishes (kammasatti / kammasamaṅgītā)
                  • kammasamaṅgītā
                    • latent kammic force (kammasatti / kiriya visesa) that can produce rebirth; it ends (becomes ahosi) with the attainment of arahatship
                      • Yāva pana arahattaṃ na pāpuṇanti, tāva sabbepi sattā pubbe upacitaṃ vipākārahaṃ kammaṃ sandhāya "kammasamaṅgino"ti vuccanti, esā kammasamaṅgitā. (M-a. IV. 87.).
                    • note:
                      • this is also the nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayasatti
                      • often referred to as atītakamma
                  • upaṭṭhānasamaṅgītā→latent kammic force that becomes active and comes forth to produce results, such as bringing the maraṇāsannanimittas before death; if not interrupted, it produces vipākacittacetasikas and kammajarūpas
                • ripe kamma (pakka / vipāka): kamma appears as vipāka citta cetasikas in the cittasantati
                  • vipākasamaṅgītā
                    • vipākacittacetasikas, the ripen state of kammasatti
                    • here, vipāka does not include kammajarūpas because, though they are an outcome of kamma and are included under vipāka in other places, they do not fit the description of vipāka ‒ vipakkabhāvamāpannānaṃ arūpadhammānametaṃ adhivacanaṃ. (Dhs-a. I. 84.) ‒ which only includes arūpadhammas
          • what does the B refer to when He mentions that kamma is the refuge of beings
            • both types of kammas: those that make effects in the present domain and those that make effects in the future domain because success greatly depends on conduct in the present life, apart from also needing the support of positive kammic forces done in past lives i.e. pubbekatapuññatā
        • 4 kammacatukkas
          • kiccakammacatukka (tetrad of actions based on function)
            • janakakamma (productive action): produces vipāka citta-cetasikas and kammajarūpas during paṭisandhi- and pavatti-kāla
              • paṭisandhikāla↔the uppādakkhaṇa (arising moment) of nāmas and rūpas at the very beginning of each existence
              • pavattikāla↔the period of life from the ṭhitikkhaṇa of the paṭisandhicitta until bhaṅgakkhaṇa of the cuticitta of any given existence (in this lesson cuti is included here but it could be set apart as cutikāla)
              • what is the foremost function performed by a kamma?
                • producing rebirth (janaka function)
                • all kammas are directed to rebirth, but not all have the capacity to produce rebirth, which is only possessed by {{38626922740825353::powerful kammas (mainly }}{{38626922740825353::kammapathas}}{{38626922740825353::)}} ; however, all kammas have the strength to {{38626922740825353::produce results during }}{{38626922740825353::pavatti}}
              • uddhaccasampayuttacitta cannot produce a new life, but can produce results during pavattikāla
              • akusala janaka kamma produces vipākacittacetasikas and kammajarūpa in
                • duggati
                  • 11 akusalacittas (exc. uddhaccasampayutta) produce at paṭisandhi
                  • 12 produce during pavatti
                • sugati (exc. asaññasatta and arūpabhūmi)
                  • 12 akusalacittas produce vipākacittacetasikas during pavatti
                    • in kāmasugatibhūmi: 7 akusalavipākacittas
                    • in 15 rūpabhūmis (exc. asaññasatta): 4 akusalavipākacittas (no ghāna-, jivhā-, and kāya-viññāṇas)
              • kusala janaka kamma
                • duggati: vipākacittacetasikas
                • sugati: vipākacittacetasikas and kammajarūpa
                • magga only produces phalacitta
            • upatthambhakakamma (supportive action): ‒supports a being born of another kamma to live longer by preventing dangers ‒supports another kamma to keep producing results
              • kusala upatthambhaka supporting
                • towards a being born of another kamma
                  • kusala ⇒ duggati / sugati being: by preventing dangers, providing what is required for living (such as food), etc.
                    • confirm if this exists towards duggati being #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • towards a kamma of the same nature
                  • kusala ⇒ another kusala: one kusalakamma that could only produce birth in a poor family may be strengthened by another kusalakamma to give birth in a rich family
              • akusala upatthambhaka supporting
                • a being born of another kamma
                  • akusala ⇒ duggati being: by extending the suffering, influencing one's own or another's mind negatively, affecting utujarūpa causing dangers, etc.
                    • clarify if they only act towards a being / kamma of the same nature or not #q🙋🏼‍♂
                    • clarify 'extending the suffering' #q🙋🏼‍♂
                    • does this mean that the prolongation of life is not always a good result? #q🙋🏼‍♂
                    • expand on what they can do (both ku and aku) #q🙋🏼‍♂
                    • how does akusala upatthambhakakamma act?
                      • they extend the life of certain vinipātika asuras and some other beings who live in bad conditions prolonging their suffering
                  • can it support a sugati being? #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • another kamma of the same nature
                  • akusala ⇒ another akusala: a weak akusalakamma that would cause rebirth in the sphere of petas, being supported by another akusalakamma, may cause rebirth in hell
            • upapīlakakamma (obstructive action): ‒intermittently obstructs a being born of some other kamma, creating obstructive conditions such as sicknesses, enemies, loss of properties, loss of jobs, insults, accusations, and so on such as the case of Ven. Cūlapanthaka ‒obstructs the result of another kamma
              • is there kusala upapīḷakakamma?
                • there is no mention of kusala upapīḷakakamma towards a being, but there is towards another kamma
                • example: Ajātasattu's anantariyakamma was weakened by wholesome deeds done during his life
              • akusala upapīḷaka kamma obstructing
                • a being: creating obstructive conditions
                  • sugati being
                  • duggati being
                • another kamma: obstructing the results of another kamma
                  • aku kamma
                  • ku kamma
              • kusala upapīḷaka kamma obstructing
                • a being: not mentioned
                • another kamma: obstructing the results of another kamma
                  • another ku kamma: (confirm)
                  • aku kamma: Ajātasattu's anantariyakamma that was going to producce result in avīci was weakened by kusalakammas and produced result in a minor hell
              • why here it is mentioned to be intermittent? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • upaghātaka- / upacchedaka-kamma (destructive action): ‒kills a being born of some other kamma without allowing it to live the entire lifespan ‒"kills" another kamma, destroying its capacity to produce rebirth
              • is there kusala upaghātakakamma?
                • mostly, the upaghātaka function towards a living being is performed by akusalakammas, but sometimes kusalakammas too perform this function;
                  • example: devadūtasutta: the recollected kusalakamma kills the hell being (upaghātaka) and brings it to a better destination (janaka)
                • upaghātaka function can also be done by a ku towards other ku / aku kammas
                  • example: jhānakusala overrides other weaker kusalas, magga destroys other ku / aku, etc.
              • do all upaghātakakammas both kill and produce the next rebirth? examples
                • some only kill without producing the next rebirth, while others may do both functions (causing death is upaghātaka function, while producing the rebirth is janaka function)
                • examples: the destructive actions of King Bimbisāra and Queen Sāmāvatī only caused their deaths, while those of Devadatta, Ciñcimāṇavikā and King Mahāpatāpa both killed them and sent them to apāya
              • 3 types of upaghātakakamma
                • maggañāṇa destroying other kammas (kammakkhaya kamma) (isn't it the cetanā?) #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • nīvaraṇa destroying jhāna
                  • what happens to jhānakammas that were overtaken by nīvaraṇa?
                    • the jhānakamma which had gotten the okāsa for giving result but was then overtaken / destroyed by nivaraṇa cannot give result in saṁsāra anymore because it can only produce paṭisandhi, bhavaṅga and cuti vipākas
                      • is this with reference to janaka function only? #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • one kamma can destroy the capacity of another kamma to produce rebirth
              • akusala upaghātaka kamma destroying
                • a being: killing it (upaghātaka) and taking it to apāya (janaka)
                  • sugati being: King Bimbisāra and Queen Sāmāvatī (only upaghātaka), Devadatta, Ciñcimāṇavikā and King Mahāpatāpa (both upaghātaka and janaka)
                    • maybe also Dusī Māra and Devadatta as a Cakkavattirāja (confirm)
                  • duggati being: (find example)
                • another kamma:
                  • another akusala kamma: a heavier anantariyakamma taking the place of a lighter one
                  • another kusala kamma:
                    • nīvaraṇa destroying the jhānakamma that had gotten okāsa
              • kusala upaghātaka kamma destroying
                • a being: killing it (upaghātaka) and taking it to sugati (janaka)
                  • sugati being: (tbc) #q🙋🏼‍♂
                    • what kills devas who attain anāgāmihood / arahatship? #q🙋🏼‍♂
                  • duggati being: devaduttasutta‒the recollected kusalakamma kills the hell being (upaghātaka) and brings it to a better destination (janaka)
                    • it is actually the kusalakamma that kills the hell being? #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • another kamma: destroying its possibilities of producing paṭisandhi
                  • another ku kamma:
                    • maggañāṇa (or is it maggacetanā?) that destroys other kusalakammas (kammakkhayakamma)
                    • a higher jhāna taking the place of a lower one
                  • aku kamma: maggañāṇa (or is it maggacetanā?) destoying akusala janakakammas (kammakkhayakamma)
            • notes: they can all be kusala or akusala
            • notes:
              • can a kamma do any function toward itself?
                • no, only toward a being or another kamma
              • how many functions can one kamma perform?
                • in general terms, one single kamma can perform all 4 functions, but the last 3 functions are only performed towards a being born of another kamma
                • in other words: a kamma that produced paṭisandhi cannot act as upatthambhaka, upapīḷaka or upaghātaka during that particular life (can it do so toward another kamma?) #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • in more detail: only stronger kammas can perform janaka function
              • what kammas perform the functions of upatthambhaka, upapīḷaka and upaghātaka?
                • it is the janakakammas themselves that occasionally perform these functions; they may do so before or even after having produced their results, but not during the life in which they produce paṭisandhi
              • how do kammas affect other kammas?
                • apart from the janaka function, kammas may perform the other 3 functions towards other kammas kusalakammas may be supported by other kusalakammas, weakened by akusalakammas of opposite nature, or destroyed by another kusala or akusalakamma akusalakammas may be supported by other akusalakammas, weakened by kusalakammas of opposite nature, or destroyed by another akusala or kusalakamma
                  • the opposite nature meant here is simply the kusala / akusala nature or a more specific one? #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • how one kamma affects another kamma
                  • kusala ⇒ kusala #q🙋🏼‍♂
                  • kusala ⇒ akusala supportive function: {{6165406244430727::no}} obstructive function: {{6165406244430727::yes, an akusalakamma may be weakened by kusalakammas of opposite nature such as in the case of the King Ajātasattu}} destructive function: {{6165406244430727::yes, a kusalagaruka kamma destroys an akusala kaṭattākamma that had gotten the opportunity and arahattamagga destroys all akusalakammas}}
                  • akusala ⇒ kusala supportive function: {{28550530484103986::no (tbc)}} obstructive function: {{28550530484103986::yes, a kusalakamma that would cause a birth in a rich family may be obstructed causing birth in a poor family}} destructive function: {{28550530484103986::yes, a garuka akusalakamma destroys a kusalakamma that had gotten the opportunity}}
                  • akusala ⇒ akusala obstructive function: {{28550530484103986::yes (example)}} destructive function: {{28550530484103986::yes, a garuka akusalakamma may be destroyed by an even heavier one}}
                  • can the janaka function be performed towards another kamma?→no it cannot, otherwise our actions would be determined by past deeds
                  • isn't the weakening of the akusalakammas of King Ajātasattu an example of kusala performing upapīḷaka function towards an akusalakamma? yes, the upapīḷaka function can be performed by a certain kamma towards another kamma but not by a kusalakamma towards a being
                • what should those who have performed akusalakammas do?→they must perform wholesome deeds that are of the opposite nature to the akusalas they have done as much as possible
                • what is kammakkhayakamma?
                  • cetanā of all 4 maggas
                  • cetanā of arahattamagga
                  • they destroys the potential of wholesome and unwholesome deeds of producing paṭisandhi
              • what happens to kammas that compete before death to produce the next life?
                • before the death moment kammas that are competing to produce the next life affect each other (strengthen or weaken each other)
              • can upatthambhakakamma extend one's life?
                • life itself cannot be extended for even a second, only the obstacles to living the full lifespan removed
              • how can the kammic functions be understood in the scenario in which someone in great need of a rare medicine, receives it, but its taste is awful?
                • how one obtained the rare medicine is kusalakamma performing upatthambhaka function, but while experiencing its bad taste it is akusalakamma performing janaka function producing akusalavipāka jivhāviññāṇa
              • why is kusala abhiññā called kusala if it does not produce results?
                • even though it does not produce results, it is still kusalasaṅkhāra; Ledi: the entire power of the cetanā is used up to perform the supernormal ability; there are other attempts to solve this question
              • can kamma actually be destroyed?
                • kamma can be prevented from giving results, not destroyed; when one kamma destroys another, it only does so with regard to its ability to produce results (janaka function); only niganthas talk about its destruction
              • okāsakata
                • one kamma may give opportunity for another to arise
              • kammas get opportunity to give result based on 4 conditions
                • gati
                  • vipatti (dugati life): in such life, past akusalakammas get opportunity more easily while past kusalakammas are subdued
                  • sampatti (sugati life): in such life, past kusalakammas get opportunity more easily while past akusalakammas are subdued
                • upadhi (appearance)
                  • vipatti: unpleasant appearance
                  • sampatti: pleasant appearance
                • kāla
                  • vippatti: bad rulers and bad natural conditions such as plagues, droughts, floods
                  • sampatti: good rulers and good natural conditions
                • payoga
                  • vipatti: performing unwholesome actions
                  • sampatti: performing wholesome actions
              • 16 types of wisdom of kammavipāka: 2nd bala of the Buddha (get information) #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • pākadānapariyāyakammacatukka (tetrad of actions based on the priority for giving result)
            • garukakamma (weighty action): powerful wholesome or unwholesome kammas that, as soon as they are performed, immediately get the opportunity (okāsa) to produce paṭisandhi
              • kusalagarukakammas
                • 9 samāpattis (5 rūpāvacara and 4 rūpāvacara jhānas)
                • 3 ways the priority of the jhānas to produce the next life can be overcome
                  • by a higher jhāna
                  • by nīvaraṇa
                  • by a wish
                • if jhānas are garukakamma, how are brahmas reborn in deva / human realms?
                  • the wish to be reborn in these realms overcomes the priority of the jhāna
              • akusalagarukakammas
                • 5 ānantariyakammas and niyatāmicchādiṭṭhi
                • note: only happen in the human realm (an animal killing its mother is not garuka) (does this apply to all of them? can't a deva, for ex., have niyatāmicchādiṭṭhi?) #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • can they their priority be overcome?
                  • only by a heavier ānantariyakamma
                • which of them is the worst?
                  • diṭṭhi is the worst, because of the tendency to hold it repeadetly
                • what is considered the worst citta?
                  • is domanassa asaṅkhārika while breaking the saṅgha (wouldn't it be the niyatāmicchādiṭṭhi?) #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • are lokuttara kusala kammas garukakammas?
                • they are never garuka since they do not produce patisandhi
              • extra notes:
                • is giving to family members considered as dāna?
                  • giving to family members is normally not considered as dāna, but it depends on the mindset; it is a maṅgala though (puttadārassa saṅgaho...)
            • āsannakamma (near-death action): the kamma performed or recalled near the time of death‒they have the 2nd priority
              • āsanna is weaker than āciṇṇa, but has priority‒simile
                • like a weak cow, if standing by the door of the cowpen, is able to exit first
              • can incomplete kammas produce paṭisandhi?
                • normally, only kammapatha (complete kammas) produce paṭisandhi, but based on some stories, it seems that incomplete āsannakammas could do so
                • it could be that they just create the atmosphere for another kusalakamma to give result
                • cdvml opinion: it is possible, based on the account of the monk who was attached to the leaf, another monk with regret, and the lady who died on the way to giving a flower to a cetiya
                  • find these stories #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • āciṇṇakamma (habitual action): a kamma performed regularly or performed once but recollected repeatedly for a long period of time‒they have the 3rd priority
              • if done in proximity to death and produces paṭisandhi, it should be considered as {{9316082571419138::āsannakamma (}}{{9316082571419138::why?}}{{9316082571419138::)}}; if it creates the conditions for another āciṇṇakamma to give result, it should be considered as {{9316082571419138::āciṇṇakamma (because if it were āsanna, it would get the priority)}} #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • but what if there was no āsannakamma? then the āciṇṇakamma, even though performed in proximity to death, could have the priority, right? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • kaṭattākamma (complete action): present life kammas that do not belong to the above 3 categories and any past life kammas‒they have the 4th priority to produce paṭisandhi
              • kaṭattākammas in the present life: {{5066081173457706::not garuka, āsanna, or āciṇṇa}} in past lives: {{5066081173457706::any kamma is kaṭattā}}
                • garuka, āsanna and aciṇṇa are always in the present life
                  • can a kamma done in past life become āsanna by recalling it in the present life? #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • according to the kiccakammacatukka, which kamma is the one that is referred to by the pākadānapariyāyakammacatukka?
                • what is mentioned as garuka, āsanna, āciṇṇa, and kaṭattākammas are nothing other than the janaka kammas that will bring forth the following rebirth
              • how can animals come out of apāya?
                • if they have akusala aciṇṇakammas (which they often do), only a kusala āsannakamma may do it
                • if they don't have aciṇṇakammas, a kusalakaṭattākamma from the present / past lives may do it
                • there are arguments over this point
                • can animals recollect an action for a long time? #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • in a way, any kamma is kaṭattā
              • among kaṭattākammas, which one has priority?
                • this is not discussed, but when asaññasatta beings are about to pass away, a dvihetukakamma may get the chance to produce result, what shows that tihetukakammas ‒ which are stronger than dvihetukas ‒ do not necessarily have priority
              • what would happen if kammas could produce result without getting opportunity?
                • it would be impossible to be free from saṁsāra because since kamma cannot be destroyed, their vipākas would arise regardless of other necessary conditions such as craving; the same kamma would give vipāka again and again
              • notes:
                • what is meant by the destruction of kamma?
                  • kamma cannot be destroyed, only its opportunity to give result destroyed, and that is done by removing taṇhā and avijjā
                • 5 akusalakammapathas that can still be done by a sotāpanna
                  • 3 vacīkammas
                    • pisuṇavācā
                    • pharusavācā
                    • samphappalāpa
                  • 2 manokammas
                    • abhijjhā
                    • byāpāda
                  • what is the reason these akusalakammas cannot produce result in apāya? sakkāyadiṭṭhi? why? are they too weak? #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • the main reason for rebirth in duggati is (defilement) {{3738546977843762::sakkāyadiṭṭhi}} the main reson for rebirth in the kāmāvacara realms is (defilement) {{3738546977843762::kāmarāga}} the main reason for rebirth in the rūpa and arūpa realms is (defilement) {{3738546977843762::bhavarāga}}
                  • why is sakkāyadiṭṭhi the main reason for rebirth in duggati? #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • pākakālakammacatukka (tetrad of actions based on the time of ripening)
            • diṭṭhadhammavedanīyakamma (action to be experienced in the present existence): cetanā (1st javana) of a very strong kusala or akusala kamma that produces only ahetukavipākacittas in the same life
                • IIT - Nissayamuttaka Course
              • examples:
                • kusala: Pūṇṇaka Seṭṭhi, Ekasāṭaka brahmin, Sumana the garland maker
                • akusala: King Kalābu, King Mahāpatāpa, and Mittavindaka, etc.
              • is it possible for the cetanā of first javana cittas of ordinary kammas to give results in the same life?
                • mostly, it is those kammas done towards very virtuous people that give results in the same life, but it is possible, yet, in such cases, the results are not known by the person who performed the act
              • which javanas are acting when experiencing results in the same life?
                • the 1st javana, acting as janaka, produces vipākacittacetasikas, but all 7 javanas can act as upatthambhaka producing the supporting results such as food
            • upapajjavedanīyakamma (action to be experienced in the subsequent existence): cetanā (7th javana) that produces results in the succeeding life
              • which javana is the ānantariyakamma?
                • it is the 7th javana, which produces paṭisandhi in the subsequent existence
            • aparāpariyavedanīyakamma (action to be experienced in successive existences): cetanā (5 intermediate javanas) that produces results in any life after the succeeding life (3rd onwards)
              • stronger kammas can produce results for a longer period but take longer to mature
              • they only become ahosi after parinibbāna
            • ahosikamma (defunct action): cetanā (any javana) that has missed all opportunities of giving result
              • when does each javanacetanā become ahosi in terms of janakakicca?
                • the 1st, at the end of the present life
                • the 7th, at the end of the second life (paṭisandhi janaka becomes ahosi when another kamma produces the paṭisandhi)
                • the 5 intermediate ones, at parinibbāna (not in detail)
                • the last 6, can only produce paṭisandhi once, but they can still produce multiple pavatti vipākas
              • 3 types of ahosi
                • patisandhi janaka ahosi
                • pavattijanaka ahosi
                • complete ahosi at parinibbāna
                • note: there are more classifications of ahosi to be studied later
            • note:
              • this is all performing janaka function (only for paṭisandhi?) #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • the stronger the kamma, the longer it lasts, but that does not explain why upapajjavedanīya cannot give results in the present life, or why aparāpariya cannot give results in the present or immediately succeeding life #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • the stronger the kamma, the longer it lasts, but the longer it takes to mature
              • how many vipākas can one single kamma cetanā produce?
                • one kamma cetanā can produce only one paṭisandhivipāka but many pavattivipākas
              • javanas and their strength
                • what is the order of strength of the 7 javanas and why?
                  • 1st (weakest): because it does not have the association of a consciousness of its own nature, only Ma
                  • [||||||||||] 2nd (stronger than 1st): because of the āsevanapaccaya obtained from the 1st, a citta of its own nature
                  • [||||||||||||||||||||]3rd (stronger than 2nd)
                  • [||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||] 4th (the strongest)
                  • [|||||||||||||||||||||||||] 5th (weaker than 4th but stronger than the 3rd): the strength begins to reduce because of cittaniyāma and the law of impermanence
                  • [|||||||||||||||] 6th (weaker than 5th but stronger than the 2nd)
                  • [|||||] 7th (weaker than the 2nd but stronger than the 1st): because even though it gets the support of the previous javana, it is, nonetheless, decaying
                  • note:
                    • the 7th is directly mentioned to be stronger than the 1st and weaker than the 2nd, but the 5th and 6th are not given, only assumed
                    • gotrabhū can only support the appaṇā being in the 3rd or 4th position in the vīthi
                    • the overall strength of a citta and the strength according to the position in the vīthi are different things
                    • why does the strength of the cetanās in the vīthi decline after the 4th javana?
                      • it is not explained, but it follows the law of consciousness and the law of impermanence; otherwise actions would keep on going without being able to change
                    • what are the vipākas of each javana and their temporal scope of result?
                      • 1st javana: {{30320554397336386::only ahetukavipākacittas in the pavatti of the same life}} 7th javana: {{30320554397336386::paṭisandhi and/or pavatti vipākas in the subsequent life}} javanas in between: {{30320554397336386::paṭisandhi and/or pavatti vipākas in any lives after the subsequent life}} note: the stronger the kamma the longer its potency lasts
                    • from the 4th javana onwards, the javana process and the mind process are considered to have fallen: {{5323209505034354::patita}}
              • which kammas strive to give rebirth?
                • every kamma strives to give rebirth (supported by bhavataṇhā), but not every cetanā is strong enough to do so
              • which one gives result more quickly, kusala or akusala? (milindapañhā)
                • (nāgasena:) akusalakamma gives result more quickly in the paccuppannabhūmi; it is not clear if this applies as well to the vipāka function (anāgatabhūmi)
              • when one kamma overrides another, it does so with regard to which functions and which javanas?
                • it does so with regard to the paṭisandhi function of a single javana

              • types of kāmāvacarakusalakamma according to hetu and quality (and which citta it is)
                • tihetukakusalakamma (4 ñāṇasampayutta mahākusala)
                  • ukkaṭṭha (4 cittas)
                    • asaṅkhārika / sasaṅkhārika
                      • somanassa / upekkhā
                  • omaka (4 cittas)
                    • asaṅkhārika / sasaṅkhārika
                      • somanassa / upekkhā
                • dvihetukakusalakamma (4 ñāṇavippayutta mahākusala)

              • 6 factors that influence the kāmāvacarakusalakamma in order of importance
                • hetu (main reason): decides whether it is ti / dvi hetuka; the first being the strongest
                  • eg: dvihetukakamma cannot give tihetuka vipāka
                • 3 factors that determine the omaka or ukkaṭṭha nature
                  • omaka
                    • intention: mean intentions such as to be famous, to demean others, expecting something in return, etc
                    • nīvaraṇa: unwholesome thoughts right before or after the deed
                    • regret: one regrets it after performing the deed
                  • ukkaṭṭha
                    • good intention: without mean intentions
                    • no nīvaraṇa: without unwholesome thoughts
                    • no regret: without regret and rejoicing in the good deed
                • saṅkhāra: decides whether it is a / saasaṅkhārika; the first being the strongest‒mainly determined by present conditions
                  • e.g.: asaṅkhārikakamma may result in sasaṅkhārikavipāka and vice-versa
                • vedanā: decides whether it is somanassa / upekkhā; the first being the strongest‒determined by many conditions such as the quality of the object given or the bhavaṅga
                  • e.g.: somanassasahagatakamma may result in upekkhāsahagatavipāka and vice versa
                • note:
                  • less important factors cannot override the more important ones; e.g.: omaka nature cannot affect the tihetuka nature
              • what is the vedanā, hetu, saṅkhāra, ukkaṭṭha / omaka natures of each of the mahākusalacittas?
                • 1st mku: somanassa, tihetuka, asaṅkhārika, ukkaṭṭha/omaka 2nd mku: somanassa, tihetuka, sasaṅkhārika, ukkaṭṭha/omaka 3rd mku: somanassa, dvihetuka, asaṅkhārika, ukkaṭṭha/omaka 4th mku: somanassa, dvihetuka, sasaṅkhārika, ukkaṭṭha/omaka 5th mku: upekkhā, tihetuka, asaṅkhārika, ukkaṭṭha/omaka 6th mku: upekkhā, tihetuka, sasaṅkhārika, ukkaṭṭha/omaka 7th mku: upekkhā, dvihetuka, asaṅkhārika, ukkaṭṭha/omaka 8th mku: upekkhā, dvihetuka, sasaṅkhārika, ukkaṭṭha/omaka

              • mahaggatakusala
                • powerful cetanā

                • 3rd and 4th jhāna
                  • 3rd jhāna (paṭisandhi and pavatti kāla) hīna: 3rd jh vip and kammajarūpa in the Parittābhā realm majjhima: 3rd jh vip and kammajarūpa in the Appamāṇābhā realm paṇīta: 3rd jh vip and kammajarūpa in the Ābhassarā realm 4th jhāna (paṭisandhi and pavatti kāla) hīna: 4th jh vip and kammajarūpa in the Parittasubhā realm majjhima: 4th jh vip and kammajarūpa in the Appamāṇasubhā realm paṇīta: 4th jh vip and kammajarūpa in the Subhākiṇhā realm
                • 5th jhāna
                  • 5th jhāna (paṭisandhi and pavatti kāla) hīna / majjhima / paṇīta: non-anāgāmī: 5th jh vip and kammajarūpa in the Vehapphala realm through cittavirāgabhāvanā: kammajarūpa in Asaññasatta realm anāgāmīphalaṭṭha with 5th jhāna: prominent saddhā: 5th jh vip and kammajarūpa in the Aviha realm prominent vīriya: 5th jh vip and kammajarūpa in the Atappa realm prominent sati: 5th jh vip and kammajarūpa in the Sudassa realm prominent samādhi: 5th jh vip and kammajarūpa in the Sudassī realm prominent paññā: 5th jh vip and kammajarūpa in the Akaniṭṭha realm
                  • cittavirāgabhāvanā‒summary
                    • some ascetics, who believe in kamma and its results, perceive the disadvantages of having consciousness, saying, "All attachments, dislikes, and ignorance arise from possessing consciousness. None of these troubles exist when there is no consciousness." Contemplating this, they develop the fifth jhāna either with vāyo kasiṇa or ākāsa kasiṇa. Then, they cultivate detachment toward consciousness (cittavirāgabhāvanā). After the attachment to consciousness is fully suppressed, upon their death, they are reborn in the Asaññasatta realm in the posture in which they died in the human realm
