      • calendar studies #edited
        • days and hours
          • a {{7123742167393994::divasa}} (day) is the duration between one dawn to the next and comprises {{7123742167393994::60}}{{7123742167393994:: }}{{7123742167393994::ghaṭikā}} (buddhist hours) with each of them being equivalent to {{7123742167393994::24 minutes}} in modern standards
        • fortnights and months
          • one {{9628323819374938::pakkha}} is the period of fifteen consecutive days either between the full and new moon, or between the new and full moon; the waning period is the {{9628323819374938::kālapakkha}} while the waxing period is the {{9628323819374938::sukkapakkha}}; both together constitute a {{9628323819374938::māsa}} (month); the month commences with {{9628323819374938::kālapakkha}} and concludes with {{9628323819374938::sukkapakkha}}, ensuring that each month concludes with a {{9628323819374938::full}} moon; however, according to the Abhidhānappadīpikā, a month begins with {{9628323819374938::sukkapakkha}} and ends with {{9628323819374938::kālapakkha}} in one year there are {{9628323819374938::18}} pakkhas with 15 days and {{9628323819374938::6}} pakkhas with 14 days
        • seasons
          • in one year there are {{2670845918658269::12}} months 4 months collectively form an {{2670845918658269::utu}} (season) in one year there are 3 seasons: {{2670845918658269::vassāna}} / {{2670845918658269::vassa}} / {{2670845918658269::pāvusa}}(rainy season), {{2670845918658269::hemanta }}(winter) and {{2670845918658269::gimhāna}} / {{2670845918658269::gimha}} / {{2670845918658269::uṇha}} / {{2670845918658269::nidāgha }}(summer) each season can be further divided into 2 smaller seasons known as {{2670845918658269::khuddaka utu}} each small season comprises 2 months totalling 6 small seasons: {{2670845918658269::vassāna}}, {{2670845918658269::sarada}}, {{2670845918658269::hemanta}}, {{2670845918658269::sisira}}, {{2670845918658269::vasanta}}, {{2670845918658269::gimhāna}}
        • names of the months
          • vassāna utu vassānamāsa 1st: first month is called {{35115371467411727::sāvaṇa}} or {{35115371467411727::nikkhamanīya}} 2nd: second month is called {{35115371467411727::poṭṭhapāda}} saradamāsa 3rd: third month is called {{35115371467411727::assayuja}} or {{35115371467411727::pubbakattika}} 4th: fourth month is called {{35115371467411727::kattika}} or {{35115371467411727::pacchimakattika}} hemanta utu hemantamāsa 5th: first month is called {{35115371467411727::māgasira}} 6th: second month is called {{35115371467411727::phussa}} sisiramāsa 7th: third month is called {{35115371467411727::māgha}} 8th: fourth month is called {{35115371467411727::phagguna}} gimhāna utu vasantamāsa 9th: first month is called {{35115371467411727::citta}} or {{35115371467411727::rammaka}} 10th: second month is called {{35115371467411727::vesākha}} gimhānamāsa 11th: third month is called {{35115371467411727::jeṭṭha}} 12th: fourth month is called {{35115371467411727::āsāḷha}} or {{35115371467411727::āsāḷhī}}
        • sun's course
          • during the three small seasons, namely vassāna, sarada, and hemanta, the sun follows the {{3992637552976803::dakkhiṇāyana}}{{3992637552976803:: (southern path)}} during the sisira, vasanta, and gimhāna small seasons, it travels along the {{3992637552976803::uttarāyana }}{{3992637552976803::(northern path)}} A {{3992637552976803::vassa}} (year) is completed when the sun completes its journey along both paths once
          • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
            • saṁvacchara→vassa, saṁvacchara, sarada, hāyana, sama
            • sarada→vassa, saṁvacchara, sarada, hāyana, sama
            • hāyana→vassa, saṁvacchara, sarada, hāyana, sama
            • sama→vassa, saṁvacchara, sarada, hāyana, sama
        • days of the week
          • in ancient pāḷi books, specific names for days within a pakkha are not mentioned; generally, they are denoted using ordinal numbers such as "aṭṭhamī", "cātuddasī", "paṇṇarasī" and so on; however, A. P. Buddhadatta has assigned pāḷi names to the days of the week in the christian calendar as follows: Monday {{6236092112923388::Candavāra (moon)}} Tuesday {{6236092112923388::Kujavāra (Mars)}} Wednesday {{6236092112923388::Budhavāra (Mercury)}} Thursday {{6236092112923388::Guruvāra (Jupiter)}} Friday {{6236092112923388::Sukkavāra (Venus)}} Saturday {{6236092112923388::Sanivāra / Soravāra (Saturn)}} Sunday {{6236092112923388::Ravivāra (Sun)}}
        • moon calendar
          • a lunar year has {{20949196756670085::354 }}days so {{20949196756670085::11}} days a year are lacking every {{20949196756670085::3}} years an extra month is added, normally to {{20949196756670085::āsāḷhīmāsa}} but sometimes to {{20949196756670085::gimhānamāsa}}, but still {{20949196756670085::3}} days are lacking after {{20949196756670085::30}} years adding a month every {{20949196756670085::3}} years, another month is added on the immediately following year, completing a cycle and starting over again {{20949196756670085::year 1 | 2 | 3}}{{20949196756670085::+}}{{20949196756670085:: | 4 | 5 | 6}}{{20949196756670085::+}}{{20949196756670085:: | 7 | 8 | 9}}{{20949196756670085::+}}{{20949196756670085:: | 10... | 27}}{{20949196756670085::+}}{{20949196756670085:: | 28 | 29 | 30}}{{20949196756670085::+}}{{20949196756670085:: | 31}}{{20949196756670085::+}}{{20949196756670085:: | 1 | 2 | 3}}{{20949196756670085::+}}{{20949196756670085::...}}
        • calendar / months (māsa) / seasons (utu) / small seasons (khuddakautu)
    • entrance to vibhaṅga vinaya (part I - continued) #edited
      • saṅghādisesa (continued)
        • duṭṭhadosasikkhāpadaṁ #edited
          • background
            • once the Buddha was residing at {{08747916556942426::the Veḷuvana monastery in Rājagaha}} when Venerable {{08747916556942426::Dabbamallaputta}} who had attained arahanthood at the age of {{08747916556942426::seven}}, decided to {{08747916556942426::arrange dwelling places and coordinate invitations for food offerings for monks (senāsanapaññāpaka)}}; having expressed his intentions the Blessed One praised it and had the Saṅgha officially appoint the venerable as {{08747916556942426::senāsana paññāpaka and bhattuddesaka; }} while he was performing his duties properly, using even the assistence of psychic powers, two monks called {{08747916556942426::Mettiya and Bhummajaka}} belonging to the group of six (chabbaggiya bhikkhus) were not happy with him and intending to expell him (did what?) {{08747916556942426::falsely accused him of a pārājikā offence}}, which was exposed as a lie after investigation; the Buddha then declared a new training rule prohibiting monks from falsely accusing other monks of pārājikā offences
            • 6 chabbaggiyas divided into 3 groups:
              • Rājagaha - the 2 who used to abuse loopholes
                • Mettiya
                • Bhummajaka
              • Sāvatthi - creating new problems
                • Lohita
                • Paṇḍaka
              • Kītāgiri -
                • Assaji
                • Punabbasuka
              • tassapāpiyasika↔monk that has been properly accused of a prjk but does not accept it; fem. (vinaya) verdict of recalcitrance; intractability; lit. according to worse for him
              • Mettiyā bhikkhunī was expelled by the Buddha because {{8933505013052447::she had fallen into prjk}}
          • pāḷi terms
            • codanā↔false accusation by means of speech or body #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • ariyupavāda↔insulting a noble one #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • ariyupahāsa↔making fun of a noble one #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • ariyaparibhāsana↔threatening or hitting a noble one #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
            • codaka↔the bhikkhu who makes the accusation; the accuser #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
            • cūdita↔the bhikkhu who is accused #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
            • suddhasaññā↔the perception that the accused is pure in his virtue with regard to a prjk offense; if one with such saññā makes a false accusation, such accusation is amūlaka #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
            • asuddhasaññā↔the perception that the accused is impure with regard to a prjk offense #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
            • samūlakacodanā↔accusation made with reasonable facts (seen, heard or suspected) when the accuser has asuddhasaññā #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
          • 4 types of codanā (accusation) according to what is stated
            • vatthusandassanena – stating the grounds such as: “You had sex"
            • āpattisandassanena – stating the offense such as “You have committed a prjk offense”
            • saṃvāsapaṭikkhepena - rejecting the communion
              • (not sgds) indirectly accusing such as saying “There won’t be any acts of uposatha, pavāraṇa or saṅghakamma with you” etc.
              • (sgds) directly accusing such as saying “You are not a monk. Therefore, there won’t be any acts of uposatha, pavāraṇa or saṅghakamma with you”
            • sāmīcipaṭikkhepena - rejecting respectful treatment
              • (not sgds) indirectly accusing by not performing sāmīcikamma
                • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
                  • sāmīcikammaṁ (nt.)↔respectful conduct; lit. proper action; such as paying due respect, rising from your seat, saluting with both hands placed together, etc
              • (sgds) directly accusing by statements such as “You are not a monk. Therefore, I will not worship you”
              • note: just saying you are not a monk (assamaṇo) is enough for the full offense
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • sandassanaṁ (nt.)↔instruction, show, pointing out
              • paṭikkhepa (m.) [pati + √khip + *a]↔refusal; rejection; lit. throwing back
          • 3 factors + saññā for an accusation to be amūlakacodanā (baseless accusation)
            • adiṭṭha - not having personally seen the pārājika act, including with dibbacakkhu
            • assuta - not having personally heard the pārājika act, including with dibbasota
            • aparisaṅkita - not having been suspicious of the pārājika act
            • note: even if a bhikkhu has actually committed a prjk, but one has not fulfilled one of these 3 conditions, one entails the full offense if one accuses the bhikkhu
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • aparisaṅkita [na > a + pari + √saṅk + ita]↔pp. not suspected; not doubted; not distrusted
          • offenses according to the intention of the accuser (adhippāya)
            • sgds: cāvanādhippāyena (with the intention of expelling him or disassociating him from the sangha)
              • what is meant by: "or disassociating him from the sangha"? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • not a sgds, but lesser offenses: (not for exam)
              • akkosādhippāya (intention of insulting) (pct)
              • kammādhippaya (intention of making the Saṅgha to do a vinayakamma upon the accused)
              • uṭṭhānādhippāya (intention of rectifying the fault of the accused)
              • uposathaṭṭhapanādhippāya (intention of prohibiting one from participating in the uposatha)
              • pavāraṇaṭṭhapanādhippāya (intention of prohibiting one from participating in the pavāraṇa)
              • anuvijjanādhippāya (intention of investigating a wrong doing of the accused)
              • dhammakathādhippāya (intention of explaining Dhamma)
          • 2 types of codanā according to where it is made and the offense
            • sammukhācodanā (in the presence of the accused): sgds
            • parammukhācodanā (in the absence of the accused, to another): dkṭ
          • this sikkhāpada is (anāṇattika/sāṇattika?) {{6268674345330854::sāṇattika}}
          • when one makes another accuse, if the agent does not have cāvanādhippāya and suddhasaññā it is {{0764264107857402::anāpatti }}{{0764264107857402::(probably because he has fulfilled the }}{{0764264107857402::suta }}{{0764264107857402::condition)}} for the agent; if he adds more information making the accusation his, it is {{0764264107857402::sgds}}
          • is the purity of the accused a mitigating factor?→whether the accused is pure or not is not a mitigating factor, based on this statement, a prjk monk is still somehow considered as a bhikkhu, which has many implications throughout the vinaya
          • if the accused immediately understands: {{8419238321271922::sgds}} if the accused does not immediately understand: not given #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • this sikkhāpada is (a/sacittaka?) {{8103519289065046::sacittaka}}; (a/saññāvimokkha?) {{8103519289065046::saññāvimokkha}}
          • instances of offenses
            • if all factors are present and one accuses a monk of a prjk offense: {{7938741536094038::sgds}} sgds offense: {{7938741536094038::pct}} other offenses: {{7938741536094038::dkṭ}} if the accused is a bhikkhunī: {{7938741536094038::dkṭ}} akkosādhippāyena: {{7938741536094038::pct}}{{7938741536094038:: (under omasavāda)}} parammukhācodanā: {{7938741536094038::dkṭ}}{{7938741536094038:: (regarding any offense)}} samūlakacodanā: {{7938741536094038::anāpatti}} if the accused does not immediately understand the accusation: it is not given performing a vinayakamma upon a monk while the accused is not present in the assembly: {{7938741536094038::dkṭ }}{{7938741536094038::for the monks who perform the kamma}} anokāsa: {{7938741536094038::dkṭ in addition}} (accusing of any offense or misbehavior, samūlaka or amūlaka, without having asked for permission beforehand; it is not necessary for a teacher or during a friendly talk)
          • 6 lies in the sāsana and their offense
            • prjk lie: 4th prjk
            • sgds lie: duṭṭhadosa - falsely accusing a monk of a prjk
            • tlc lie: indirectly lying about one's own attainments, directly lying but not being understood immediately, falsely accusing a monk of a prjk and not being immediately understood
            • pct lie: pc1 (any another)
            • pct lie 2: falsely accusing a monk of a sgds
            • dkṭ lie: falsely accusing of an offense apart from prjk or sgds, falsely accusing a bkī of any offense, lying as a pubbapayoga for the second prjk
            • note: silence is never a lie: in the ptmk it is a dkṭ to remain silent having remembered an offense

        • aññabhāgiyasikkhāpadaṁ #edited
          • background
            • once the Buddha was residing at {{4969228568135087::Rājagaha, Veḷuvana monastery, in Kalandakanivāpa }} when Venerables {{4969228568135087::Mettiya and Bhūmajaka (/Bhummajaka)}} while descending from the mount {{4969228568135087::Gijjhakūṭa}} saw {{4969228568135087::a male goat (chagalaka) and a female goat (ajikā) having sex; }}they decided to name them as {{4969228568135087::Dabbamallaputta and bhikkhunī Mettiyā respectively}}; afterwards, they told other monks what they had seen using those names; the monks who did not believe this accusation, advised the duo not to make such allegations and informed the Buddha of the matter; who then gathered the Saṅgha and questioned the accused, Venerable {{4969228568135087::Dabbamallaputta}}, three times, whether he had committed such act, who replied “{{4969228568135087::Yathā maṁ bhante bhagavā jānāti (The Blessed One knows who I am)}}”; the Buddha then said {{4969228568135087::“Dabba, this issue will not be solved with such type of answers. You need to directly say whether you have committed such an inappropriate act or not”}}; to which the venerable replied, {{4969228568135087::“Bhante, I do not recall having had sex even in a dream, let alone while awake”}}; the Buddha then instructed the Saṅgha to investigate the accusers, Venerables {{4969228568135087::Mettiya and Bhummajaka}}, further; the truth was disclosed and the Buddha promulgated the aññabhāgiya training rule
            • chabbaggiya (group of six) refers to six monks who were very good friends but did not live a virtuous life during the Buddha’s time; all the six monks had {{25086052468228104::1.500}} disciple monks, altogether {{25086052468228104::9.000}}; in Vinaya texts, any member of this large group was referred to as chabbaggiya monks in general
          • pāḷi terms
            • aññabhāgiya↔something other than the accused (something external to the accused)
            • adhikaraṇa↔animate or inanimate object that is the base for the lesa; in this case the goat
            • the goat that was named by the chabbaggiyas as Dabbalamallaputta is an {{040302988648710736::aññabhāgiya adhikaraṇa (an object other than the accused) }}
            • lesa↔attribute, name, pretext; there are 10 types (jāti, nāma, gotta, liṅga...); in this case it is the name "Dabbamallaputta" that was bestowed upon the goat by them
            • aññābhāgiyassa adhikaraṇassa kiñcidesaṁ lesamattaṁ upādāya...(taking the lesa from the third party and accusing) which means that they first gave the name (lesa) Dabba to the goat (aññābhāgiya adhikaraṇa) and then used that lesa to make the accusation
          • 6 aṅga
            • ...bhikkhuṁ...: the accused is generally perceived as being a bhikkhu
              • perceived by the accuser or by others in general? #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • suddhasaññā (the accuser perceives the accused as pure with regard to prjk offenses)
            • amūlakacodanā (being a baseless accusation)
            • aññabhāgiyassa...upādāya...: accusing by taking an attribute (lesa) of an external object (aññabhāgiya adhikaraṇa)
            • appeva nāma...cāveyyān'ti: sammukhācodanā (done in the presence of the accused) cāvanādhippāyena (intended on expelling)
            • the accused understands the accusation immediately
        • saṅghabhedasikkhāpadaṁ #edited
          • background
            • once the Buddha was residing at {{8146421347930963::Rājagaha }}{{8146421347930963::in the }}{{8146421347930963::Veḷuvana }}{{8146421347930963::monastery}} when Venerable {{8146421347930963::Devadatta}} approached monks such as {{8146421347930963::Kokālika}} and proposed to cause a schism in the Saṅgha by requesting 5 things from the Buddha that He would certainly reject, and then use that to conquer people's faith; the 5 things were that all monks always be {{8146421347930963::araññaka }}{{8146421347930963::(forest-dwellers), }}{{8146421347930963::piṇḍapātika }}{{8146421347930963::(alms goers), }}{{8146421347930963::paṁsukūlika }}{{8146421347930963::(rag-robe wearers), }}{{8146421347930963::rukkhamūlika }}{{8146421347930963::(root-of-tree dwellers), }}{{8146421347930963::yāva jīvaṁ macchamaṁsaṁ na khādeyyuṁ}}{{8146421347930963:: (vegetarian)}}; being requested thus the Buddha replied that such practices were optional; the ven. then approach the people and said that the Buddha had declined five types of wholesome practices suggested by him and gained followers; coming to know of his plot the Buddha laid down the saṅghabheda training rule which is intended to {{8146421347930963::prevent the person who is attempting to cause a schism from committing such kamma (saṅghabheda kamma which is an ānantariyakamma) which is a prjk offense}}, by inflicting a saṅghādisesa offence beforehand note: lohituppādakamma is also a prjk offense
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • lūkhapasanna (adj.)↔having confidence in austerity; having faith based on simplicity; pleased by asceticism; lit. pleased by roughness
              • tikoṭiparisuddha↔(adj.) pure in three regards (said of macchamaṁsaṁ)
              • koṭi [√kuṭ + *i]↔card. ten million (10 000 000); 2 point; end point; 3 top, summit
          • pāḷi terms
            • saṅghabheda↔a "broken" saṅgha
            • saṅghabhedaka↔the schismatic monk promoting one of the 18 bhedakaravatthus
            • saṅgharājī↔a "cracked" saṅgha
            • samanubhāsanakamma↔formal vinayakamma performed by the saṅgha to prevent monks from performing wrong deeds
          • 8 steps leading to saṅghabheda
            • vatthu: bringing up one of the 18 bhedakaravatthus
            • intention: heaving the unwholesome intention to promote one's ideals
            • sīmā: doing so within the sīmā where formal acts are performed
            • followers: converting 4 or more monks to accept one's ideals
            • kamma: performing one of the vinayakammas (any of the fourfold vinayakammas)
            • consent: doing so without the consent of at least 4 bhikkhus within the sīmā
            • number: there being at least 9 bhikkhus within the sīmā
            • sides: 4 of them are bhedanuvattakas, the bhedaka himself and at least 4 monks opposing the bheda
            • mem aid:
          • consequences of saṅghabhedakamma
            • the bhedaka is prjk
            • he becomes abhabbapuggala
            • he commits anantariyakamma which certainly leads to avīci hell in his immediately following rebirth; there he certianly suffers until the end of the antarakappa
            • the bhedanuvattakas commit a tlc offense
            • note: as a result of other anantariyakamma it is possible one may be released from avīci before the antarakappa ends, unlike saṅghabheda
          • when the vinayakamma that causes the schism is performed, there must be at least {{8736344398161784::9}} higher ordained bhikkhus within the sīmā: {{8736344398161784::4 }}{{8736344398161784::bhedanuvattakas}}{{8736344398161784::, the }}{{8736344398161784::bhedaka}}{{8736344398161784:: himself and at least 4 }}{{8736344398161784::not bhedanuvattakas}}, a vinayakamma must be performed without the consent of the other bhikkhus otherwise the schism is not effected

            • if one has heard that a schism may occur, one should travel even {{2289912699949086::half a yojanā}} and admonish the schismatic thrice privately, and if necessary thrice amidst the saṅgha; not doing so is {{2289912699949086::dkṭ}} if the bhedaka persists he incurrs a {{2289912699949086::dkṭ}} and the saṅgha must perform{{2289912699949086:: }}{{2289912699949086::samanubhāsanakamma}} on him; by the end of the ñatti, the schismatic incurrs a {{2289912699949086::dkṭ}}, by the end of each of the first two anusāvanas a {{2289912699949086::tlc}}, and by the end (-eyya) of the third anusāvana a {{2289912699949086::sgds }}{{2289912699949086::(the dkṭ and tlc are substituted by the higher offense)}} performing a vinayakamma without the other monks is an offense, but not saṅghabheda the main bhedaka has a {{2289912699949086::sgds}} while his followers have a {{2289912699949086::tlc}}

        • bhedānuvattakasikkhāpadaṁ #edited
          • background
            • once the Buddha was residing at {{18162641707002547::Rājagaha }}{{18162641707002547::in the }}{{18162641707002547::Veḷuvana }}{{18162641707002547::monastery}}; during that time, Venerable {{18162641707002547::Devadatta}} was {{18162641707002547::attempting to cause a }}{{18162641707002547::schism }}{{18162641707002547::in the Saṅgha}}; virtuous ones who favoured the unity of the Saṅgha criticized him, but his friends, such as Venerable {{18162641707002547::Kokālika}}, opposed their criticisms and eulogized his actions; the virtuous ones then criticized them and reported it to the Buddha who then declared the bhedānuvattaka training rule in order to {{18162641707002547::prevent monks from following a schismatic monk}}
          • pāḷi terms
            • saṅghabhedānuvattaka↔bhikkhus who favour a schismatic's idea, who support and praise him and try to increase his alliance
              • 2 types
                • those who do it knowing it is wrong (devadatta's 3 friends)
                • those who do not know it is wrong and were just convinced to follow the schismatic (the other 500 followers)
          • instances of offenses
            • monks once aware of the existence of a schismatic's sympathizers should admonish them thrice in private and if necessary in the presence of the Saṅgha, otherwise they incur a {{38999927924464317::dkṭ}}; if the sympathizers persist they incur a {{38999927924464317::dkṭ}} and the saṅgha must {{38999927924464317::perform }}{{38999927924464317::samanubhāsanakamma }}{{38999927924464317::on them (max. 3 at a time)}}; if they still persist, by the end of the ñatti they incur a {{38999927924464317::dkṭ}}, by the end of each anusāvana a {{38999927924464317::tlc}}, and by the end of the third anusāvana a {{38999927924464317::sgds }}{{38999927924464317::(lesser offenses are replaced by a higher one)}}
          • anāpatti→as sgds 10
          • cattāri aṅgāni
            • adopting the ideas of a schismatic bhikkhu
            • dhammakammena samanubhāsanaṃ (the Saṅgha performs the samanubhāsanakamma in a righteous manner)
            • kammavācāpariyosānaṃ (concluding the recitation of the kammavācā thrice)
            • appaṭinissajjanaṃ (not giving up the intention of following the schismatic)
        • dubbacasikkhāpadaṁ #edited
          • background
            • once the Buddha was residing at {{8594810284354137::Ghositārāma }}{{8594810284354137::in }}{{8594810284354137::Kosambhi}}; during that time, Venerable {{8594810284354137::Channa}} was misbehaving and when admonished would get offended and insult the monks back due to {{8594810284354137::his pride of being a close associate of the bodhisatta even before renunciation as his charioteer}}; monks were disappointed with him and informed the Buddha of his bad behavior and arrogance; the Buddha admonished and advised him and promulgated the dubbaca training rule designed to {{8594810284354137::prevent individuals from being unreceptive to guidance which can hinder their development}}
          • pāḷi terms

          • instances of offenses→as sgds 10

            • yāva tatiyaṁ samanubhāsitabbo: dhammakammena samanubhāsanaṃ (the Saṅgha performs the samanubhāsanakamma in a righteous manner)
            • yāva tatiyaṁ: kammavācāpariyosānaṃ (concluding the recitation of the kammavācā thrice)
            • no ce paṭinissajjeyya: appaṭinissajjanaṁ (not giving up his tenaciousness)
        • kuladūsakasikkhāpadaṁ #edited
          • background
            • once the Buddha was residing at the {{7193962991543492::Jetavana }}{{7193962991543492::monastery in }}{{7193962991543492::Sāvatthi}}; during that time, two monks Venerables {{7193962991543492::Assaji }}{{7193962991543492::and }}{{7193962991543492::Punabbasuka }}{{7193962991543492::and their followers}} were living in {{7193962991543492::Kīṭāgiri}} where they were having improper associations with lay devotees and performing unsuitable acts such as growing flower trees, as well as committing utterly inappropriate acts for monks to do; one day a virtuous monk, after finishing his rains retreat in the county called {{7193962991543492::Kāsī}} was on his way to meet the Buddha, entered the district and went for alms round abiding by the vinaya rules; however, due to associating those monks, lay devotees could not recognize the value of abiding by the Vinaya rules; they criticized the newcomer's behavior and praised the local monks; one wise lay devotee saw the virtuous monk, approached him, asked if he had gotten alms easily, and hearing a negative answer invited the monk to his house and offered him a meal; he then reported the bad behavior of the local monks and requested it to be reported to the Buddha; after doing so the Buddha {{7193962991543492::advised Venerables }}{{7193962991543492::Sāriputta }}{{7193962991543492::and }}{{7193962991543492::Moggallāna }}{{7193962991543492::to go to Kīṭāgiri and perform a }}{{7193962991543492::pabbājanīyakamma }}{{7193962991543492::to all the monks there; with difficulty they did so but the monks were displeased and did not submit to it and instead criticized them back; }}being informed of what had happened the Buddha declared the kuladūsaka training rule prohibiting monks from not submitting to the pabbājanīyakamma that has been done righteously
            • relationship between the laity and the saṅgha
              • the laity is responsible for providing the basic requisites needed by the saṅgha and the saṅgha for providing the laity with the Dhamma; if monks provide the laity with requisites the laity will associate monks for the sake of requisites, favours or improper friendship, causing the laity to lose respect, expect material things from the monks and dwindle in wholesome states while causing the saṅgha to lose support, the monks to be intent on gain, causing the disappearance of the sāsana "{{8505625782263755::agārā anagārāca ubho aññoñña nissitā}}" (householders and renunciants both depend on each other)
              • in the monastery the Buddha always talks first
          • pāḷi terms
            • kuladūsana↔destroying the correct faith of the laity
              • 8 kuladūsana acts
                • pupphadāna – Giving flowers to the laity
                • phaladāna – Giving fruits to the laity
                • cuṇṇadāna – Giving soap powder to the laity
                • mattikādāna – Giving clay to the laity (only in areas where clay is rare)
                • dantakaṭṭhadāna – Giving toothpicks to the laity
                • veḷudāna – Giving cane to the laity
                • vejjakamma – Providing medical services for the laity
                • jaṅghapesanikā – Carrying messages of the laity (between laity)
                • mem aid:
                • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
                  • mattikā (f.) mattika (adj) [√madd + ikā]↔clay; earth; (adj.) maternal, came form mother, belonging to a mother
                  • dantakaṭṭha (nt.) [danta + kaṭṭha]↔tooth stick; stick of medicinal wood for cleaning the teeth
                  • jaṅghapesanika (nt.)↔taking messages by foot; running errands; (m.) who carries messages
                  • jaṅgha (adj.) jaṅghā (f.)↔with calves; (f.) shin; calf; lower leg (from ankle to knee)
            • pāpasamācāra↔engaging in unsuitable acts to please the laity, breaking their correct faith
              • 4 pāpasamācāra
                • mālāvacchaṃ ropeti ropāpeti (planting flowers and getting them planted)
                • mālāvacchaṃ siñcati siñcāpeti (watering flower plants and getting them watered)
                • mālāvacchaṃ ocināti ocināpeti (plucking flowers and getting them plucked)
                • mālāvacchaṃ gantheti ganthāpeti (making garlands and getting them made)
                • they are inappropriate only when done to please the laity; when done for monastic purposes as per rules of Vinaya it is appropriate
                • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
                  • mālāvaccho (m.)↔flowering tree; floral shrub
                  • vaccha (m.)↔tree; shrub; flowering plant
                  • ropeti √ruh↔pr. (+acc) plants; grows; cultivates; lit. causes to grow
                  • gantheti √ganth↔pr. (+acc) ties; bundles; knots; strings together
            • pabbājanīyakamma↔formal vinayakamma performed by the saṅgha on an upasampanna that repeatedly performs unsuitable acts of kuladūsana or pāpasamācāra to prevent him/her from corrupting the faith of the laity; it consists of banishing him/her from dwelling in the same monastery and of going for alms on the same village, as well as imposing certain duties to follow
              • when one (a bhikkhu or bhikkhunī) constantly engages in acts of kuladūsana, the Saṅgha must perform the {{06069610255587565::pabbājanīyakamma}} which is a kamma that consists of {{06069610255587565::preventing one from residing in the monastery in which one engaged on such acts, going for alms in that village, as well as imposing certain duties one must follow}} after the kamma, if the offender remains residing in the same monastery, can the offender go piṇḍapāta in the same village? what about another nearby village? {{06069610255587565::no, the offender is not allowed to go piṇḍapāta on neither of these villages}} after the kamma, can the offender live in another monastery in the same village? what about piṇḍapāta? {{06069610255587565::yes, the offender can reside in another monastery in the same village but cannot go piṇḍapāta on that village, although a nearby village is allowed}}
              • can the offender dwell in another village and go piṇḍapāta on the same corrupted village? #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • steps leading to the full offense
            • one repeatedly commits acts of kuladūsana or pāpasamācāra
            • the saṅgha should perform the pabbājanīyakamma on the offender
            • the offender does not conform to the pabbājanīyakamma and accuses the saṅgha of acting biasedly
            • the saṅgha should admonish the offender in private
            • the saṅgha should admonish the offender in the midst of the saṅgha
            • the saṅgha should perform samanubhāsanakamma on the offender
            • if the offender persist through all these steps the offender incurs the full sgds offense at the end of the third anusāvana
          • instances of offenses
            • committing acts of kuladūsana or pāpasamācāra is {{07645242546134567::dkṭ}} if saṅghika items are given away thinking it is one's own property it is {{07645242546134567::tlc}} if given out of stealing thoughts it is {{07645242546134567::prjk}}{{07645242546134567:: (depending on the value)}} if one does not conform to the pabbajjānīyakamma, accuses the saṅgha of being affected by agati, and after being admoninshed in private persists, it is a {{07645242546134567::dkṭ}} if samanubhāsanakamma is performed, by the end of the ñatti one incurs a {{07645242546134567::dkṭ}}, by the end of each of the first and second anusāvanas a {{07645242546134567::tlc}}, and by the end of the third a {{07645242546134567::sgds}}
              • what is meant by thoughts of one's own superiority? #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • anāpatti→as per sgds 10
          • cattāri aṅgāni
            • chandādīhi pāpanaṁ (stating that the bhikkhus who performed the pabbājanīyakamma did so out of agati)
            • dhammakammena samanubhāsanaṃ (the Saṅgha performs the samanubhāsanakamma in a righteous manner)
            • kammavācāpariyosānaṃ (concluding the recitation of the kammavācā thrice)
            • appaṭinissajjanaṁ (not giving up the claims that the bhikkhus have been affected by agati)
          • note:
            • offenders are not bound to go and confess the offense if they honestly think there are no monks within {{4560051310057238::1/2 yojana}} even concealing a dkṭ is a dkṭ offense according to cūḷavagga (when extending the peyyalas)
    • entrance to vibhaṅga vinaya (part II) - nissaggiya pācittiya #edited
      • introduction #edited
        • what is the purpose of the nissaggiya pācittiya rules?
          • monks should be careful when receiving, preparing and using the 4 requisites and these rules are to avoid inappropriate acts related to these requisites
        • what happens when a N. pācittiya rule is broken?
          • the item related to the training rule becomes a nissaggiya item which is an item that has to be forfeited, in addition to the monk committing a pct offence
        • what is a nissaggiya item / requisite?
          • it is the item related to the NP rule transgressed by a monk which has to be forfeited
        • what is nissajjana?
          • the forfeiture of a nissaggiya item to a single bhikkhu, to a gaṇa, or to the saṅgha, or its abandonment in the midst of the saṅgha as a vinayakamma
        • when purposely transgressing any rule a {{6377387643295387::dosamūla}}citta arises (anādariya)
        • making use of a nissaggiya item prior to the vinayakamma entails a {{38962323968689505::dkṭ}}
        • types of nissaggiya items according to what happens after nissajjana
          • some must be returned to the offender (np1...)
          • some cannot be made use of by the offender
          • some must be forfeited and another object received in return must be used by the offender (np22)
          • gold, silver and currency (rūpiya) accepted by a monk must be relinquished amidst the Saṅgha
        • 3 types of NP rules according to how the object is forfeited
          • bhikkhu / gaṇa / Saṅgha: rules in which the object is forfeited to the Saṅgha, a group of bhikkhus or a single bhikkhu
          • Saṅgha: rules in which the object is forfeited to the Saṅgha
          • Saṅgha majjhe: rules in which the object is forfeited in the midst of the Saṅgha (gold, silver or money) (not to the Saṅgha)
        • most NP rules are (sacittaka / acittaka?) {{3072659713769772::acittaka}}
        • 4 np rules related to asking: {{28441382908885093::np }}{{28441382908885093::6}}{{28441382908885093:: (aññātakaviññatti), }}{{28441382908885093::8}}{{28441382908885093:: (paṭhamaupakkhaṭa), }}{{28441382908885093::9}}{{28441382908885093:: (dutiyaupakkhaṭa) and }}{{28441382908885093::10}}{{28441382908885093:: (rāja)}}

        • np 1 - paṭhamakaṭhinasikkhāpada
          • background
            • while the Buddha was residing at the {{39777304762119137::Gotamaka shrine,}}{{39777304762119137:: }}{{39777304762119137::Vesāli}}{{39777304762119137::,}} He allowed monks to use ticīvara; the {{39777304762119137::chabbaggiyas}}{{39777304762119137:: }}used to visit villages dressed in different sets of three robes; frugal bhikkhus did not appreciate it and reported it to the Buddha who proclaimed: “{{39777304762119137::Yo pana bhikkhu atirekacīvaraṃ dhāreyya nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ}}”; later, ven. {{39777304762119137::Ānanda }}received an additional robe and wished to offer it to ven. Sāriputta who was residing at the city of Sāketa; after inquiring from the Buddha how to proceed he was asked when would ven. Sāriputta return to which he guessed 9 or 10 days; the Buddha then preached: “{{39777304762119137::Anujānāmi bhikkhave dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretuṃ}}” amending the rule
          • description
            • a bhikkhu's robes must be determined ({{028967352911764888::adhiṭṭhāna}}) or their ownership shared ({{028967352911764888::vikappana}}) with one of the five sahadhammikas, otherwise they are considered additional robes ({{028967352911764888::atireka}}{{028967352911764888:: cīvara}}) during a non-cīvarakāla season an atirekacīvara becomes nissaggiya and unfit for use after {{028967352911764888::10 }}days of receiving it; the bhikkhu will also be subject to a {{028967352911764888::pct}} offence
          • size of the robe
            • minumum size for a cloth to be considered a robe: {{3911401532386134::8x4}} sugataṅguli {{3911401532386134::24x12}} majjhimapurisaṅguli / vaḍḍhakī {{3911401532386134::36x18}} pakatipurisaṅguli maximum size: {{3911401532386134::9x6}} sugatavidatthi note: if any one of the dimensions is less then the minimum, the cloth does not qualify as a robe
          • pāḷi terms
            • atirekacīvara↔an adhiṭṭhānūpaga vikappanūpaga cloth that has not been determined nor its ownership shared
            • vikappanūpaga↔a robe fit for vikappana
            • adhiṭṭhānūpaga↔a robe fit for determination
            • adhiṭṭhāna↔the act of determining a suitable cloth as one of the 9 types of robes; the purpose is to increase the sense of responsibility and awareness towards the robes
            • adhiṭṭhita cīvara↔a robe that has been determined
            • vikappana↔the act of sharing ownership of a cloth with any of the pañcasahadhammikas; after one of the owners gives up his share of ownership, the other owner can use it as he likes
            • vikappita cīvara↔a robe of which the ownership has been shared
            • paccuddharaṇa / paccuddhāraṇa↔the act of relinquishing the determination of an adhiṭṭhitacīvara making it an atirekacīvara
              • procedure for paccuddhāraṇa
                • while being apart from the robe: {{962356267303176::considering the place the robe is kept and saying, “}}{{962356267303176::Etaṃ cīvaraṃ paccuddharāmi}}{{962356267303176::” }} while the robe is within hatthapāsa: {{962356267303176::if not in direct contact with the robe by saying, “}}{{962356267303176::Imaṃ cīvaraṃ paccuddharāmi}}{{962356267303176::” if in direct contact merely thinking, “}}{{962356267303176::Imaṃ cīvaraṃ paccuddharāmi}}{{962356267303176::” }}
            • cīvarakālasamaya / kāla samaya
              • the period for making robes which is 1 or 5 months depending on whether the monk has spread the kaṭhina or not; 1 month being from the day after the Assayujapuṇṇamā until the Kattikapuṇṇamā if the kaṭhina was not spread; 5 months being until Phaggunapuṇṇamā if it was spread; this is the period in which most robes are offered and made; if a monk leaves the residence where he observed vassa, and he has neither cīvarapalibodha nor āvāsapalibodha his cīvarakālasamaya ends “cīvarakālasamayo nāma anatthate kathine vassānassa pacchimo māso, atthate kaṭhine pañca māsā.”
            • kaṭhinānisaṁsa↔benefits of kaṭhina (one of them being that monks are allowed to keep atirekacīvaras without having to subject them to adhiṭṭhāna or vikappana before 10 days have elapsed)
            • cīvarapalibodha↔"obstacles related to robes"; a monk has the intention of making a robe; this ends when the monk finishes the robe or at the end of the cīvarakālasamaya
            • āvāsapalibodha↔"obstruction related to dwellings" a monk has the intention of returning to the monastery where he spent the vassa
            • kaṭhinuddhāra↔formal vinayakamma done to suspend the kaṭhinānisaṁsa in occasions allowed by the Buddha
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • palibodha [pari + √rudh + *a] (m.)↔(+dat) obstruction (for); impediment (for); hindrance (for); 2 drawback; disadvantage; lit. obstruction
          • cīvarakālasamaya
            • one who has observed purimikā rains, done the pavāraṇa on the Assayujapuṇṇamā and has cīvara or āvāsa palibodha, receives kaṭhinānisaṃsa from: {{06746287855322541::the day after the Assayujapuṇṇamā until the Kattikapuṇṇamā}} if such monk has spread the kaṭhina, the kaṭhinānisaṁsa is extended until: {{06746287855322541::Phaggunapuṇṇamā (5 months)}}
            • during which period is the paṭhamakaṭhinasikkhāpada applicable?→it is only applicable outside of the cīvarakālasamaya when one does not have kaṭhinānisaṁsa (if kaṭhinuddhāra is done, it is applicable)
            • if one did not spread the kaṭhina is it still called kaṭhinānisaṁsa or just kālasamaya? #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • counting days
            • how should the days be counted here?
              • the days should be counted starting from the dawn of the day one received the cloth; only the days outside of the cīvarakālasamaya are counted, in other words only the days in the akālasamaya are counted here, so the counting can be interrupted during the kālasamaya and resumed afterwards: | 1. {s} | 2. m | 3. t | 4. w | 5. th | 6. f | 7. sa | 8. s | 9. m | 10. t | 11. w | {1.} | 2. | 3. | 4. | kālasamaya | 5. | 6. | 7. | 8. | 9. | 10. | 11. {} = the day the cloth is received | = the 11th dawn in which the offense is committed
          • if any of the following occurs before the 11th dawn breaks, there is no offense
            • if the cloth is adhiṭṭhita
            • if it is vikappita
            • if ownership is lost (it is given away, destroyed or stolen)
            • if it is taken on trust by someone else
            • if it is cut into small pieces that are neither vikappanūpaga nor adhiṭṭhānūpaga
          • aṅgāni (factors)
            • ubbhatasmiṁ kaṭhine: absence of kaṭhinānisaṁsa
            • dasāhaparamaṁ...taṁ atikkāmayato: exceeding the 10 days
            • atirekacīvaraṁ: the robe being an atirekacīvara
              • (at least one robe made with one out of six allowable materials for robes)
              • (the robe being vikappanūpaga)
          • cha cīvarāni: 6 types of allowable robe materials
            • khomaṁ↔linen
            • kappāsikaṁ↔cotton
            • koseyyaṁ↔silk
            • kambalaṁ↔wool / goat hair
            • sāṇaṁ↔Madras hemp / Sunn hemp: cloth woven from hemp thread
            • bhaṅgaṁ↔mixture of various threads
            • 6 extra types of allowable cīvara based on the catumahāpadesa
              • dukūlaṃ: a soft / fine cloth
              • pattuṇṇaṃ: a kind of silk
              • cīnapaṭṭaṃ: Chinese silk
              • somārapaṭṭaṃ: silk from the country of Somāra
              • iddhimayikaṃ: made by psychic powers
              • devadattiyaṃ: given by deities
              • note:
                • catumahāpadesa: Yaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ‘Idaṃ na kappatī’ti appaṭikkhittaṃ tañce akappiyaṃ anulometi, kappiyaṃ paṭibāhati, taṃ vo na kappati. Yaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ‘Idaṃ na kappatī’ti appaṭikkhittaṃ tañce kappiyaṃ anulometi, akappiyaṃ paṭibāhati, taṃ vo kappati. Yaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ‘Idaṃ kappatī’ti ananuññātaṃ tañce akappiyaṃ anulometi, kappiyaṃ paṭibāhati, taṃ vo na kappati. Yaṃ, bhikkhave, mayā ‘Idaṃ kappatī’ti ananuññātaṃ, tañce kappiyaṃ anulometi, akappiyaṃ paṭibāhati, taṃ vo kappatī
            • note:
              • Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, cha cīvarāni – khomaṃ kappāsikaṃ koseyyaṃ kambalaṃ sāṇaṃ bhaṅgaṃ
              • tattha khomanti khomavākehi katasuttaṃ bhaṅganti pāṭekkaṃ vākasuttamevāti eke. Etehi pañcahi missetvā katasuttaṃ pana bhaṅganti veditabbaṃ. (nissaggiyakaṇḍaṃ)
              • sāṇanti sāṇavākasuttaṃ. - Sāṇa is the thread from the bark of hemp
              • Bhaṅganti pāṭekkaṁ vākasuttamevāti eke. Etehi pañcahi missetvā katasuttaṁ pana “bhaṅga”nti veditabbaṁ - Bhaṅga: some say it is just a separate thread from bark. But bhaṅga is to be understood as the thread made by mixing the (other) five.
              • it is suitable to use other types of cloth that are not transparent and can be cut into pieces, sewn and dyed
              • robes should not be made out of {{33196087067263425::hair}}{{33196087067263425::, }}{{33196087067263425::feathers}}{{33196087067263425:: and }}{{33196087067263425::padding material}}
          • nissajjana
            • in the presence of the Saṅgha "{{7220483297728928::idaṃ me, bhante, cīvaraṃ dasāhātikkantaṃ nissaggiyaṃ. Imāhaṃ }}{{7220483297728928::saṅghassa}}{{7220483297728928:: nissajjāmi}}" in the presence of 2 or 3 bhikkhus "{{7220483297728928::i}}{{7220483297728928::daṃ me, bhante, cīvaraṃ dasāhātikkantaṃ nissaggiyaṃ. Imāhaṃ }}{{7220483297728928::āyasmantānaṃ }}{{7220483297728928::nissajjāmi}}" in the presence of a bhikkhu (for final exam) "{{7220483297728928::idaṃ me, bhante, cīvaraṃ dasāhātikkantaṃ nissaggiyaṃ. Imāhaṃ }}{{7220483297728928::āyasmato}}{{7220483297728928:: }}{{7220483297728928::nissajjāmi}}"
          • notes:
            • pacchattharaṇa can be worn if it is of an allowable color, but not by a tecīvarikaṅgika monk
            • what is the purpose of vikappana?→it was allowed to prevent the nissaggiya offenses note: 2 opinions: if one of the shareholders of a robe relinquishes his share the robe becomes atirekacīvara but the comm says it is still vikappana and can be kept and used as one likes
            • can one hint for a kaṭhinacīvara?→kathinacīvara should not be hinted for even to one's parents
            • counting vassa
              • different ways of counting vassa
                • at the beginning of the vassa retreat
                • at the end of the retreat (problematic)
                  • if vassa (seniority) is counted at the end of the vassa, a pacchimika who has ordained before another monk who entered purimikāvassa will be one vassa after his junior
                • at the beginning of the vassāna season (less problematic)
                • at the end of the vassāna season (less problematic)
                • the day of one's higher ordination (less problematic)
              • mgvhr: it is better if the vassa is counted either in the beginning or the end of the vassāna season or on the day of one's ordination
        • np 2 - dutiyakaṭhinasikkhāpada (uddositasikkhāpada)
          • background #editing
            • The Tathāgata was residing one time at the {{2098409862527062::Jetavana temple, Sāvatthi}}. During this period, most bhikkhus were in the habit of leaving their robes with other bhikkhus, and travelling to the many surrounding districts wearing the uttarāsaṅga (upper robe) and antarāvāsaka (inner robe) robes. Those robes that were left behind would become moldy. Having been aware of this situation, the Buddha declared this training rule On another occasion, in the city of {{2098409862527062::Kosambi}}, a bhikkhu became ill. A messenger was sent by his relatives inviting him to be taken care of. The monk stated: “The Buddha has preached that a dawn must not be passed, separated from the three robes. I have fallen ill”. The Buddha who came to know about this proclaimed: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānassa bhikkhuno ticīvarena avippavāsasammutiṃ dātuṃ'' and declared a sub statute as “aññatra bhikkhusammutiyā” allowing monks to stay apart from the three robes if an allowance from the Saṅgha is obtained.
          • description
            • a monk should be responsible of his ticīvara at all times, but specially at night; if unable to be with the robes during the night, at the very least the monk should be with it at the break of dawn, otherwise the robe will become nissaggiya and a pācittiya offense will be committed
          • pāḷi terms
            • ticīvara
              • antaravāsaka (inner robe / under / lower robe)
              • uttarāsaṅga (upper robe)
              • saṅghāṭi (double robe)
              • note: only one set is allowed
              • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
                • āsaṅga (m.) [ā + √sañj + a]↔robe; cloak (s.w/ ā)
                • saṅghāṭi [saṃ + √ghaṭ + *i] (f.)↔outer robe; double robe; patchwork robe; lit. joined together
            • rattivippavāsa
              • being apart from one of the ticīvaras at dawn which is defined by where the monk and the robes are according to the place
            • nivesana
              • a house (under this rule it is outside a village)
            • aruṇa
              • 3 ways in which the day can be measured
                • starting at midnight (present day system)
                • starting at sunrise (astrology)
                • starting at dawn (Vinaya)
              • 2 meanings of aruṇa
                • the pastel red color
                • the rays of light that are visible in the eastern sky at dawn that are of a pastel red color
              • definition in Abhidhānappadīpikā: “sūrassodayato (before the arising of the sun) pubbuṭṭhitaraṃsi (the rays which arose) siyāruṇo''.
              • when does aruṇa occur?
                • about 30 minutes prior to sunrise (sāsanāvataraṇaya gives 1 hour)
                • note: it occurs 5-10 min after the astronomical twilight has begun when the sun is between 18 to 12 degrees below the horizon (Bhante Greece Ñāṇadassana's research)
              • notes:
                • Bhante Greece Ñāṇadassana thinks aruṇa and aruṇūgamana are different things (he thinks one should be able to work with daylight at that time) and decided about 30 min after the aruṇa
                • Galduwa: 30 minutes before sunrise (following Bhante Greece Ñāṇadassana's research) Candawimala: follows 1h before sunrise Pa auk: 40 min before sunrise
                • dawn is considered as if in open space, even if one is in a covered area; rain and clouds do not interfere
                • kañkhāvitaraṇī purāṇatīka says kāla and vikāla is according to jambudīpa
                • making dawn too late can also be a problem for those who undertake duties close to dawn while taking mānatta, so it is better to keep the robes and undertake mānatta before the astronomical dawn
          • rattivippavāsa
            • a bhikkhu should try not to be apart from his ticīvara after dark but must not be apart from them at least at the break of dawn; this rule is only applicable (during which period of the year?) {{34178864830885614::outside of the cīvarakālasamaya}}
            • rattivippavāsa is defined depending on where the bhikkhu and his robes are and those places are four-fold
              • ekūpacāra (one precinct) / parikkhitta (surrounded): all sides of the place are bordered by walls, fences, rivers, moats, etc. (natural or man-made)
                • according to one vinaya expert in mahāvihāra being bordered 3/4 (yebhuyyena) is enough
              • nānūpacāra (multi-precinct) / aparikkhitta (not surrounded): a place that is not bordered as above
              • ekakula (single family)
              • nānākula (multi-families)
            • the hatthapāsa under this rule is {{019340883204146175::2.5 cubits}}
            • places in which nissaggiya could happen
              • gāma, nigama and nagara
                • ekakula: {{2898832467426855::those under a single king or village head (gāma bhojaka; who collects taxes)}} nānākula: {{2898832467426855::those under more than one king or village heads}} ekūpacāra: {{2898832467426855::those with demarcated boundaries}} nānūpacāra: {{2898832467426855::those without decarcated boundaries}}
                • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
                  • gāmabhojaka↔collector of revenues, taxes of a village
                • type of village and how is rattivippavāsa applied
                  • in ekakula ekūpacāra villages ⇒ monk should be {{00042683687457722996::anywhere within the village}} in ekakula nānūpacāra villages ⇒ the monk should be {{00042683687457722996::inside the }}{{00042683687457722996::house}}{{00042683687457722996:: or }}{{00042683687457722996::hatthapāsa }}{{00042683687457722996::from the house (measured from the line made when rain falls from the roof); if not inside a house, }}{{00042683687457722996::hatthapāsa from the robe}}{{00042683687457722996:: (the same as nānākula nānūpacāra)}} in nānākula ekūpacāra villages ⇒ monk should be {{00042683687457722996::within the }}{{00042683687457722996::house }}{{00042683687457722996::or the following places on the }}{{00042683687457722996::same street(s) in order of priority}}{{00042683687457722996::: }}{{00042683687457722996::village hall }}{{00042683687457722996::(where visitors stay overnight)}}{{00042683687457722996::, village gate,}}{{00042683687457722996:: same }}{{00042683687457722996::street, }}{{00042683687457722996::or on another}}{{00042683687457722996:: house }}{{00042683687457722996::(}}{{00042683687457722996::house, hall, gate, street, another house}}{{00042683687457722996::)}} in nānākula nānūpacāra villages ⇒ the monk should be {{00042683687457722996::inside the }}{{00042683687457722996::house}}{{00042683687457722996:: or }}{{00042683687457722996::hatthapāsa }}{{00042683687457722996::from the house (measured from the line made when rain falls from the roof); if not inside a house, }}{{00042683687457722996::hatthapāsa from the robe}}{{00042683687457722996:: (the same as ekakula nānūpacāra)}} summary: {{00042683687457722996::e e > village e n > house / hp n e > house / hall / gate / street / an.house n n > house / hp}} note: hatthapāsa from these places is enough
                    • note:
                      • if the house has more than one street they all streets count as long as there is an entrance to the house from that street
                      • if there is no road, one must stay in the house
                      • the robe can be in any of these places
                      • gist: one should be in a situation where one can easily know what happens to the robe
                • notes:
                  • village is an area decided by the government
                  • licchavi was nānākula; autocracy; 7707 rulers controling in monthly rotation
                  • bimbisara and kosalla kingdoms were ekakula
                  • it seems like most places are nānākula nowadays
              • other locations below (nivesanādi) are only applicable if they are located outside the villages
                • Srd-ṭ. II, 394: Nivesanādīni gāmato bahi sanniviṭṭhāni gahitānīti veditabbaṃ. Antogāme ṭhitānañhi gāmaggahaṇena gahitattā gāmaparihāroyevāti (the one located inside the gāma, gāma includes everything inside the village).
              • nivesana (house outside a village)
                • ekakula: {{9687858548448804::one that belongs to one family (probably nuclear family)}} nānākula: {{9687858548448804::one that belongs to more than one family}} ekūpacāra: {{9687858548448804::one that is surrounded by walls, etc.}} nānūpacāra: {{9687858548448804::one that is not surrounded}}
                  • what if it belongs to a monk? #q🙋🏼‍♂
                • type of nivesana and how is rattivippavāsa applied
                  • ekakula ekūpacāra ⇒ the monk should be {{16139963164942994::in the }}{{16139963164942994::house}} ekakula nānūpacāra ⇒ the monk should be {{16139963164942994::in the }}{{16139963164942994::same room}}{{16139963164942994:: as the robe}} nānākula ekūpacāra ⇒ the monk should be {{16139963164942994::in the }}{{16139963164942994::same room}}{{16139963164942994:: as the robe or at the }}{{16139963164942994::door}}{{16139963164942994:: of the house }} nānākula nānūpacāra ⇒ the monk should be {{16139963164942994::in the }}{{16139963164942994::same room}}{{16139963164942994:: as the robe}} summary: {{16139963164942994::e e > house e n > room n e > room / door n n > room}} note: being hatthapāsa from these places is enough the same principles apply to a vihāra (monastic dwelling outside a village) here the whole building is taken as house
              • khetta (grain field; includes 7 grains; outside a village)
                • ekakula: {{5721579400910168::it belongs to a single family}} nānākula: {{5721579400910168::it belongs to more than one family}} ekūpacāra: {{5721579400910168::enclosed by fences, etc}} nānūpacāra: {{5721579400910168::not enclosed}}
                • type of khetta and how is rattivippavāsa applied
                  • ekakula ekūpacāra ⇒ the monk should be {{08462088235749676::anywhere within the khetta}} ekakula nānūpacāra ⇒ the monk should be {{08462088235749676::hatthapāsa from the robe}} nānākula ekūpacāra ⇒ the monk should be {{08462088235749676::anywhere within the khetta or hatthapāsa from its gate }} nānākula nānūpacāra ⇒ the monk should be {{08462088235749676::hatthapāsa from the robe}} summary: {{08462088235749676::e e > khetta e n > hp n e > khetta / gate n n > hp}} note: the same applies to threshing floors (dhaññakaraṇa), flower gardens (pupphārāma) and orchards (phalārāma)
                    • why is the third more relaxed than the first? #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • vihāra (monastic dwelling outside a village)

                • ekakula: {{004533956169622044::one that belongs to a single family}} nānākula: {{004533956169622044::one that belongs to more than a single family}} ekūpacāra: {{004533956169622044::there is no particular definition}} nānūpacāra: {{004533956169622044::there is no particular definition}}

              • ajjhokāsa (open space outside a village)
                • there is no ekakula, nānākula, ekūpacāra or nānūpacāra here

          • paccuddharaṇa
            • in case a monk is unable to stay with the robes during the night and not even at dawn, as a last resort, what may the monk do?→the determination of the robes can be relinquished making them atirekacīvara
          • ticīvara avippavāsa sammuti
            • permission given by the Saṅgha for a sick monk to stay apart from the three robes while sick; after recovery it is automatically rescinded but if the monk falls sick again it is automatically applicable again
          • perception and intention
            • this sikkhāpada is (sacittaka / acittaka?) {{1762725247772685::acittaka}} and (saññāvimokkha / asaññāvimokkha?) {{1762725247772685::asaññāvimokkha}}

            • ...ticīvarena...: the robe being one of the ticīvara
            • ...aññatra bhikkhu sammutiyā...:not having cīvara avippavāsa sammuti

Imāhaṃ }}{{214878386332795::saṅghassa}}{{214878386332795:: nissajjāmi.}} in the presence of 2 or 3 bhikkhus {{214878386332795::idaṃ me, bhante, cīvaraṃ rattivippavutthaṃ aññatra bhikkhusammutiyā nissaggiyaṃ.
