            • Nissaggiyavatthus become nissaggiya after accepting for {{40550412343321063::one’s own use}}. And the monk commits a {{40550412343321063::pācittiya}} offence for doing so. Accepting them on behalf of others results in a {{40550412343321063::dukkaṭa}} offence. On the other hand, by accepting dukkaṭavatthu for one’s own use or for others, a monk commits a {{40550412343321063::dukkaṭa}} offence. When accepting these unallowable objects, multiple offences occur according to {{40550412343321063::the number of items accepted}}. If any of these objects are collected for safekeeping, outside the monastery or residence of monks, a {{40550412343321063::pācittiya}} offence will be committed through the {{40550412343321063::ratana sikkhāpada}} if a sāmaṇera accepts it for others {{40550412343321063::it doesn't break the rule}}
              • note:
                • this rule is mainly about nissaggiyavatthu
                • 3 ways of accepting + 2
                  • uggaṇheyya: accepting directly
                  • uggaṇhāpeyya: getting another to accept on one's behalf
                  • upanikkhittaṁ sādiyeyya: mentally accepting
                  • taking a discarded object
                  • getting another to take the discarded object on one's behalf
            • rūpiya is offered If a relative or lay sponsor keeps a nissaggiya vatthu closer to a bhikkhu with the intention of donating it, even if the desire is present to accept, {{7273951277263724::it must be rejected by a gesture or by words or at least by thought}} the donor leaves When done so, if the donor leaves the items behind saying (or intending), “I will not take what I have given. These items are yours now,” {{7273951277263724::the items must be left as they are.}} another layperson Subsequently, if another layman comes and asks “What is this Sir?”, the reason must be explained. If he says, “Sir, this must be kept safely. Please let me know a suitable place to keep it,” then the bhikkhu {{7273951277263724::must show a place for safekeeping such as a room, cupboard or a box. }}{{7273951277263724::The bhikkhu must not say, “Keep it here or there}}{{7273951277263724::.”}} safekeeping When the layman keeps it at the place shown, the doors must be closed and money must be kept safely. Such an act will {{7273951277263724::not result in an }}offence. The bhikkhu must not take any of them. He must not get another to take it on his behalf. It is good to inform the kappiya that there is an unallowed object (akappiya vatthu). trader When an appropriate object is brought by a trader and he says, “Sir, take this,” the bhikkhu must say {{7273951277263724::“Friend, we require this, there’s money here also, but, we do not have a kappiya.”}} Hearing this, if the trader says, “I will become your kappiya. Let me know where it is,” the bhikkhu {{7273951277263724::must show him the place. }}{{7273951277263724::He must not say “Take it}}{{7273951277263724::.”}} If the trader takes the sufficient amount for the goods and hands the goods over to the bhikkhu, the monk can accept it. If the trader tries to take more money than the exact value of the good, the bhikkhu should {{7273951277263724::not talk to him about reducing the cost of the goods}}{{7273951277263724::. The bhikkhu must say, “We will not take your goods. You may go.”}}
            • If a devotee offers money saying, “I offer this money for the construction or renovation of the pagoda, monastery or a monastic building,” (the money is not offered to the monk nor saṅgha) the monk should {{17922407958159914::not reject it but should inform the donor's intention to the kappiyas saying, " They are saying so and so"}} candavimala: If not, the monk, without accepting the money by himself, can tell the devotee about the person who is collecting the funds regarding these matters. This is not asking the donor to handover the money to the kappiya but mentioning who is in charge of fund collecting. unknowingly accepting money is {{17922407958159914::also the full offense}}
          • Forfeiture
            • forfeiting in the midst of the Saṅgha A bhikkhu who accepts money, must {{18350945701038146::go to the Saṅgha, wear the uttarāsaṅga properly over one shoulder, worship senior bhikkhus at their feet, squat and keep the money in front of the Saṅgha.}} Then the money must be forfeited in the midst of the Saṅgha (not to the Saṅgha; but the forfeiture sentence say so) saying the following: {{18350945701038146::“Ahaṃ bhante rūpiyaṃ paṭiggahesiṃ, idaṃ me nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ saṃghassa nissajjāmi”}} confession then he should confess the offence (or offences) and a senior bhikkhu must accept the offence. disposing by a layperson If an upāsaka is present, he must be told, {{18350945701038146::“Friend, take this.”}} When he asks, “What should I buy from this?” he must not be told: {{18350945701038146::“Bring this and that particular object.”}} He must be told: {{18350945701038146::“Such and such item is appropriate for bhikkhus.”}} making use of the allowable items Thereafter, if he brings something appropriate like oil or ghee or honey from that money, it should be consumed by {{18350945701038146::all bhikkhus except the bhikkhu who accepted the money}}. Even if the offender receives something from another monk who received it, {{18350945701038146::he must not accept it}}. The light shone by a lamp that is lit from the oil bought from that money is {{18350945701038146::also inappropriate }}for this monk. If this money is used to dig a well or pond, the water that is generated through them is {{18350945701038146::inappropriate}} for this monk. If a bed or chair is bought from that money, such will be {{18350945701038146::inappropriate}} for this bhikkhu. if not smart enough If the layman to whom the money was forfeited is not smart enough to make it useful for the Saṅgha, he must be told to {{18350945701038146::take and dispose of the inappropriate object.}} If he takes away the money without disposing of the object, {{18350945701038146::he must not be stopped}}. if no laymen or the laymen leaves If he just leaves the rūpiya object without taking it, the Saṅgha must {{18350945701038146::appoint one monk to have the money disposed of.}} That monk is called {{18350945701038146::rūpiyachaḍḍaka}}.
            • Disposing by the rūpiyachaḍḍaka has to be done as follows.
              • The bhikkhu must be requested to dispose of the money.
              • Soon after, the following kammavācā must be recited in a vinayakamma.
              • (not for exam) Suṇātu me bhante, saṃgho. Yadi saṃghassa pattakallaṃ saṃgho (itthaṃ nāmaṃ) bhikkhuṃ rūpiyachaḍḍakaṃ sammanneyya, esā ñatti. Suṇātu me bhante, saṃgho. (itthaṃ nāmaṃ) bhikkhuṃ rūpiyachaḍḍakaṃ sammannati. Yassāyasmato khamati. (itthannāmassa) bhikkhuno rūpiyachaḍḍakassa sammuti, so tuṇhassa, yassa nakkhamati so bhāseyya. Sammato saṃghena (itthannāmo) bhikkhu rūpiyachaḍḍako, khamati saṃghassa tasmā tuṇhi. Evametaṃ dhārayāmi.
              • The rūpiyachaḍḍaka monk must then take the money and throw it to deep waters, precipice or jungle where it cannot be found again, closing his eyes
              • note: at present, this is not allowed to be done for currencies as it is against the law
          • Factors
            • jātarūparajataṁ: 1. Being an object of rūpiya: Gold or silver or any type of money
            • uggaṇheyya vā uggaṇhāpeyya vā upanikkhittaṁ vā sādiyeyya: 3. Accepting it, getting it accepted or tacitly accepting without rejecting when offered
              • Being for oneself
        • np 19 - rūpiyasaṃvohārasikkhāpada
          • background
            • The Tathāgata was residing one time at the Jetavana monastery near the city of Sāvatthi. Chabbaggiya monks traded (buying and selling) with various rūpiya items, i.e., gold, silver and money. People started blaming them. Minimalistic bhikkhus informed this to the Buddha. The Buddha in this instance imposed the rūpiyasaṃvohāra training rule.
          • Training rule in Pali
            • Yo pana bhikkhu nānappakārakaṃ rūpiyasaṃvohāraṃ samāpajjeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. If a monk trades with gold or silver or money in various ways, a nissaggiya pācittiya offence will be committed
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • saṃvohāro [saṃ + vi + ava + √har + *a] masc.↔business; trading; dealing ; 2 masc. interacting; transacting; dealing (with); (comm) communicating [saṃ + vi + ava + √har + *a] ✓
          • Description of the training rule
            • This training rule prohibits exchange
          • instances of offenses
            • giving nv, receiving nv, offense: {{6515236003035954::np}} giving nv, receiving dv, offense: {{6515236003035954::np}} giving nv, receiving kv, offense: {{6515236003035954::np}} giving dv, receiving nv, offense: {{6515236003035954::np}} giving dv, receiving dv, offense: {{6515236003035954::dkṭ}} giving dv, receiving kv, offense: {{6515236003035954::dkṭ}} giving kv, receiving nv, offense: {{6515236003035954::np}} giving kv, receiving dv, offense: {{6515236003035954::dkṭ}} giving kv, receiving kv, offense: {{6515236003035954::np20}} {{6515236003035954::mem aid}}{{6515236003035954::: if there is }}{{6515236003035954::nv}}{{6515236003035954:: involved it is a }}{{6515236003035954::np}}{{6515236003035954:: offense otherwise if there is a }}{{6515236003035954::dv}}{{6515236003035954:: involved it is a }}{{6515236003035954::dkṭ }}{{6515236003035954::offense}} nv: nissaggiya vatthu dv: dukkaṭa vatthu kv: kappiya vatthu
              • note:
          • Forfeiture
            • for the trades in which one receives a nissaggiyavatthu the forfeiture is the same as in rūpiyasikkhāpada apart from the sentence being different: "{{0599841888494248::Ahaṃ bhante nānāppakārakaṃ rūpiyasaṃvohāraṃ samāpajjiṃ. Idaṃ me nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ saṃghassa nissajāmi}}. If the received object is a dukkaṭa vatthu or a kappiya vatthu, the offence must be confessed and there is no specific procedure given for their forfeiture (dv such as lakes can be given away to local leaders)
          • Important details related to the training rule
            • following are 5 types of patta received in exchange with rūpiya
              • paṭhamapatta (mahā akappiya patta / 'rūpiya'ayo'patta')
                • procedure: {{3859481629611272::accepting money, buying iron and getting a bowl made}} allowance: {{3859481629611272::not allowed for anyone and cannot be made allowable by any means; anything made from it or with it is also not allowed}}
                • notes:
                  • there are different opinions about this idea in different sub-commentaries saratthadipani: no way for a monk, but any unallowable requisite is given to someone beyond the circle of sahadhammika and kappiya (including relatives), if it comes back it is allowable vimativinodani: no way to make it allowable, it says saratthadipani is wrong
              • dutiyapatta ('rūpiyapatta')
                • procedure: {{9839599526588334::accepting money and buying a bowl}} allowance: {{9839599526588334::not allowed for anyone but can be made allowable by reversing the process (the money is returned to its owner and the bowl to the seller, then it is appropriate for that bhikkhu to get it back again via proper means)}}
              • tatiyapatta ('rūpiya'kappiyavohāra'patta')
                • procedure: {{7660776414284867::accepting money, keeping it with a caretaker, using kappiyavohāra saying "this is good for me" in a shop and the kappiya buying the bowl and offering it to the monk}} allowance: {{7660776414284867::not allowed for anyone but if the money had been properly forfeited beforehand the bowl would be suitable for all sahadhammikas except for the bhikkhu who accepted the money}}
              • catutthapatta ('akappiyavohāra'patta')
                • procedure: {{6366935519075319::in a shop, with a kappiya, using akappiyavohāra saying, "Please, take this money and give me the bowl / Please, take this bowl for me giving this money to the shopkeeper"}} allowance: {{6366935519075319::not allowed for that monk but allowed for other sahadhammikas}}
                • note:
                  • teeling a kappiya to take money for oneself is NP, but to give it to someone else (even if the word used is take but the money is going away) it is a different offense (what offense?) #q🙋🏼‍♂
                  • some ideas say it has to go through a vinayakamma but normally not
              • pañcamapatta (kappiyapatta / 'kappiyavohāra'patta')
                • procedure: {{5628004763239463::in a shop, with a kappiya, using kappiyavohāra saying "This is good for me"}} allowance: {{5628004763239463::allowed to everyone}}
              • it is not allowable for oneself when {{5918677634781169::it was bought with the money one accepted}} it is not allowable for the other sahadhammikas when {{5918677634781169::it was bought with the money that had not been properly forfeited}}
              • to whom each object is allowed:
                • rūpiya accepted, not forfeited, kappiyavohāra: allowed for {{26037609476591683::no one}} rūpiya accepted, not forfeited, akappiyavohāra: allowed for {{26037609476591683::no one}} rūpiya accepted, forfeited, akappiyavohāra: allowed for {{26037609476591683::no one}} rūpiya accepted, forfeited, kappiyavohāra: allowed for {{26037609476591683::other sahadhammikas only}} rūpiya not accepted, akappiyavohāra: allowed for {{26037609476591683::other sahadhammikas only}} rūpiya not accepted, kappiyavohāra: allowed for {{26037609476591683::everyone}}
            • Factors
              • 1. The object that is given or taken being rūpiya
              • 2. Exchanging
          • note:
            • kappiyañca akappiyañca nissāya tiṭṭhati
        • np 20 - kayavikkayasikkhāpada
          • background
            • The Tathāgata was residing one time at the Jetavana temple near the city of Sāvatthi. Venerable Upananda, the Sākyan son was proficient in making robes. One wandering mendicant (paribbājaka) gave a silk shawl to Venerable Upananda and took a beautifully dyed saṅghāṭi from him. Subsequently, the paribbājaka asked for the silk shawl again knowing that the exchange was not profitable to him. However, Upananda Thera did not return the shawl. The mendicant started to bad-mouth bhikkhus. Based on this incident, this training rule was declared.
          • Training rule in Pali
            • Yo pana bhikkhu nānāppakārakaṃ kayavikkayaṃ samāpajjeyya nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. If a monk trades all sorts of allowable objects (exchange allowable requisites for other allowable requisites), a nissaggiya pācittiya offence will be committed
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • kayavikkayaṃ samāpajjeyya→engaging in an exchange by saying: “Take this object and give me that object"; Kaya means to take an object of another. Vikaya means to give in return something that belongs to oneself
          • pāḷi terms
            • saddhādeyya vinipāta↔a monk giving his own belonging to a lay person other than his parents (and other exceptions such as ārāmikas)
          • instances of offenses
            • commanding to exchange (just giving the command): {{004909870981042452::dkṭ}} giving the kappiyavatthu: {{004909870981042452::dkṭ}} taking the other kappiyavatthu in exchange: {{004909870981042452::np}} taking first: {{004909870981042452::dkṭ}} giving later: {{004909870981042452::np}} exchanging kappiyavatthus: {{004909870981042452::np}} exchanging akappiyavatthus: {{004909870981042452::dkṭ or np under np19 (if nv is involved it is a np, if not, a dkṭ)}} exchanging with sahadhammikas: {{004909870981042452::no offense}} exchanging with parents: {{004909870981042452::np}} exchanging with those other than sahadhammikas: {{004909870981042452::np}}
          • relationship between saddhādeyya vinipāta, aññātaka viññatti and kayavikkaya nissaggiya
            • exchanging with parents saddhādeyya vinipāta (imaṁ gaṇhāhi): {{6046216505987065::no offense}} aññātaka viññātti (imaṁ dehi): {{6046216505987065::no offense}} kayavikkayanissaggiya (iminā imaṁ dehi): {{2967792308017996::offense}} exchanging with other ñātakas saddhādeyya vinipāta (imaṁ gaṇhāhi):{{35023026908023547:: offense}} aññātaka viññātti (imaṁ dehi): {{38715347210052675::no offense}} kayavikkayanissaggiya (iminā imaṁ dehi): {{977719962616201::offense}} exchanging with aññātaka saddhādeyya vinipāta: {{6046216505987065::yes}} aññātaka viññātti: {{6046216505987065::yes}} kayavikkayanissaggiya: {{6046216505987065::yes}} exchanging with sahadhammikas saddhādeyya vinipāta: {{6046216505987065::no}} aññātaka viññātti: {{6046216505987065::no}} kayavikkayanissaggiya: {{6046216505987065::no}}
          • exchanging uncooked and cooked rice if the monks says to a man: “We have uncooked rice that we cannot make any use of. Cooked rice however would be useful for us.”, and the man takes the uncooked rice and offers his packet of cooked rice: {{7845342421989352::no offense}} if the monks say: “Give me the cooked rice and take this uncooked rice”: {{7845342421989352::np}} exchanging rice for firewood saying: "eat this and bring firewood in return", the man does so: {{7845342421989352::np as per the number of firewood}} exchanging rice for a service saying: "eat this and sweep the compound": {{7845342421989352::pācittiya offense}}{{7845342421989352:: but there is no object to be forefeited therefore only the confession is to be made (this is the only place where there is pācittiya but no object to forfeit)}} exchanging cloth for a pen saying to a trader: “We have a cloth that is not useful for us. However, a pen would be.”, followed by the trader performing the trade by himself: {{7845342421989352::no offense}} inquiring the value of objects during an exchange: {{7845342421989352::no offense}} realizing the cloth is more valuable the monk must say: “Our cloth is more valuable. Therefore, give the pen to someone else.” At this instance, if the trader gives another object along with the pen to even things out, accepting both: {{7845342421989352::no offense}} if one’s own object is exchanged knowing that it’s not as valuable as the one being exchanged with, it must be noted that it may even result in a prjk offence (if done with a cheating mind)
            • isn't saying "cooked rice would be useful for us" close to aññatakaviññātti? what is the difference here? #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • Factors
            • 1. The exchanged objects, which belongs to oneself and the other party, being kappiya vatthu
            • 2. The exchange being carried out with someone other than the five sahadhammikas
            • 3. Exchanging
          • note: A bhikkhu who is proficient in Vinaya can exchange things without being subjected to an offence.

        • np 21 - pattasikkhāpada #edited
          • background
            • The Tathāgata was residing at the Jetavana monastery near the city of Sāvatthi. At this time, the Chabbaggiya monks used to collect a lot of bowls. People, who visited temples, having seen the collection of bowls, bad-mouthed the monks saying: “These monks are collecting many bowls. Are they trading bowls?” The bhikkhus who heard this, informed the Buddha. Then the Buddha laid down the patta sikkhāpada prohibiting monks from keeping extra bowls. At another time, Venerable Ānanda received an extra bowl. He desired to offer it to Venerable Sāriputta. The latter was residing in Sāketa by then. Venerable Ānanda inquired the Buddha what he should do as the Buddha had barred monks from keeping extra bowls. When asked, the Buddha inquired from Venerable Ānanda: “When will Sāriputta come here?” Ānanda replied; “Sir, in nine or ten days.” Then the Buddha amended the patta sikkhāpada allowing monks to keep extra bowls for ten days.
          • Training rule in pāḷi
            • Dasāhaparamaṃ atirekapatto dhāretabbo. Taṃ atikkāmayato nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. An extra bowl must only be kept for ten days. If that is exceeded the bowl becomes nissaggiya. A pācittiya offence will be committed
          • pāḷi terms
            • atirekapatta↔a bowl that has not been determined or subjected to vikappana
            • adhiṭṭhitapatta↔a bowl that has been determined
            • belt area of the patta↔an area of 2 aṅguli from its rim
          • when a bhikkhu receives a bowl, it must be determined or subjected to vikappana within {{03367198651117742::ten days}}, otherwise: {{03367198651117742::np}} not all bowls received will be subjected to this offence. An offence will only occur if the bowl is {{03367198651117742::of the appropriate }}{{03367198651117742::material}}{{03367198651117742::, }}{{03367198651117742::size}}{{03367198651117742:: and }}{{03367198651117742::burnt }}{{03367198651117742::(for it to be suitable to be determined it has to be properly}}{{03367198651117742:: }}{{03367198651117742::burnt) }} determining a second bowl: {{03367198651117742::the determination is not valid and the second bowl is still atirekapatta}} after nissajjana keeping the atirekapatta for over 10 days: {{03367198651117742::np}} if the adhiṭṭhāna is broken the bowl should be redetermined within 10 days but if not fit for adhiṭṭhāna the days only count after it has been fixed (in case of a hole) using a nissaggiya patta: {{03367198651117742::dkṭ}}
          • nissajjana procedure
            • approach another monk
            • wear the robe over one shoulder, worship the senior (if so), crouch with the bowl in hands
            • nissajjana: “{{48449692168707226::Ayaṃ me, bhante, patto dasāhātikkanto nissaggiyo. Imāhaṃ āyasmato nissajjāmi}}.”
            • forfeit the bowl to the other monk
            • confess the pācittiya offense
            • the other monk says, “Imaṃ pattaṃ āyasmato dammi”, and hands over the bowl back
          • Method of relinquishment and determination
            • paccuddharaṇa for patta within hatthapāsa, in contact with it: “{{1379372512101118::Imaṃ pattaṃ paccuddharāmi}}" (3x) at a distance, thinking of its location: "{{1379372512101118::Etaṁ pattaṁ paccuddharāmi}}" (3x) adhiṭṭhāna for patta being in contact with the bowl: “{{1379372512101118::Imaṃ pattaṃ adhiṭṭhāmi}}" (3x) if at a distance, thinking of its location: "{{1379372512101118::Etaṁ patta adhiṭṭhāmi}}" (3x)
            • 9 reasons due to which the adhiṭṭhāna of a bowl is broken
              • 1. Acchedena / coraharaṇa- If stolen by others
              • 2. Dānena - By giving it to another
              • 3. Vissāsaggāhena - By someone taking out of trust (not tāvakālikaggāha)
              • 4. Vibbhamena - By becoming a layman
              • 5. Maraṇena - Due to death
              • 6. Paccuddharaṇena - By removing the determination
              • 7. Liṅgaparivattanena - Due to sex change
              • 8. Sikkhāpaccakkhānena - By relinquishing the upasampadā
              • 9. Chiddena - Due to a hole big enough for a grain of millet (kaṅgu) to pass below the belt area (2 aṅguli from the rim of the bowl)
                • 7 types of grains
                  • sāli (hill rice)
                  • vīhi (other rice categories)
                  • yava (barley)
                  • godhuma (wheat)
                  • kaṅgu (millet)
                  • varaka (?)
                  • kudrūsaka (finger millet)
              • mem aid:
                • "Acchedadānagāhehi, vibbhamā maraṇuddhaṭā Liṅgasikkhāhi chiddena, pattodhiṭṭhānamujjhati"
              • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
                • vibbhamati [vi + √bham + a + ti]↔pr. leaves monkhood; disrobes; lit. spins /turns away; 2 pr. goes astray
                • ujjhati↔pr. leaves, forsakes
                • uddhaṭa [ud + √dhar + ta] pp.↔pulled out; removed; extracted; 2 pp. raised, lifted

          • vikappana (sharing ownership)
            • 2 method of vikappana
              • sammukhā vikappana; procedure:
                • preliminary steps as in forfeiture
                • say “Imaṃ pattaṃ tuyhaṃ vikappemi.” / plural: “Ime patte tuyhaṃ vikappemi”

                • if the second monk does paccuddhāra: “Mayhaṃ santakaṃ paribhuñja vā vissajjehi vā yathāpaccayaṃ karohi,” and hands it back / plural: "Mayhaṁ santake..."
                • then it can be used as one likes
              • asammukhā vikappana; procedure:
                • preliminary steps as in forfeiture
                • inform the other monk where the bowl is
                • say “Etaṃ pattaṃ tuyhaṃ vikappemi” / plural: "Ete patte..."
          • Factors
            • dasāhaparamaṁ...dhāretabbo taṁ atikkāmayato: Surpassing ten days after having received it
            • atirekapatto: Being an extra bowl
              • The bowl belonging to oneself
              • A bowl that is made out of proper material and size and properly burnt
        • np 22 - ūṇapañcabandhanasikkhāpada #edited
          • background
            • One pot maker invited monks to ask him for bowls if needed. The bhikkhus exceeded their limit and kept asking for more bowls. This made the potter unable to support his family. Seeing this, people started to scold the bhikkhus. Then the Buddha promulgated a rule prohibiting monks from asking for bowls (from aññātaka and appavārita lay devotees) Due to this rule, monks whose bowls were broken went for piṇḍapāta and received alms with their palms. Seeing this, people started to criticise monks saying, “Disciples of the Gotama go for alms and receive food with their palms like ascetics of other religions.” Knowing this, the Buddha amended the rule allowing monks whose bowls are broken to ask for bowls from lay devotees. Subsequently, Chabbaggiya bhikkhus began discarding their bowls due to the slightest scratch and hole, and kept asking for new bowls from the same potter. This made the potter unable to support his family. Seeing this, people started to scold the bhikkhus. Then the Buddha amended the training rule for the second time and promulgated it again as follows.
          • Training rule in Pali
            • Yo pana bhikkhu ūnapañcabandhanena pattena aññaṃ navaṃ pattaṃ cetāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Tena bhikkhunā so patto bhikkhuparisāya nissajitabbo. Yo ca tassā bhikkhuparisāya pattapariyanto so tassa bhikkhuno padātabbo ‘Ayaṃ te bhikkhu, patto yāva bhedanāya dhāretabbo’ ti. Ayaṃ tattha sāmīci. If a monk requests for and receives a new bowl while using a bowl that has not been repaired in five places, such bowl (newly received one) will become nissaggiya. A pācittiya offence will also be committed. This bhikkhu must forfeit the bowl in front of a group of bhikkhus. The final bowl left after the procedure of forfeiture is done, must be given to that bhikkhu saying, “Monk, you must use this bowl till it’s broken”. This is how the training rule must be followed.
          • Description of the training rule
            • the purpose of this training rule is to {{39855350572820214::avoid bhikkhus from requesting aññātaka appavārita donors for new bowls }}{{39855350572820214::when there is no actual need}}
          • pāḷi terms
            • 2 types of patta
              • mattikapatta↔clay bowl
                • ūṇapañcabandhanapatta↔a mattikapatta that has less than five bandhana or bandhanokāsa
                • pañcabandhanapatta↔a mattikapatta that has 5 bandhanas or bandhanokāsas and is not considered a patta (apatta)
                • apatta↔not considered a patta (used for mattikapatta that has 5 or more bandhanas or bandhanokāsas)
              • ayopatta↔an iron / steel bowl
                • akappiyapatta (under this rule)↔ayopatta that is broken beyond repair or that, after repair, remains with an uneven surface that retains food
                • kappiyapatta (under this rule)↔an ayopatta that has an even surface that does not retain food, regardless of whether it is broken or not, as long as it can be fixed
            • bandhana↔a mend which is at least 2 aṅguli long
            • bandhanokāsa↔a crack that should be mended which is at least 2 aṅguli long
            • pattagāhāpaka bhikkhu↔the monk appointed to make others take the forfeited patta
          • counting bandhanas / bandhanokāsas
            • principles: every 2 aṅguli of crack / mend ⇒ 1 bandhana / bandhanokāsa is counted a crack / mend must be at least 2 aṅguli long to be considered as bandhana / bandhanokāsa a crack / mend of less than 2 aṅguli long = {{39757109291825943::not bandhana / bandhanokāsa}} 1 crack / mend of 2 aṅguli = {{39757109291825943::1 bandhana / bandhanokāsa}} 2 cracks / mends of 2 aṅguli = {{39757109291825943::2 bandhana / bandhanokāsa}} 1 crack / mend of 4 aṅguli = {{39757109291825943::2 bandhana / bandhanokāsa}} etc...
            • what is a patta with 4 bandhanas or bandhanokāsas?
              • is a mattikapatta with a crack / mend of 8 aṅguli, 4 cracks / mends of 2 aṅguli, or any combination of cracks / mends amounting to 4 bandhanas total
          • instances of offenses
            • asking for a new bowl from an aññātaka and appavārita lay sponsor while still having an ūṇapañcabandhana patta (only asking): {{47682826537927614::dkṭ}} when the bowl is received: {{47682826537927614::np}} asking while having a pañcabandhanapatta: {{47682826537927614::no offense}} asking while having a kappiya ayopatta: {{47682826537927614::np}} asking while having an akkapiya ayopatta: {{47682826537927614::no offense}} asking for another: {{47682826537927614::not np (which offense?)}} during the forfeiture vinayakamma not taking the forfeited patta for not liking it or for effacement: {{47682826537927614::no offense}} not taking the forfeited patta out of compassion for the offender: {{47682826537927614::dkṭ}} after the forfeiture if the offender uses the bowl he receives from the Saṅgha in a way that it would get damaged or destroyed: {{47682826537927614::dkṭ}} if he gives it away: {{47682826537927614::dkṭ}} if he tries to exchange it with another monk: {{47682826537927614::dkṭ}} if another bhikkhu takes the offender's bowl and gives him his own bowl in exchange: {{47682826537927614::no offense}}
              • asking for another is which offense? #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • nissajjana procedure
            • the offender approaches the Saṅgha with the suitable preliminary steps, all bowls must be brought
            • he forfeits the bowl saying: “{{16058609946807012::Ayaṃ me, bhante, patto ūnapañcabandhanena pattena cetāpito nissaggiyo. Imāhaṃ saṅghassa nissajjāmi}}.”
            • the Saṅgha appoints a pattagāhāpaka bhikkhu
            • the pattagāhāpaka bhikkhu gives the forfeited patta to the most senior monk in the gathering saying, “Sir, may you take this!”
            • if the senior takes the bowl, his own bowl must be given to the second in line
            • if the senior does not take the bowl the pattagāhāpaka bhikkhu should offer it to the next in line of seniority
            • the process must continue until the most junior upasampadā monk either take or pass a bowl
            • finally, the bowl that remains at the end (probably the worst bowl) must be given to the offender saying, "{{41865132277750083::ayaṁ te patto, yāva bhedanāya dhāretabbo}}"
          • aṅgāni
            • ūṇapañcabandhanena pattena: being a clay bowl that has less than five bandhanas or bandhanokāsas, or a kappiya iron bowl
            • being for oneself
            • aññaṁ navaṁ pattaṁ cetāpeyya: Requesting a new bowl
            • receiving a new bowl
          • note:
            • this rule is moslty applicable to mattikapatta
        • np 23 - bhesajjasikkhāpada #edited
          • background
            • The Tathāgata was residing at the Jetavana monastery near the city of Sāvatthi. At this time, Venerable Piḷindavaccha Thera was residing in the city of Rājagaha. One day, with the intention of freeing a poor family who were their attendants the Thera determined and made King Bimbisāra’s palace gold. The people who saw this and were moved by this act offered ghee, fresh butter etc. to Piḷindavaccha Thera. The Thera distributed most of such offerings among the brethren. Some monks stored them in pots and pans. As a result, the dwellings of monks got dirty due to spilling of ghee, butter etc. Moreover, dwellings were overrun with rats. The people who visited the temple seeing this, criticised the bhikkhus’ act. The Buddha, becoming aware of this matter, imposed this training rule.
          • training rule in pāḷi
            • Yāni kho pana tāni gilānānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ paṭisāyanīyāni bhesajjāni, seyyathīdaṃ, sappi, navanītaṃ, telaṃ, madhu, phāṇitaṃ. Tāni paṭiggahetvā sattāhaparamaṃ sannidhikārakaṃ paribhuñjitabbāni, taṃ atikkāmayato, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Medicinal items such as ghee, butter, sesame oil, bee honey and jaggery that should be used by sick bhikkhus must be stored and consumed within seven days of accepting them. If seven days have passed, the bhikkhu will have committed a nissaggiya pācittiya offence
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • paṭisāyanīya [pati + √sāy + anīya]↔ptp. edible; palatable; tasty; delicious; lit. to be tasted
              • sappiṁ nt.↔ghee; clarified butter
              • navanītaṁ nt.↔fresh butter
              • phāṇitaṁ nt. [√phaṇ + *e + ita]↔sugar treacle; jaggery; molasses
          • description
            • pāḷi terms
              • pañcabhesajja↔sappi, navanītaṁ, telaṁ, madhu, phāṇitaṁ
              • kāyika paribhogatthāya↔for applying on the body; does not include using it through the nostrils
              • bāhira paribhogatthāya↔for external purposes such as lighting lamps
              • ajjhoharaṇaṁ↔swallowing, eating, drinking, internal use; including through the nose; it is not clear whether it includes applying it on the eyes or ears
            • instances of offenses
              • keeping the bhesajja past the dawn of the 8th day without finishing it, giving it away, determining it as kāya / bāhira paribhoga or relinquishing it: {{8936402578267744::np}} keeping one vessel of bhesajja for more than 7 days: {{8936402578267744::np}} kapping two vessels of bhesajja for more than 7 days: {{8936402578267744::2 np}} {{8936402578267744::principle}}{{8936402578267744::: the number of vessels determines the number of offenses}}
              • using unoffered oil for ajjhoharaṇa: {{3596469544967864::pc (dantaponasikkhāpada)}} using it as kāyaparibhoga: {{3596469544967864::no offense}} using it as bāhiraparibhoga: {{3596469544967864::no offense}} keeping it for more than 7 days: {{3596469544967864::not nissaggiya}} taking something unoffered and getting it offered: {{3596469544967864::uggahita paṭiggahita dukkaṭa}} using it internally: {{3596469544967864::dkṭ}}
              • mixing yāvakālika / yāmakālika with sattāhakālika / yāvajīvika that have been offered and stored over night (ex.: mixing food / juice with honey / salt from the day before): {{5665108080041406::pc (it makes the mixture to be of the day the sattāhakālika or yāvajīvika was accepted)}} mixing yāvakālika with sattāhakālika / yāvajīvika that were accepted on the same day during the kāla (ex. mixing food and honey received on the same morning): {{5665108080041406::no offense}} mixing yāvakālika with sattāhakālika / yāvajīvika that were accepted during vikāla (ex.: mixing food with honey in the afternoon): {{5665108080041406::pc}} note: only the amount mixed changes nature, not the whole container where it came from
              • oil extracted from yāvajīvika is {{2059855331251068::sattāhakālika}} oil extracted from yāvajīvika offered on the same day can be used for: {{2059855331251068::seven days}} oil extracted from yāvajīvika offered on the previous day can be used for: {{2059855331251068:: six days}} oil extracted from yāvajīvika offered 2 days before, can be used for: {{2059855331251068::five days}} oil extracted from yāvajīvika offered 3 days before, can be used for: {{2059855331251068::four days}} oil extracted from yāvajīvika offered 7 or more days before, for the sake of ajjhoharaṇa: {{2059855331251068::not allowed}} oil extracted from yāvajīvika offered 7 or more days before, for the sake of kāya / bāhira paribhoga: {{2059855331251068::allowed}} {{2059855331251068::principle}}{{2059855331251068::: extracting oil does not change the date it was offered}}
              • using the bhesajja after forfeiture for ajjhoharaṇa: {{16416973823537662::not allowed}} using the bhesajja after forfeiture for kāyaparibhoga: {{16416973823537662::not allowed}} using the bhesajja after forfeiture for bāhiraparibhoga: {{16416973823537662::allowed}} another monk using the bhesajja after forfeiture for ajjhoharaṇa: {{16416973823537662::not allowed}} another monk using the bhesajja after forfeiture for kāyaparibhoga: {{16416973823537662::allowed}} another monk using the bhesajja after forfeiture for bāhiraparibhoga: {{16416973823537662::allowed}}
          • aṅgāṇi
            • bhesajjāni: being one of the pañcabhesajja
              • being a kappiya object
              • not determining it as something to be used for kāyika or bāhira paribhoga
            • sattāhaparamaṃ sannidhikārakaṃ...taṃ atikkāmayato: exceeding the seventh day (breaking of the dawn of the eighth day)
          • nissajjana
            • the offender approaches another monk with the usual preliminary steps
            • he says: “{{348532432658734::Idaṃ me, bhante, bhesajjaṃ sattāhātikkantaṃ nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ āyasmato nissajjāmi}}” and hands over the item to the other monk
            • he confesses the offense
            • is it given back to him? #q🙋🏼‍♂
          • note:
            • mixing does not include, for example, putting avocado juice on a coconut with the flesh, even though the flesh and the juice are in contact it is not considered as mixing
            • only the amount mixed changes nature, not the bottle but because sometimes the spoon goes back into the container some monasteries practice to divide "milk" sugar and normal sugar #q🙋🏼‍♂
            • if something is considered as food anywhere, it should not be taken as medicine (yattha yattha) (opinion)
        • np 24 - vassikasāṭikasikkhāpada #edited
          • background
            • The Tathāgata was residing at the Jetavana monastery near the city of Sāvatthi. The Chabbaggiya bhikkhus went in search of vassikasāṭika (rain robes) well ahead of rainy season saying that the Buddha had recommended vassikasāṭika for bhikkhus. The stitching was done and the robes were used well in advance. Due to have been used in advance, vassikasāṭika robes decayed during the rainy season. As a result, some monks of the Chabbaggiya group took baths naked in open areas. Other bhikkhus started criticising this act. They informed the Tathāgata also. It is then that this training rule was imposed. mem aid: Jetavana, chabbaggiyas procured, made and worn vassikasāṭikacīvaras well before vassāna and the robes decayed during the rainy season, leading them to bathe naked in public
          • training rule in pāḷi
            • ‘Māso seso gimhānanti, bhikkhunā vassikasāṭikacīvaraṃ pariyesitabbam, ‘aḍḍhamāso seso gimhāna’nti, katvā nivāsetabbaṃ. ‘Orena ce māso seso gimhāna’nti, vassikasāṭikacīvaraṃ pariyeseyya, ‘orenaḍḍhamāso seso gimhāna’nti, katvā nivāseyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. Rain robes must be looked for during the last month of the summer. It could be put to use from the last half month of the summer. If one searches for (and obtains) or wears a rain robe before this time frame, a nissaggiya pācittiya offence will be committed.
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • orena [ora + ena]↔ind. (+gen) earlier (than); sooner (than); lit. by low
              • ora [ava > o + ra]↔adj. lower; inferior; 2 nt. this side; this bank; near side
          • description
            • a vassikasāṭikacīvara can be procured (pariyesati) during which period?→from the last month of the gimhāna season (āsāḷhī) to the end of the vassāna season; this 5 month-period is called pariyesanakhetta
            • a vassikasāṭikacīvara can be procured (pariyesati), made (karoti) and worn (nivāseti) during which period?→from the sukkapakkha of āsāḷhī (the last pakkha of the gimhāna season) to the end of the vassāna season; this period is called kāraṇa-nivāsana-khetta
            • a vassikasāṭikacīvara can be determined (adhiṭṭhāti) during which period?→only during the vassāna season
            • note:
              • there is a disagreement about the word karaṇa
          • pāḷi terms
            • vassikasāṭikacīvaraṁ↔rain-robe
            • catubiddhaṁ khettaṁ
              • pariyesana khetta↔the period in which vassikasāṭika can be procured which lasts for 5 months (from āsāḷhī to the end of the rainy season) (Māso seso gimhānan'ti bhikkhunā vassikasāṭikacīvaraṃ pariyesitabbam)
              • nivāsana khetta↔the period in which vassikasāṭika can be worn which lasts for 4 1/2 months (the sukkapakkha of āsāḷhī and the rainy season) it is identical with the kāraṇa khetta
              • kāraṇa khetta↔the period in which vassikasāṭika can be made which lasts for 4 1/2 months (the sukkapakkha of āsāḷhī and the rainy season) it is identical with the nivāsana khetta
                • kāraṇa nivāsana khetta↔the period in which vassikasāṭika can be made, and worn which lasts for 4 1/2 months (the last pakkha of āsāḷhī and the rainy season) (aḍḍhamāso seso gimhānan'ti katvā nivāsetabbaṃ); during this period it can also be procured (pariyesana)
              • adhiṭṭhāna khetta↔the period in which vassikasāṭika can be determined which is the 4 months of vassāna, outside of which it is normally kept under vikappana but this requirement changes if a kaṭhina was spread and due to other allowances
            • paṭilābho (masc.) [pati + √labh + *a]↔(+gen) obtaining (of); acquiring (of); gaining (of); personal acquisition (of)
            • paridahita↔pp. put on, clothed, dressed oneself
          • instances of offenses
            • if the robe is kept beyond 10 days without determining it or sharing its ownership: {{01210394145972038::np1}} if received 10 days before vassāna season, it must be made and determined: {{01210394145972038::on the day the rainy season starts}} if received during the vassāna season, it must be made and determined: {{01210394145972038::within 10 days}} if it takes more than that to be made, it must be determined: {{01210394145972038::on the very same day it is completed}} if procured and received before the āsāḷhī: {{01210394145972038::np}} if worn before the last pakkha of āsāḷhī (sukkapakkha): {{01210394145972038::np}} if procured and received mistakenly thinking it to be the right time: {{01210394145972038::np}}
            • np24 apply in two ways
              • for paṭilābha (receiving) it due to pariyesana (searching) outside the pariyesanakhetta
              • for nivāsana (wearing) it outside the kāraṇa-nivāsana-khetta
            • this training rule is (sacittaka / acittaka?) {{2626957782979973::acittaka}} and (saññāvimokkha / nosaññāvimokkha?) {{2626957782979973::nosaññāvimokkha}}
          • aṅgāni (in two ways)
            • paṭilābha due to pariyesana
              • it being for oneself
              • orena ce māso seso gimhānan'ti vassikasāṭikacīvaraṃ pariyeseyya: seeking it outside the pariyesanakhetta
              • receiving the rain robe
            • nivāsana
              • having robes to wear and cover
              • there being no allowed reasons to wear it, such as dangers and so on
              • vassikasāṭikacīvaraṁ: being a rain robe that belongs to oneself
              • orenaḍḍhamāso seso gimhānan'ti katvā nivāseyya: wearing it before the stipulated time period (before the sukkapakkha of āsaḷhī)
          • nissajjana
            • Idaṃ me, bhante, vassikasāṭikacīvaraṃ atirekamāse sese gimhāne pariyiṭṭhaṃ atirekaddhamāse sese gimhāne katvā paridahitaṃ nissaggiyaṃ, imāhaṃ āyasmato nissajjāmi
          • note
        • np 25 - cīvaraacchindanasikkhāpada #edited
          • background
            • The Tathāgata was residing at the Jetavana monastery near the city of Sāvatthi. Venerable Upananda, said the following to a student monk (saddhivihārika) of his brother who was also a monk: “Friend, come; I will be travelling in the countryside.” Then he replies: “Sir! My robes are weak. Therefore, I’m not going.” Then Venerable Upananda asked him to join in his journey saying, “Come with me, Friend. I shall give you a robe.” This bhikkhu (student of Venerable Upananda’s brother) then heard that the Buddha was also travelling at the same time in the countryside. Therefore, he did not travel with Upananda Thera. This made Venerable Upananda very angry, and he took away the robe that he gave that particular monk. The Buddha who came to know about this incident, imposed this training rule. mem aid: Jetavana Upananda Thera gave another monk a robe for them to travel together but after the monk changed his mind deciding to travel with the Buddha, Upananda Thera got angry and snatched the robe back
          • training rule in pāḷi
            • Yo pana bhikkhu bhikkhussa sāmaṃ cīvaraṃ datvā kupito anattamano acchindeyya vā acchindāpeyya vā, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. If a bhikkhu gives a robe to another bhikkhu, and later on, takes it back or gets someone else to take it back forcefully, out of dissatisfaction and anger, a nissaggiya pācittiya offence will be committed.
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • sāmaṃ↔ind. oneself; by oneself; for oneself; 2 ind. individually; personally
              • acchindati [ā + √chid + ṃa + ti]↔pr. (+acc) takes back; snatches back; tears away; 2 pr. breaks off
          • description
            • instances of offenses
              • ordering the robe to be given back / ordering another to take the robe back (only the order): {{4844365786328433::dkṭ}} snatching back angrily a robe one gave another: {{4844365786328433::np}} the number of offenses depends on: {{4844365786328433::the number of robes snatched back}} snatching back another type of parikkhāra other than a vikappanūpagacīvara: {{4844365786328433::dkṭ for ordering and dkṭ when getting it}} snatching back a robe or any other parikkhāra from an anupasampanna: {{4844365786328433::dkṭ for ordering and dkṭ when getting it}} if one expresses one's dissatisfaction and the other gives it back, angrily or not: {{4844365786328433::no offense}}
          • aṅgāni
            • bhikkhussa sāmaṁ...datvā: giving by oneself to a bhikkhu
            • cīvaraṁ: being a vikappanūpaga robe
            • sakasaññā: the perception of it being one's own
            • kupito anattamano acchindeyya vā acchindāpeyya vā: taking it back by oneself or through another person out of an angry mind
          • forfeiture
            • Idaṃ me, bhante, cīvaraṃ bhikkhussa sāmaṃ datvā acchinnaṃ nissaggiyaṃ. Imāhaṃ āyasmato nissajjāmi.
        • np 26 - suttaviññattisikkhāpada #edited
          • background
            • The Tathāgata was residing at the Veḷuvana monastery in the city of Rājagaha. Chabbaggiya bhikkhus requested for a lot of thread during the cīvara kāla period. Once the robes were completed most of the thread was leftover. Then those same monks asked for thread again, and got more robes done. This was repeatedly done a second and third time. This resulted in the criticism of bhikkhus by the general public. Based on this incident, this training rule was declared. mem aid: Veḷuvana, Rājagaha the Chabbaggiyas, during the cīvarakālasamaya, asked for more thread than they needed three times leading to a lot of leftovers they were criticized
          • training rule in pāḷi
            • Yo pana bhikkhu sāmaṃ suttaṃ viññāpetvā tantavāyehi cīvaraṃ vāyāpeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. If a bhikkhu gets a robe woven by an unrelated and appavārita cloth-weaver using the thread requested by himself, he will be committing a nissaggiya pācittiya offence.
          • description
            • purpose→to prevent the weaving of robes by aññātaka and appavārita cloth-weavers (tantavāya) using thread requested from aññātaka and appavārita lay devotees
          • pāḷi terms
            • suttaṁ [√siv + ta] nt.↔thread; string
              • akappiyasutta↔thread acquired by requesting an aññātaka appavārita dāyaka
              • kappiyasutta
                • thread acquired by requesting a ñātaka dāyaka,
                • thread acquired by requesting a pavārita dāyaka,
                • thread collected as paṃsukūla,
                • or thread acquired by converting one’s own wealth following Vinaya procedures
            • tantavāya [tanta + vāya] masc.↔weaver; cloth maker; lit. weaving thread
              • kappiyatantavāya
                • ñātaka tantavāya
                • a pavārita tantavāya that has invited the monk to ask for weaving a robe or his needs
                • 'volunteer'-tantavāya: the tantavāya that willingly offers to weave a robe when the monk has requested saying, “Help me weave a robe / give me help”, etc

        • np 27 - mahāpesakārasikkhāpada #edited
          • background
            • The Tathāgata was residing at the Jetavana monastery near the city of Sāvatthi. One man ready to leave for a different region said as follows to his wife: “Collect some thread and order that particular cloth-weaver to prepare a robe and keep it. I’m hoping to offer it to Venerable Upananda.” A monk who was travelling for alms heard this and informed Venerable Upananda about the gain he is going to get in future. Venerable Upananda then went to the cloth-weaver and instructed him to make the robe longer and broader. The weaver went to the wife of the donor and asked for more thread. Then the wife of the donor gave the weaver another portion of thread that was equal to what was given earlier. The aforementioned man once back at home, got to know the news about the robe, and offered the robe to Upananda Thera. However, he criticised the act of Venerable Upananda for instructing to enlarge the robe. The Buddha who came to know this matter, declared this training rule. mem aid: Jetavana a man, before travelling, arranged for a robe to be weaved and kept intending to offer it to āyasmā Upananda later the ven. got wind of it and asked the weaver for a longer and broader robe who then asked for more thread from the family the donor offered the robe but criticized the thera
          • training rule in pāḷi
            • Bhikkhuṃ paneva uddissa aññātako gahapati vā gahapatānī vā tantavāyehi cīvaraṃ vāyāpeyya, tatra ce so bhikkhu pubbe appavārito tantavāye upasaṅkamitvā cīvare vikappaṃ āpajjeyya, ‘Idaṃ kho, āvuso, cīvaraṃ maṃ uddissa viyyati, āyatañca karotha, vitthatañca, appitañca suvītañca suppavāyitañca suvilekhitañca suvitacchitañca karotha, appeva nāma mayampi āyasmantānaṃ kiñcimattaṃ anupadajjeyyāmā’ ti. Evañca so bhikkhu vatvā kiñcimattaṃ anupadajjeyya antamaso piṇḍapātamattampi, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. An unrelated male or female householder gets a robe woven by a cloth-weaver for a particular bhikkhu. Even before the lay sponsor asked for instructions from the monk on how to make the robe, that bhikkhu goes up to the cloth-weaver and orders: “This robe is being woven for me. Therefore, make it longer, broader, lay the thread in such a way to make it thicker, lay the thread evenly, weave the centre of the robe well. We will give you something in return”, and offers alms at the very least. This results in a nissaggiya pācittiya offence.
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]

              • vitthata [vi + √thar + ta]↔adj. wide; extended; broad
              • appita [√ar + *āpe + ita]↔adj. thick; firm; dense; solid
              • suvīta [su + √ve + ita]↔adj. well woven; (comm) evenly woven
              • suppavāyita [pa + √ve + a + ita]↔adj. tightly woven; with the warp well stretched
              • suvilekhita [vi + √likh + *e + ita]↔adj. well scraped; well brushed
              • suvitacchita [su + vi + √tacch + ita]↔adj. well brushed; well plucked; (comm) well cleaned
              • appeva [api + eva]↔sandhi. (+opt) it is likely that; perhaps; maybe; hopefully; if only; please may; it would be good
              • anupadajjeyya [anu + pa + √dā + a + eyya]↔opt. (+acc) should continue; should undertake; should follow through; lit. should give more; 2 opt. (+acc) could give; should hand over

              • āyataṁ (longer)
              • vitthataṁ (wider)
              • appitaṁ (thicker)

        • np 28 - accekacīvarasikkhāpada #edited
          • background
            • The Tathāgata was residing at the Jetavana temple near the city of Sāvatthi. One senior minister was looking to travel to a far off region and sent a messenger to convey a message to the bhikkhus as follows: “Sir! Please visit me. I will offer the vassāvāsika robes.” The bhikkhus did not visit him as by then the Buddha had allowed only the monks who had finished the vassa to accept vassāvāsika robes. At this instance, the senior minister began to bad-mouth the bhikkhus. The Buddha who got to know this declared: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, accekacīvaraṃ paṭiggahetvā nikkhipituṃ.” Then the bhikkhus accepted acceka cīvaras and surpassed (?) the robe season (cīvarakālasamaya). Based on this matter, the following training rule was imposed. mem aid: Jetavana minister informs the monks he wishes to offer vassāvāsika robe at that time only those who had finished vassa could accept it so they did not go they were criticized
          • training rule in pāḷi
            • Dasāhānāgataṃ kattikatemāsikapuṇṇamaṃ, bhikkhuno paneva accekacīvaraṃ uppajjeyya, accekaṃ maññamānena bhikkhunā paṭiggahetabbaṃ, paṭiggahetvā yāva cīvarakālasamayaṃ nikkhipitabbaṃ. Tato ce uttariṃ nikkhipeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. A bhikkhu receives an accekacīvara ten days before the pavāraṇa. The bhikkhu who is aware of this must accept it. It can be accepted and kept till the cīvara kāla samaya (suitable season for making robes) (without determining it). If it is kept beyond this period, the bhikkhu will be committing a nissaggiya pācittiya offence.
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • acceka [ati + √i + *a + *ika]↔adj. urgent; pressing; extraordinary
          • description
            • what is the purpose of this rule?→this training rule has been laid down to explain the time period in which an accekacīvara can be kept without being determined and to allow lay devotees to offer vassāvāsika robes in cases they cannot wait for the end of the vassa
          • pāḷi terms
            • accekacīvara↔a robe offered before the pavāraṇā saying, "I'm offering vassāvāsika robe"
            • vassāvāsika cīvara↔a robe offered to the monks who have observed vassa; it is usually offered after the pavāraṇā; when offered before they are called accekacīvara
          • instances of offenses
            • an accekacīvara can be kept as atirekacīvara for up to {{9507103577118234::10 days}} if received 10 days or less before the pavāraṇā it can be kept as atirekacīvara for up to {{9507103577118234::10 days without counting the kālasamaya}}e.g.: if received 5 days before the pavāraṇa and the kaṭhina is spread by the monk, the accekacīvara can be kept as atirekacīvara until {{9507103577118234::the dawn of the 5th day after Phaggunapuṇṇamā in which the robe becomes nissaggiya}} saṅghika accekacīvaras can be distributed among the Saṅgha before or after the pavāraṇā if distributed before, they can be received by monks who are observing the vassa and kept as atirekacīvara for up to {{9507103577118234::10 days}}; if the monk happens to break his vassa the cīvara becomes {{9507103577118234::saṅghika property (if it was offered originally as saṅghika property)}} if distributed after the pavāraṇā, only the monks who completed the vassa should receive it; it can then be kept as atirekacīvara until {{9507103577118234::the end of the cīvarakālasamaya and an extra 10 days}} when the time limit is exceeded the accekacīvara becomes {{9507103577118234::nissaggiya}} and the monk incurs a {{9507103577118234::pācittiya}} offense
              • what about those observing the pacchimikā vassa? #q🙋🏼‍♂
              • if it was offered as personal property what happens? #q🙋🏼‍♂

        • np 30 - pariṇatasikkhāpada #edited
          • background
            • Buddha in: Jetavana, Sāvatthi monks involved: chabbaggiya incident: devotees from Sāvatthi annually offered alms together with robes to the Saṅgha and on one occasion the chabbaggiyas asked for those robes for themselves and being pressurized by them, gave in and handed the robes; the Buddha laid down the rule
          • training rule in pāḷi
            • Yo pana bhikkhu jānaṃ saṅghikaṃ lābhaṃ pariṇataṃ attano pariṇāmeyya, nissaggiyaṃ pācittiyaṃ. If a bhikkhu knowingly allocates a requisite upon himself, which has been set aside to be offered to the Saṅgha, and receives it, a nissaggiya pācittiya offence will be committed
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • pariṇāmeti [pari + √nam + *e + ti]↔pr. (+acc & +dat) transfers (to); allocates (to); designates (for); diverts (to); lit. inclines
          • description
            • purpose of the rule→to prevent monks from committing the immoral act of redirecting requisites allocated to the Saṅgha to oneself
          • pāḷi terms
            • pariṇata↔a requisite that has been designated / assigned / allocated by expressing it verbally "I will give this to X"
          • instances of offenses
            • asking for the pariṇata requisites allocated to the Saṅgha for oneself: {{08295525542501925::dkṭ}} receiving it: {{08295525542501925::np}} asking for the pariṇata requisites to be diverged (in any case): {{08295525542501925::dkṭ}} -donation allocated to the saṅgha diverged to yourself: {{08295525542501925::np 30}} another person: {{08295525542501925::pc 82}} another saṅgha / cetiya: {{08295525542501925::dkṭ}} -donation allocated to a cetiya diverged to yourself / another person / another saṅgha / another cetiya: {{08295525542501925::dkṭ}} -donation allocated to another person even a dog diverged to saṅgha / cetiya / another person / yourself: {{08295525542501925::dkṭ}} -donation allocated to yourself diverged to anyone else: {{08295525542501925::no offense}} if asked to be given to oneself not knowing it was allocated to any other recipient: {{08295525542501925::no offense}}
          • nature

        • 4 paribhogas:
          • Aparepi cattāro paribhogā – lajjiparibhogo, alajjiparibhogo, dhammiyaparibhogo, adhammiyaparibhogoti.
            • Tattha alajjino lajjinā saddhiṃ paribhogo vaṭṭati, āpattiyā na kāretabbo. Lajjino alajjinā saddhiṃ yāva na jānāti, tāva vaṭṭati. Ādito paṭṭhāya hi alajjī nāma natthi, tasmā yadāssa alajjībhāvaṃ jānāti tadā vattabbo “Tumhe kāyadvāre ca vacīdvāre ca vītikkamaṃ karotha, taṃ appatirūpaṃ mā evamakatthā”ti. Sace anādiyitvā karotiyeva, yadi tena saddhiṃ paribhogaṃ karoti, sopi alajjīyeva hoti. Yopi attano bhārabhūtena alajjinā saddhiṃ paribhogaṃ karoti, sopi nivāretabbo. Sace ¶ na oramati, ayampi alajjīyeva hoti. Evaṃ eko alajjī alajjīsatampi karoti. Alajjino ¶ pana alajjināva saddhiṃ paribhoge āpatti nāma natthi. Lajjino lajjinā saddhiṃ paribhogo dvinnaṃ khattiyakumārānaṃ suvaṇṇapātiyaṃ bhojanasadisoti.
            • Dhammiyādhammiyaparibhogo paccayavasena veditabbo. Tattha sace puggalopi alajjī piṇḍapātopi adhammiyo, ubho jegucchā. Puggalo alajjī piṇḍapāto dhammiyo, puggalaṃ jigucchitvā piṇḍapāto na gahetabbo. Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana dussīlo saṅghato uddesabhattādīni labhitvā saṅghasseva deti, etāni yathādānameva gatattā vaṭṭantīti vuttaṃ. Puggalo lajjī piṇḍapāto adhammiyo, piṇḍapāto jeguccho na gahetabbo. Puggalo lajjī, piṇḍapātopi dhammiyo, vaṭṭati.
            • Apare dve paggahā; dve ca paribhogā – lajjipaggaho, alajjipaggaho; dhammaparibhogo āmisaparibhogoti. (Commentary to Vinaya)

      • 3 types of donors
        • dānadāsa: promising a certain dāna and giving less (or nothing); or giving less/of lower quality than for themselves - one is a 'slave' of the object since one cannot overcome attachment to it
        • dānasahāya: promising a certain dāna and giving as promised; or giving the same amount/of the same quality than for themselves - one is a friend of the object due to not relinquishing the liking for it
        • dānapati: promising a certain dāna and giving more; or giving more/of higher quality than for themselves - one is a master of the object since one can overcome attachment to it
        • note:
          • in svākkhātadhamma the receiver should know the amount they should accept, while in dvākkhātadhamma the donor should know the amount they should offer
          • Saddahatīti "dātā dānassa phalaṃ paccanubhotī"ti pattiyāyati. Dāne sūroti dānasūro deyyadhamme īsakampi saṅgaṃ akatvā muttacāgo. Svāyamattho kammassakataññāṇassa tikkhavisadabhāvena veditabbo, tenāha "na saddhāmattakenevā"tiādi. Yassa hi kammassakatā paccakkhato viya upaṭṭhāti, so evaṃ vutto. Yaṃ dānaṃ detīti yaṃ deyyadhammaṃ parassa deti. Tassa pati hutvāti (having become the master of that) tabbisayaṃ (ta visayaṁ - that object) lobhaṃ suṭṭhu abhibhavanto tassa adhipati hutvā (having become the master of that) deti anadhibhavanīyattā. "na dāso, na sahāyo"ti vatvā tadubhayaṃ anvayato (accordingly), byatirekato (in an opposing way) ca dassetuṃ "yo hī"tiādi vuttaṃ. Dāso hutvā deti taṇhāya dānassa dāsabyataṃ upagatattā. Sahāyo hutvā deti tassa piyabhāvānissajjanato. Sāmī hutvā deti tattha taṇhādāsabyato attānaṃ mocetvā abhibhuyya pavattanato. Sāmiparibhogasadisā hetassāyaṃ (hi etassa ayaṁ) pavattatīti.
            • vocab: #[[pāḷi vocab (2nd year)]] #[[pāḷi vocab (1st year) ]]
              • abhibhavanto↔one who is overwhelming, overcoming
              • tadubhaya [tad + ubhaya]↔adj. both of those
              • anadhibhavanīyattā na adhi bhavanīya ttā↔because of the state of not being overwhelmed (by the object)
              • byatireka masc.↔(logic) negative, negation; 2 masc. (gram) negative, negation
              • dāsabyataṃ↔the state of a slave
              • upagatattā↔because of the state of having reached
              • ta sa piyabhāvānissajjanato↔for not relinquishing the state of liking that
              • taṇhādāsabyato↔from the state of a slave of craving

    • sīla
      • definition
        • avoidance of unwholesome acts
        • observance of precepts including the duties
        • practice which purifies bodily and verbal actions
      • 2 types of sīla according to kattabba / akattabba and what helps fulfil them (merge with repeated info) #q🙋🏼‍♂
        • cārittasīla: fulfilling duties, things that should be done "kattabbaṁ"
          • practiced with the help of vīriya and saddhā
        • vārittasīla: abstaining from prohibited acts, "idaṁ na kattabbaṁ" (more significant)
          • practiced with the help of saddhā
        • notes:
          • Duvidhakoṭṭhāse yaṃ bhagavatā "idaṃ kattabba"nti paññattasikkhāpadapūraṇaṃ, taṃ cārittaṃ. Yaṃ "idaṃ na kattabba"nti paṭikkhittassa akaraṇaṃ, taṃ vārittaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ vacanattho. Caranti tasmiṃ sīlesu paripūrakāritāya pavattantīti cārittaṃ. Vāritaṃ tāyanti rakkhanti tenāti vārittaṃ. Tattha saddhāvīriyasādhanaṃ cārittaṃ, saddhāsādhanaṃ vārittaṃ. Evaṃ cārittavārittavasena duvidhaṃ. (Vsm. I. 11.).

              • sappasirūpamā kāmā...(similar to a snake’s head for being perilous)

    • pattidāna
      • definition: {{46259815352687705::attano santāne nibbattā patti dīyati etenāti pattidānaṃ; giving one's own acquired merit to others by saying it aloud}}
        • pajjitthāti patti. attani laddhapuññakoṭṭhāsassa nāmaṃ. pāpīyatītivā patti. parehi anumodantehi laddhabbassa puññānisandassetaṃ nāmaṃ. pattiṃ dadanti etenāti pattidānaṃ.
      • panvedīma↔puring water to signify the act of giving something that cannot be given by hand (performed by the King Bimbisara when offering the veḷuvana); it is not necessary to do it, but if the recipients believe it should be done they may not rejoice if it is not done
      • paradattūpajīvika petā: petas fully depend on merit given by relatives (and friends) for acquiring food, clothing, dwelling places, and so on; those who receive the merit enjoy its benefits immediately according to what was given; if food was offered, they will receive food, if clothing, clothing, and so on...; if one offers to a certain passed relative and it happens that the relative is not in a position to partake of the donation (aṭṭhāna), other relatives who are in such condition partake of it
      • ṭhāna and aṭṭhāna for partaking of the donation according to jāṇussoṇisutta (dasakanipāta)
        • ṭhāna is only the pettivisaya of the paradattūpajīvika petas where they depend on what is offered for food, shelter, clothing and so on
        • other destination are aṭṭhāna
      • the duty of sharing merit: sharing merit to those who have passed away is one's duty, and in case of being in destination in which no benefit is acquired, the merit-maker still fulfils the duty and accumulates merit
        • sharing merit with devas: devas occasionally assist humans and they sympathize with those who share merits with them; sharing merits is what can be done by humans to show gratitude and also assist devas
        • sharing merits with all beings
      • improper method for sharing merit
        • merit should not be shared by wishing the recipient to pass away and be reborn in a good destination; the petas do not wish to die, but to receive what they lack; if done so they may not rejoice
      • the giver of merit only increases his merit by merit-sharing, while the recipient only partakes of the merit given if he rejoices in it
      • method of transfering merit in pāḷi
        • for relatives:
          • idaṁ vo ñātīnaṁ hotu sukhitā hontu ñātayo
        • for devas:
          • ettāvatā ca amhehi sambhataṁ puññasampadaṁ sabbe devā anumodantu sabbasampatti siddhiyā
        • for all living beings:
          • ettāvatā...sabbe sattā anumodantu...
      • vocab:
        • pajji [√pad + ya + i]→aor. (+acc) experienced suffering; suffered
        • sambhataṁ puññasampadaṁ: the acquired merit accumulated
    • pattānumodanā
      • definition: {{46259815352687705::pattiṃ anumodati etāyāti pattānumodanā (rejoicing in the merit acquired or shared by another)}}
      • it hits envy: rejoicing in other's merits is opposed to envy of the donor and specially envy of the recipient (in the cases one is not the recipient); out of jealousy one may criticize the donor and the recipient and may even prevent the donation
      • one acquires the merit of rejoicing regardless of whether the merit was shared or not; the greater the merit done the greater the merit of rejoicing in it; the greater the faith and understanding, the greater the merit
      • when do those who accept merit experience the results?→paradattūpajīvika petas experience the results immediately while other beings experience them at the time of the vipāka
      • for such petas (paradattūpajīvika) the result of rejoicing in merits occurs immediately. Does that mean it is diṭṭhadhammavedanīyakamma? #q🙋🏼‍♂

        • alagaddapariyatti: learning dhamma for the sake of gain (lābhasakkāra)
          • tattha yo buddhavacanaṃ uggahetvā evaṃ cīvarādīni vā labhissāmi, catuparisamajjhe vā maṃ jānissantīti lābhasakkārahetu pariyāpuṇāti, tassa sā pariyatti alagaddapariyatti nāma. evaṃ pariyāpuṇato hi buddhavacanaṃ apariyāpuṇitvā niddokkamanaṃ varataraṃ.
        • nittharaṇapariyatti: for crossing over
          • yo pana buddhavacanaṃ uggaṇhitvā sīlassa āgataṭṭhāne sīlaṃ pūretvā samādhissa āgataṭṭhāne samādhigabbhaṃ gaṇhāpetvā vipassanāya āgataṭṭhāne vipassanaṃ paṭṭhapetvā maggaphalānaṃ āgataṭṭhāne maggaṃ bhāvessāmi14 sacchikarissāmīti uggaṇhāti, tassa sā pariyatti nittharaṇapariyatti nāma hoti.phalaṃ
        • bhaṇḍāgārikapariyatti:
          • khīṇāsavassa pana pariyatti bhaṇḍāgārikapariyatti nāma. tassa hi apariññātaṃ appahīnaṃ abhāvitaṃ asacchikataṃ vā natthi. so hi pariññātakkhandho pahīnakileso bhāvitamaggo sacchikataphalo, tasmā buddhavacanaṃ pariyāpuṇanto tantidhārako paveṇipālako vaṃsānurakkhakova hutvā uggaṇhāti. itissa sā pariyatti bhaṇḍāgārikapariyatti nāma hoti.

        • itivuttakaṃ (quotations)
          • vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā"tiādinayappavattā dasuttarasatasuttantā itivuttakanti veditabbaṃ
          • note:
            • memorized by Kujuttara bhikkhunī
        • jātakaṃ (birth stories)
          • apaṇṇakajātakādīni paññāsādhikāni pañca jātakasatāni jātakanti veditabbaṃ.
          • note:
            • commentary says 550 stories but we have 547
        • abbhutadhammaṃ (marvellous accounts)
          • "cattārome, bhikkhave, acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande"ti (dī. ni. 2.209) -ādinayappavattā sabbepi acchariyaabbhutadhammapaṭisaṃyuttā suttantā abbhutadhammanti veditabbaṃ.
        • vedallaṃ (analyses / question and answers)
          • cūḷavedalla-mahāvedalla-sammādiṭṭhi-sakkapañha-saṅkhārabhājaniya-mahāpuṇṇamasuttādayo sabbepi vedañca tuṭṭhiñca laddhā laddhā pucchitasuttantā vedallanti veditabbaṃ.

          • these categories overlap

          • abbhuta (adj.)↔marvellous; extraordinary; unbelievable; astonishing
          • vedallaṁ (nt.) [vi + √dal + *ya]↔questions-and-answers; catechism; one of the nine kinds of suttas; lit. to be split apart
      • 4 modes of desanā (teachings) / suttanikkhepas
        • attajjhāsaya suttanikkhepa (discourse preached according to the one’s inclination)
        • parajjhāsaya suttanikkhepa (discourse preached according to another’s inclination)
        • pucchāvasika suttanikkhepa (discourse preached as the result of a question)
        • atthuppattika suttanikkhepa (discourse preached on account of an arisen need)
        • notes:
          • cattāro hi suttanikkhepā attajjhāsayo parajjhāsayo pucchāvasiko aṭṭhuppattiko (brahmajālasutta-a)
            • "tattha yāni suttāni bhagavā parehi anajjhiṭṭho kevalaṃ attano ajjhāsayeneva kathesi, seyyathidaṃ, ākaṅkheyyasuttaṃ, vatthasuttaṃ, mahāsatipaṭṭhānaṃ, mahāsaḷāyatanavibhaṅgasuttaṃ, ariyavaṃsasuttaṃ, sammappadhānasuttantahārako, iddhipādaindriyabalabojjhaṅgamaggaṅgasuttantahārakoti evamādīni, tesaṃ attajjhāsayo nikkhepo.
            • yāni pana "paripakkā kho rāhulassa vimuttiparipācaniyā dhammā, yaṃnūnāhaṃ rāhulaṃ uttariṃ āsavānaṃ khaye vineyya"nti, (saṃ. ni. 4.121) evaṃ paresaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ khantiṃ manaṃ abhinīhāraṃ bujjhanabhāvañca avekkhitvā parajjhāsayavasena kathitāni, seyyathidaṃ, cūḷarāhulovādasuttaṃ, mahārāhulovādasuttaṃ, dhammacakkappavattanaṃ, dhātuvibhaṅgasuttanti evamādīni, tesaṃ parajjhāsayo nikkhepo.
            • bhagavantaṃ pana upasaṅkamitvā catasso parisā, cattāro vaṇṇā, nāgā, supaṇṇā, gandhabbā, asurā, yakkhā, mahārājāno, tāvatiṃsādayo devā, mahābrahmāti evamādayo – "bojjhaṅgā bojjhaṅgā"ti, bhante, vuccanti. "nīvaraṇā nīvaraṇā"ti, bhante, vuccanti, "ime nu kho, bhante, pañcupādānakkhandhā". "kiṃ sūdha vittaṃ purisassa seṭṭha"ntiādinā nayena pañhaṃ pucchanti. evaṃ puṭṭhena bhagavatā yāni kathitāni bojjhaṅgasaṃyuttādīni, yāni vā panaññānipi devatāsaṃyutta-mārasaṃyutta-brahmasaṃyutta-sakkapañha-cūḷavedalla-mahāvedalla-sāmaññaphala-āḷavaka-sūciloma-kharalomasuttādīni, tesaṃ pucchāvasiko nikkhepo.
            • yāni pana tāni uppannaṃ kāraṇaṃ paṭicca kathitāni, seyyathidaṃ – dhammadāyādaṃ, cūḷasīhanādaṃ, candūpamaṃ, puttamaṃsūpamaṃ, dārukkhandhūpamaṃ, aggikkhandhūpamaṃ, pheṇapiṇḍūpamaṃ, pāricchattakūpamanti evamādīni, tesaṃ aṭṭhuppattiko nikkhepo.
        • vocab:
          • ajjhāsaya (m.)→intention; disposition
          • uppattika (adj.) [ud + √pad + ti + ka]↔arising; appearing; occurring
      • cattāri pañhabyākaraṇāni
        • ekaṃsabyākaraṇīyo pañho (question which should be given a straight answer)
        • paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo pañho (question which should be answered with a counter-question)
        • vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho (question which should be answered with a detailed analysis)

          • paṭipucchābyākaraṇīya (adj.) [paṭipucchā + byākaraṇīya]↔which should be answered with a counter-question
          • vibhajjabyākaraṇīya [vibhajja + byākaraṇīya] (adj.)↔which should be answered with a detailed analysis
          • ṭhapanīya [√ṭhā + *āpe + anīya]↔ptp. should be set aside; should be placed aside; should be left alone; lit. to cause to be stood

    • diṭṭhijukamma
      • definition: {{4329345578821091::the development of the kusala knowledge on various aspects of kamma and vipāka such as kusala and akusala, their good and bad results; '}}{{4329345578821091::diṭṭhiyā ujukaraṇaṃ diṭṭhijukammaṃ}}{{4329345578821091::' }}
      • "diṭṭhijukammaṃ sabbesaṃ niyamalakkhaṇaṃ, yaṃkiñci puññaṃ karontassa hi diṭṭhiyā ujukabhāveneva mahapphalaṃ hoti”
      • definiton (atthi dinnaṁ...)
        • "atthi dinnaṃ, atthi yiṭṭhaṃ, atthi hutaṃ, atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, atthi ayaṃ loko, atthi paro loko, atthi mātā, atthi pitā, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā, sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedenti"
        • 10 kinds of right understanding related to kamma:
          • atthi dinnam→right understanding that alms-giving, if performed with benevolence, in a previous existence, yields beneficial results in subsequent existences; related to belongings or food (annādi vatthu)
          • atthi yiṭṭhaṃ→right understanding that liberality, if extended with belief in past kamma and with faith in and respect for the virtuous qualities of recipients, yields beneficial results in future existences; related to great offerings (mahāyāgo, sabbasādhāraṇa mahādāna)
          • atthi hutam→right understanding that gifts, even on a small scale, (ahuna, pahuna) if made in previous existences with good will, beneficial results will result in future existences; related to sending gifts out of respect (peheṇaka sakkāro, pāhuṇabhāvena kattabba sakkāro)
          • atthi sukatadukkaṭānaṁ kammānaṁ phalam vipāko→right understanding that cruel deeds done to beings in previous existences yield bad results in subsequent existences, and that refraining from such evil acts yields beneficial results
          • atthi ayam loko, atthi paroloko: right understanding that this world (ayam loko) is the human world, and the other world consists of the four lower worlds (hell, the worlds of animals, petas and asurakas), the deva worlds and the brahma worlds.
          • atthi mātā atthi pitā→right understanding that good and evil deeds done to one's mother or father yield good and evil results respectively in subsequent existences
          • atthi sattā opapātikā→right understanding that there really exist beings born by apparitional rebirth who are invisible to human eyes
          • atthi loke samanabrahmanā samaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokam parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedenti→there are higher spiritual knowledges (abhinna) and omniscience (sabbaññutāñāṇa). monks and brahmins who exert themselves diligently in fulfilling the perfections (pāramitā) and practising samatha and vipassana bhāvanā in this human world can achieve such ñāṇa; personages who have achieved such nana appear in this world time to time.
      • diṭṭhijukamma's pubbacetanā can be any of the {{6523830138756719::8 mahākusala}} cittas muñcanacetanā can be {{6523830138756719::only one of the 4 ñāṇasampayutta mahākusala}} cittas aparacetanā can be any of the {{6523830138756719::8 mahākusala}} cittas
      • kammassaka.. (pāḷi)
        • "kammassakā sabbe sattā, kammadāyādā, kammayoni, kammabandhu, kammapaṭisaraṇā, yaṁ kammaṁ karissanti, kalyāṇaṁ vā pāpakaṁ vā, tassa dāyādā bhavissanti"
        • vocab:
          • kammassakā (kamma + saka)→(beings are) the owner of their actions
          • kammadāyāda↔(beings are) the inheritors of their actions
          • kammayoni↔(beings have) kamma as their origin, source, cause
          • kammabandhu↔(beings have) kamma as their relative, they are bound to their actions
          • kammapaṭisaraṇā↔(beings have) actions as refuge, support
      • why is it given as the first factor of the ariyamagga?→because due to right view living beings' minds tend towards wholesome states; it is the root and assistance for all wholesome actions
      • according to the question raised in cūḷakammavibhaṅga sutta by the young man Subha Todeyyaputta, kamma is the cause and reason for beings to become inferior or superior in the followings aspects
        • 1. Longevity of the lifespan (āyu)
        • 2. Health (ābādha)
        • 3. Physical appearance (vaṇṇa)
        • 4. Retinue, influence (appesakkha, mahesakkha)
        • 5. Wealth (bhoga)
        • 6. Rank or clan (kulīna)
        • 7. Intelligence (paññā)
        • note: This develops the understanding of how much kamma means to our life and what results can be produced by kamma
